===Cincinnati Bengals===
====2011 season====
{{See also|2011 Cincinnati Bengals season}}
On April 29, 2011, the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] selected Dalton in the second round, as the 35th overall pick, in the [[2011 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 29, 2011 |title=Bengals pick TCU's Dalton early in 2nd round |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/draft2011/news/story?id=6451436 |access-date=July 3, 2022 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |archive-date=July 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220703015109/https://www.espn.com/nfl/draft2011/news/story?id=6451436 |url-status=live }}</ref> Out of the twelve quarterbacks that were chosen in the 2011 NFL Draft, he was the fifth selected.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=August 14, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170814023237/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Andy dalton 2012 pro bowl.jpg|thumb|right|Dalton at the [[2012 Pro Bowl]]]]
After Dalton was selected by the Bengals, there was much speculation over whether Dalton or veteran [[Bruce Gradkowski]] would start at quarterback. [[Carson Palmer]], the first overall draft pick in the [[2003 NFL draft]], demanded to be [[Trade (sports)|traded]] or released and was traded later in the season to the [[Oakland Raiders]]. On June 29, 2011, the Bengals signed Dalton to a four-year, $5.21 million rookie contract with a $2.29 million signing bonus and $4.02 million guaranteed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sportrac.com:Andy Dalton contracts |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/cincinnati-bengals/andy-dalton-7750/ |access-date=October 22, 2016 |website=Sportrac.com |archive-date=October 23, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161023135634/http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/cincinnati-bengals/andy-dalton-7750/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On August 8, before their first pre-season game against the [[Detroit Lions]], Bengals head coach [[Marvin Lewis]] released his first [[depth chart]] per NFL rules but noted that it meant little. The depth chart had Dalton listed as the first-string quarterback, followed by Gradkowski.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 7, 2012 |title=First depth chart released |url=http://cincinnati.com/blogs/bengals/2011/08/08/first-depth-chart-released-2/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120707033004/http://cincinnati.com/blogs/bengals/2011/08/08/first-depth-chart-released-2/ |archive-date=July 7, 2012 |access-date=September 15, 2021 |website=Cincinnati.com }}</ref>

Dalton's first NFL regular-season start came on September 11, on the road against the [[Cleveland Browns]]. Dalton, in one half of play before leaving the game due to injury, completed 10 of his 15 pass attempts for 81 yards and a touchdown, posting a [[passer rating]] of 102.4. The Bengals won the game, 27–17, Dalton's first divisional [[AFC North]] victory as well as first win against the divisional rival Browns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Cleveland Browns – September 11th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201109110cle.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150336/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201109110cle.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Dalton's second game on was also on the road, against the [[Denver Broncos]]. Despite a 24–22 loss, he led a comeback, completing 19 of 29 pass attempts for 280 yards and two touchdowns in the second half alone, and achieving a passer rating of 107.0 for the game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 18, 2011 |title=Kyle Orton's 2 TD passes help John Fox get first win in Denver |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap/_/gameId/310918007 |access-date=July 3, 2022 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=July 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220703214938/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap/_/gameId/310918007 |url-status=dead }}</ref> During a Week 6 27–17 victory over the [[Indianapolis Colts]], Dalton completed 25 of 32 passes for 264 yards and a touchdown. In that game, he had a season-high 78.1 completion percentage and 111.5 passer rating.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Cincinnati Bengals – October 16th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201110160cin.htm |access-date=October 1, 2019 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 22, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190322045746/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201110160cin.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On November 3, Dalton was named the NFL Offensive Rookie of the Month for October. He led the Bengals to a 4–0 record with 909 passing yards and six touchdowns in the month.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Michael David |date=November 3, 2011 |title=Andy Dalton tops Cam Newton as Offensive Rookie of the Month |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2011/11/03/andy-dalton-tops-cam-newton-as-offensive-rookie-of-the-month/ |access-date=October 1, 2019 |work=ProFootballTalk |archive-date=October 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191001174533/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2011/11/03/andy-dalton-tops-cam-newton-as-offensive-rookie-of-the-month/ |url-status=live }}</ref> During Week 9, Dalton then threw for 217 yards and a season-high three touchdowns with no interceptions against the [[Tennessee Titans]] in a comeback 24–17 victory, earning him [[NFL Rookie of the Week]] honors.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Tennessee Titans – November 6th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201111060oti.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150253/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201111060oti.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Three weeks later, Dalton passed for 270 yards and a touchdown for a 105.6 passer rating in a comeback 23–20 victory over the Browns, again winning Rookie of the Week. This game featured a 51-yard strike from Dalton to [[A. J. Green]] with only 1:08 remaining in the fourth quarter, setting up the Bengals' game-winning field goal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Cincinnati Bengals – November 27th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201111270cin.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150322/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201111270cin.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> By the end of the season, Dalton had led the Bengals to a 9–7 record and a berth in the [[2011–12 NFL playoffs|NFL playoffs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 Cincinnati Bengals Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/cin/2011.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150313/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/cin/2011.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On January 7, 2012, the Bengals faced the [[T. J. Yates]]-led [[Houston Texans]] in the [[2011–12 NFL playoffs#AFC: Houston Texans 31, Cincinnati Bengals 10|Wild Card Round]] of the NFL playoffs. This game marked the first time in NFL playoff history that two rookie quarterbacks started in the same game against each other.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barnwell |first=Bill |date=January 5, 2012 |title=Playoff Preview: Bengals at Texans |url=http://www.grantland.com/story/_/id/7427164/bengals-texans |access-date=October 1, 2019 |website=Grantland.com |archive-date=October 9, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131009174047/http://www.grantland.com/story/_/id/7427164/bengals-texans |url-status=live }}</ref> Dalton completed over 64 percent of his passes but also had three turnovers as the Texans won the game, 31–10.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 7, 2012 |title=Texans harass Andy Dalton, Bengals en route to first playoff win |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap/_/gameId/320107034 |access-date=July 3, 2022 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=July 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220703214936/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap/_/gameId/320107034 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

During his rookie season, Dalton had four wins featuring fourth-quarter comebacks (against the [[Buffalo Bills]], [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], Tennessee Titans and Cleveland Browns). He became the first quarterback in NFL history not drafted in the first round to start all 16 games of his rookie season. Dalton became just one of five rookie quarterbacks with over 3,000 passing yards and at least 20 touchdown passes, joining fellow rookie [[Cam Newton]] and also [[Peyton Manning]], [[Dan Marino]], and [[Charlie Conerly]].<ref name="bengals.com" />

At the end of the season, Dalton received the Emerging Player Award from the [[NFL Players Association]] during the NFLPA PULSE Awards. The other nominees for the award were [[Carolina Panthers]] quarterback Cam Newton, [[New Orleans Saints]] tight end [[Jimmy Graham]], [[New England Patriots]] tight end [[Rob Gronkowski]], and Lions defensive tackle [[Ndamukong Suh]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garrison |first=Jason |date=January 22, 2012 |title=Bengals Rookie Andy Dalton Wins NFLPA Emerging Player Award |url=http://www.cincyjungle.com/2012/1/22/2725193/bengals-rookie-andy-dalton-wins-nflpa-emerging-player-award |access-date=October 1, 2019 |archive-date=April 12, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412154443/https://www.cincyjungle.com/2012/1/22/2725193/bengals-rookie-andy-dalton-wins-nflpa-emerging-player-award |url-status=live }}</ref>

Dalton was named initially as a [[2012 Pro Bowl|Pro Bowl]] Alternate in his first year, and was added to the [[American Football Conference]] (AFC) Pro Bowl roster after the Patriots won the AFC Championship, forcing [[Tom Brady]] to withdraw.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crow |first=Alfie |date=December 27, 2011 |title=Pro Bowl Voting Results 2012: Andy Dalton, Tim Tebow Named AFC Alternates |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2011/12/27/2664912/pro-bowl-voting-results-2012-tim-tebow-andy-dalton |access-date=October 1, 2019 |website=SBNation.com |archive-date=October 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191001174332/https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2011/12/27/2664912/pro-bowl-voting-results-2012-tim-tebow-andy-dalton |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/probowl.htm |access-date=March 21, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=August 30, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180830174119/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/probowl.htm |url-status=live}}</ref> Dalton and Newton became the first pair of rookie quarterbacks to make the Pro Bowl in the same season.<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 26, 2012 |title=Pro Bowl to feature 2 rookie QBs for the first time with Cam Newton, Andy Dalton |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/redskins/pro-bowl-to-feature-2-rookie-qbs-for-the-first-time-with-cam-newton-andy-dalton/2012/01/26/gIQAzfhMSQ_story.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120126220648/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/redskins/pro-bowl-to-feature-2-rookie-qbs-for-the-first-time-with-cam-newton-andy-dalton/2012/01/26/gIQAzfhMSQ_story.html |archive-date=January 26, 2012 |newspaper=Washington Post |agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>

====2012 season====
{{See also|2012 Cincinnati Bengals season}}
During Week 2, Dalton guided the Bengals to a 34–27 victory over the [[Cleveland Browns]]. He completed 24 of 31 passes for 318 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception, for a 128.2 [[passer rating]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 16, 2012 |title=Andy Dalton throws 3 TDs, helps Bengals past Browns |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=320916004 |access-date=January 11, 2021 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=January 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112121716/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=320916004 |url-status=live }}</ref> In the next game against the [[Washington Commanders|Washington Redskins]], Dalton completed 19-of-27 passes for 328 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception, for a season-high 132.9 passer rating, in leading the Bengals to a 38–31 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 23, 2012 |title=Andy Dalton throws 3 TDs as Bengals outlast Redskins |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=320923028 |access-date=January 11, 2021 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=January 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112154813/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=320923028 |url-status=live }}</ref> Furthermore, he lined up as a wide receiver on the first play from scrimmage of the game, acting as a decoy while [[wildcat formation|wildcat]] quarterback [[Mohamed Sanu]] threw a 73-yard touchdown pass to [[A. J. Green]], then again flanked as a receiver while [[BenJarvus Green-Ellis]] rushed for a touchdown via a direct snap. The following week against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], Dalton threw for 244 yards and had three touchdowns (two passing, one rushing) in leading the Bengals to a 27–10 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 30, 2012 |title=Andy Dalton, A. J. Green pace surging Bengals to 3rd straight win |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=320930030 |access-date=January 11, 2021 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=July 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220703214938/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=320930030 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On October 14, 2012, Dalton threw for a career-high 381 yards to go with three touchdowns against the Browns, but also threw three interceptions as the Bengals lost 34–24.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 14, 2012 |title=Browns beat Bengals to snap 11-game skid, record 1st win of season |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=321014005 |access-date=January 11, 2021 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=January 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113082153/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=321014005 |url-status=live}}</ref> This was the second game in what would become a four-game losing streak. Dalton and the Bengals rebounded by defeating the [[New York Giants]] by a score of 31–13. He completed 21 of 30 passes for 199 yards and a season-high four touchdowns, attaining a 127.6 passer rating and a season-high 94.5 [[total quarterback rating|QBR]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 11, 2012 |title=Andy Dalton throws career-high 4 TDs as Bengals blow out Giants |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore?gameId=321111004 |access-date=January 10, 2021 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304233029/http://espn.go.com/nfl/boxscore?gameId=321111004 |url-status=live }}</ref> For his performance against the Giants, Dalton was named the AFC Offensive Player of the Week for the first time in his career.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 14, 2012 |title=Dalton named AFC Offensive Player of Week |url=http://www.foxsports.com/other/story/dalton-named-afc-offensive-player-of-week-111412 |access-date=January 11, 2021 |work=FOX Sports |archive-date=April 12, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412154751/https://www.foxsports.com/other/story/dalton-named-afc-offensive-player-of-week-111412 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Week 10 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/week_10.htm |access-date=March 21, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=October 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181013014321/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/week_10.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In the next game against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], Dalton completed 18 of 29 passes for 230 yards and two touchdowns thrown (a 109.8 passer rating) while adding a rushing touchdown in the 28–6 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 18, 2012 |title=Andy Dalton, A. J. Green lead Bengals past woeful Chiefs |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=321118012 |access-date=January 11, 2021 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=May 8, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210508093703/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=321118012 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On November 25, in a much-hyped game with the [[Oakland Raiders]] due to the return of former Bengals quarterback [[Carson Palmer]] to Cincinnati, Dalton outperformed Palmer by throwing for 210 yards and three touchdowns, achieving a 109.0 passer rating, and leading the Bengals to a 34–10 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 25, 2012 |title=Andy Dalton throws 3 TDs as Bengals demolish Carson Palmer, Raiders |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=321125004 |access-date=January 11, 2021 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=January 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112132945/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=321125004 |url-status=live}}</ref> In the fourth quarter, an unnecessary roughness penalty by [[Lamarr Houston]] on Dalton was one part of a sequence of events leading to the ejections of [[Andrew Whitworth]], [[Tommy Kelly (American football)|Tommy Kelly]], and Houston from the game. With his performance, Dalton became one of three players in NFL history with at least 20 touchdown passes in each of his first two seasons, joining [[Peyton Manning]] and [[Dan Marino]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shareef |first=Jameel |date=November 27, 2012 |title=Cincinnati Bengals: Andy Dalton Joins Peyton Manning & Dan Marino |url=http://www.footballnation.com/content/cincinnati-bengals-andy-dalton-joins-peyton-manning-dan-marino/19681/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160317004630/http://www.footballnation.com/content/cincinnati-bengals-andy-dalton-joins-peyton-manning-dan-marino/19681/ |archive-date=March 17, 2016 |access-date=January 10, 2021 |work=Football Nation}}</ref>

In two of the next three following weeks, Dalton's mobility proved to be valuable as he scrambled for the go-ahead touchdown runs in victories over the [[San Diego Chargers]] and [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. On December 23, against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], his 21-yard pass to Green with fourteen seconds remaining set up the game-winning field goal, propelling the Bengals to a 13–10 road victory and a second consecutive berth in the [[2012–13 NFL playoffs|NFL playoffs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Pittsburgh Steelers – December 23rd, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201212230pit.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=June 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220629153702/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201212230pit.htm |url-status=live}}</ref> This game marked the first time Dalton was able to defeat the divisional rival Steelers, and the first time the Bengals made the playoffs in consecutive seasons since 1981–1982.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 23, 2012 |title=Bengals secure 2nd straight postseason berth on Josh Brown's late FG |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=321223023 |access-date=January 11, 2021 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=January 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112155318/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=321223023 |url-status=live }}</ref> The following week, Dalton threw for a touchdown and a 101.5 quarterback rating in one half of play in a 23–17 victory over the [[Baltimore Ravens]]. This marked his first victory over the divisional rival Ravens and capped a 10–6 regular-season record.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 30, 2012 |title=Starters sit as playoff-bound Bengals beat division rival Ravens |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=321230004 |access-date=January 11, 2021 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=January 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112081457/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=321230004 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On January 5, 2013, Dalton and the Bengals faced the [[Houston Texans]] in the [[2012–13 NFL playoffs#AFC: Houston Texans 19, Cincinnati Bengals 13|Wild Card Round]] of the NFL playoffs. In a defensive struggle with neither Dalton nor Texans quarterback [[Matt Schaub]] able to pass for a touchdown, the Bengals lost 19–13, the second consecutive year the Bengals fell to the Texans in the opening round of the playoffs. With 2:57 remaining in the fourth quarter, Dalton overthrew a pass to an open Green, for what would have been the go-ahead touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2013 |title=Arian Foster, defense carry Texans past Bengals in wild-card game |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=330105034 |access-date=January 11, 2021 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=April 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220413030909/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=330105034 |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2013 season====
{{See also|2013 Cincinnati Bengals season}}
In the season opener against the [[Chicago Bears]], Dalton completed 26 of 33 passes for a career-high 78.8 completion percentage, 282 yards, two touchdowns, two interceptions, and a 91.8 [[total quarterback rating|QBR]] as the Bengals lost on the road by a score of 24–21.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rapien |first=James |date=September 11, 2013 |title=Gruden believes Dalton played "well" in week one. |url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2013/9/11/4717994/jay-gruden-backs-andy-dalton-after-bengals-season-opening-loss-to |access-date=September 15, 2021 |work=Cincy Jungle |archive-date=September 15, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210915214303/https://www.cincyjungle.com/2013/9/11/4717994/jay-gruden-backs-andy-dalton-after-bengals-season-opening-loss-to |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 8, 2013 |title=Bears rally by Bengals in Marc Trestman's debut|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap/_/gameId/330908003 |agency=[[Associated Press]] J. Dalton finished the regular season with 4,293 passing yards for 34 passing touchdowns, 20 interceptions, and an 88.8 passer rating. His passing yards and touchdowns were both career highs and Bengals single-season franchise records. In the Bengals' [[2013–14 NFL playoffs#AFC: San Diego Chargers 27, Cincinnati Bengals 10|Wild Card]] game against the Chargers, Dalton threw his first NFL postseason touchdown pass. However, he also threw two interceptions and lost a fumble, on three consecutive possessions in the second half, as the Bengals lost by a score of 27–10. After the game, Dalton was heavily criticized for his poor play and consistent failure to advance in the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Doyel |first=Gregg |date=January 5, 2014 |title=Bengals QB Andy Dalton dodges his role in loss better than he does INTs |url=http://www.cbssports.com/general/writer/gregg-doyel/24399646/bengals-qb-andy-dalton-dodges-his-role-in-loss-better-than-he-does-ints |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140106023832/https://www.cbssports.com/general/writer/gregg-doyel/24399646/bengals-qb-andy-dalton-dodges-his-role-in-loss-better-than-he-does-ints |archive-date=January 6, 2014 |work=CBS Sports}}</ref> In his eight 2013 primetime ([[ESPN Sunday Night Football|SNF]], [[Monday Night Football|MNF]], [[Thursday Night Football|TNF]], [[NFL playoffs|playoffs]]), and/or AFC North intradivisional games, Dalton completed 192 of 349 passes (55.0 completion percentage) for 2,036 passing yards, 5.83 yards per attempt, 11 passing touchdowns, 16 interceptions, and a 63.6 passer rating. In his other nine games of 2013, Dalton completed 200 of 288 passes (69.4 completion percentage) for 2,594 passing yards, 9.01 yards per attempt, 23 passing touchdowns, seven interceptions, and a 114 passer rating. Such performances raised doubt about whether Dalton was a "big-game" quarterback.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Harvey |first=Coley |date=November 12, 2013 |title=Is Andy Dalton just not a big-game QB? |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/cincinnati-bengals/post/_/id/2902/bengals-andy-dalton-big-game-quarterback |access-date=July 3, 2022 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |archive-date=March 30, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140330005240/http://espn.go.com/blog/cincinnati-bengals/post/_/id/2902/bengals-andy-dalton-big-game-quarterback |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2015 season====
{{See also|2015 Cincinnati Bengals season}}
[[File:Andy Dalton 2015.jpg|thumb|200px|Dalton in [[M&T Bank Stadium|Baltimore]] in 2015]]
The Bengals began the 2015 season on a historic winning streak. In the season-opening 33–13 road victory over the [[Oakland Raiders]], Dalton threw his 100th career touchdown pass, which was to tight end [[Tyler Eifert]], in the second quarter. Dalton finished the game with 269 passing yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Oakland Raiders – September 13th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201509130rai.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 3, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180103133338/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201509130rai.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In the next game, Dalton threw for 214 yards and three touchdowns in a 24–19 defeat of the [[San Diego Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Diego Chargers at Cincinnati Bengals – September 20th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201509200cin.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150350/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201509200cin.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> It marked the fourth straight home-opening win for the Bengals and the 15th three-touchdown performance for Dalton. He threw for a career-high 383 yards and three touchdowns in Week 3 against the Ravens, 321 yards in Week 4 against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], and 331 yards in a Week 5 game where Dalton also threw two touchdowns and ran for one as he led the Bengals back from a fourth-quarter 24–7 deficit to a 27–24 overtime win over the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at Cincinnati Bengals – October 11th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201510110cin.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=August 4, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170804014315/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201510110cin.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> This was the second-biggest comeback in franchise history. During a Week 6 34–21 road victory over the [[Buffalo Bills]], Dalton completed 22 of 33 passes for 243 yards with three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati at Buffalo – 2015-10-18 – National Football League |work=Yahoo! Sports |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/cincinnati-bengals-buffalo-bills-20151018002/ |access-date=October 19, 2015 |archive-date=October 20, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151020033506/http://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/cincinnati-bengals-buffalo-bills-20151018002/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Dalton was named the AFC Offensive Player of the Month for October. Following a bye week, Dalton led the Bengals to another fourth-quarter comeback against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] on the road. The 16–10 win gave the Bengals their first 7–0 start in franchise history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Pittsburgh Steelers – November 1st, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511010pit.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150316/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511010pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> They extended this to 8–0 with Dalton's 139.8 passer rating in a victory over the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Cincinnati Bengals – November 5th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511050cin.htm |access-date=July 3, 2022 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 15, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220115070628/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511050cin.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Dalton failed to reach 200 yards passing for the first time in a Week 9 10–6 loss to the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Cincinnati Bengals – November 16th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511160cin.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150258/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511160cin.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In the next game against [[Arizona Cardinals]], he threw for 315 yards and led two scoring drives in less than four minutes in the late fourth quarter to tie the game, the Bengals lost on the road by a score of 34–31.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Arizona Cardinals – November 22nd, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511220crd.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150220/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511220crd.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Dalton bounced back with three touchdowns and a 121.4 rating in a Week 11 31–7 victory over the [[St. Louis Rams]], and a career-high passer rating of 146.8 in a Week 12 37–3 road victory over the Browns. During Week 13, Dalton fractured the thumb on his throwing hand while tackling [[Stephon Tuitt]] after an intercepted [[shovel pass]], missing the season's final three games (replacement [[A. J. McCarron]] was 2–1 with a 97.1 passer rating).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals – December 13th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512130cin.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150242/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512130cin.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Dalton finished the year with 3,250 passing yards, 25 touchdowns, and seven interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Dalton 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaltAn00/gamelog/2015 |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 13, 2018 ====2016 season====
{{See also|2016 Cincinnati Bengals season}}
Dalton began the 2016 season with back-to-back 366 yard games, overcoming seven sacks for a 55-yard game-winning drive in the 23–22 road victory over the [[New York Jets]] in Week 1, but losing on the road 24–16 in Week 2 to the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at New York Jets – September 11th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609110nyj.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=June 21, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220621020150/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609110nyj.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Pittsburgh Steelers – September 18th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609180pit.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150326/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609180pit.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> After an off-night of 206 yards, zero touchdowns, and an interception in a 29–17 loss to the [[Denver Broncos]], Dalton completed 69.5% of his passes for 1,127 yards, six touchdowns, and no interceptions in four straight 100+ passer rating games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denver Broncos at Cincinnati Bengals – September 25th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609250cin.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150342/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609250cin.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Despite a middle-of-the-pack 89.7 rating through 13 games, Dalton had been sacked a league-leading 32 times and the Bengals were 3–7–1 and out of the playoffs. Dalton had 332 yards and a 130.0 passer rating in a Week 13 32–14 victory over the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], but averaged just 208 yards over the season's last four games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at Cincinnati Bengals – December 4th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612040cin.htm |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150223/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612040cin.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> The Bengals ended the season with a 6–9–1 record, with Dalton throwing a career-low 18 touchdowns, and second in the league with 41 sacks. However, he recorded over 4,000 passing yards for the second time in his career, had just eight interceptions on 563 attempts, and contributed four rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Dalton 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaltAn00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=January 13, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150344/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaltAn00/gamelog/2016/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Marvin Lewis]] praised it as "the best campaign of [Dalton's] career", and he earned his third Pro Bowl recognition, replacing the Super Bowl-bound [[Tom Brady]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 23, 2017 |title=Dalton Named For Third Career Pro Bowl Trip |url=http://www.bengals.com/news/article-1/Dalton-Named-For-Third-Career-Pro-Bowl-Trip/81419bfa-9519-47c2-98f2-d1345f378425 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170306211643/http://www.bengals.com/news/article-1/Dalton-Named-For-Third-Career-Pro-Bowl-Trip/81419bfa-9519-47c2-98f2-d1345f378425 |archive-date=March 6, 2017 |access-date=March 6, 2017 |website=bengals.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/probowl.htm |access-date=March 21, 2018 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=March 17, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180317035954/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/probowl.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2017 season====
{{See also|2017 Cincinnati Bengals season}}
[[File:Andy dalton 2017 (1).jpg|thumb|175px|Dalton in [[Northwest Stadium|Washington]] in 2017]]
Dalton threw three interceptions in the first half during the home opener against the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in Week 1. Overall, he finished the game with 170 passing yards and had four interceptions as the Bengals were shut out and lost by a score of 20–0. Dalton's four interceptions tied his career high for a single game, with the other instance occurring against the Ravens in a 2013 matchup.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Dalton Career Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaltAn00/gamelog/ |access-date=October 6, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] |archive-date=October 7, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171007022818/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaltAn00/gamelog/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hanzus |first=Dan |date=September 10, 2017 |title=Andy Dalton has three-pick meltdown in first half |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/andy-dalton-has-three-pick-meltdown-in-first-half-0ap3000000841702 |access-date=September 10, 2017 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=September 11, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170911051304/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000841702/article/andy-dalton-has-threepick-meltdown-in-first-half |url-status=live }}</ref> Though the Bengals were eliminated from playoff contention by the time of the rematch with Baltimore in Week 17, Dalton threw a game-winning touchdown pass to [[Tyler Boyd (American football)|Tyler Boyd]] with 44 seconds left in the game, eliminating the Ravens from the postseason and allowing the [[Buffalo Bills]] to clinch their first playoff berth since 1999.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 31, 2017 |title=Bengals stun Ravens, 31–27; Dalton to Boyd with 44 seconds left |url=http://www.bengals.com/news/article-1/Bengals-stun-Ravens-31-27-Dalton-to-Boyd-with-44-seconds-left/d9341c53-b58c-43ce-b5ef-e1109f76b665 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180105180330/http://www.bengals.com/news/article-1/Bengals-stun-Ravens-31-27-Dalton-to-Boyd-with-44-seconds-left/d9341c53-b58c-43ce-b5ef-e1109f76b665 |archive-date=January 5, 2018 |access-date=January 5, 2018 |website=Bengals.com}}</ref> Thanks to the Bengals' victory, thousands of grateful Bills fans donated money to Dalton's personal charity. Most of the donations were in $17 increments in honor of the Bills breaking their 17-year playoff drought.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/01/03/sports/andy-dalton-bills-charity.html|title=Andy Dalton Saved the Bills, and Fans Flocked to His Charity|last=Victor|first=Daniel|date=2018|work=The New York Times|access-date=2018-01-04|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Over 11,000 people donated a combined over $250,000 to the Andy & Jordan Dalton Foundation, while Boyd's charity of choice, the Western Pennsylvania Youth Athletic Association, received $50,000 in donations from Bills fans.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://buffalonews.com/2018/01/03/dalton-foundation-buys-billboards-to-say-thank-you-to-bills-fans/|title=Bengals QB Andy Dalton's foundation buys billboards to say 'thank you' to Bills fans|last=Besecker|first=Aaron|date=2018-01-03|work=The Buffalo News|access-date=2018-01-04}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/nfl/bengals/2018/01/04/buffalo-bills-fans-also-generous-tyler-boyds-charity/1003369001/|title=Buffalo Bills fans also generous with Tyler Boyd's charity|first=Dave|last=Clark|work=The Cincinnati Enquirer|date=January 4, 2018|access-date=January 4, 2018}}</ref> In the Bengals' 7–9 season, Dalton started all 16 games and finished with 3,320 passing yards, 25 touchdowns, and 12 interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Dalton 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaltAn00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=July 3, 2022 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]] |archive-date=January 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220111004858/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaltAn00/gamelog/2017/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2018 season====
{{See also|2018 Cincinnati Bengals season}}
During Week 2, Dalton threw four touchdown passes in the home-opener against the division rival [[Baltimore Ravens]]. All four touchdowns were in the first half, three of them were caught by [[A. J. Green]]. The Bengals went on to win 34–23.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hobson |first=Geoff |date=September 13, 2018 |title=Complete Team Effort Lifts Bengals Past Ravens, 34–23 |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/complete-team-effort-lifts-bengals-past-ravens-34-23 |access-date=June 26, 2019 |website=Bengals.com |archive-date=September 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180915042334/https://www.bengals.com/news/complete-team-effort-lifts-bengals-past-ravens-34-23 |url-status=live}}</ref> During Week 12 against the [[Cleveland Browns]], Dalton suffered a thumb injury in the fourth quarter and did not return.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marcum |first=Jason |date=November 26, 2018 |title=Bengals place Andy Dalton on injured reserve; claim QB Tom Savage off waivers |url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2018/11/26/18113325/bengals-tom-savage-waivers-49ers-andy-dalton-injured-reserve |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200305065447/https://www.cincyjungle.com/2018/11/26/18113325/bengals-tom-savage-waivers-49ers-andy-dalton-injured-reserve |archive-date=March 5, 2020 |access-date=June 18, 2020 |website=Cincy Jungle|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> It was revealed that he suffered torn ligaments in the thumb and was placed on [[injured reserve]] on November 26, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Teope |first=Herbie |date=November 26, 2018 |title=Bengals place Andy Dalton (thumb) on injured reserve |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bengals-place-andy-dalton-thumb-on-injured-reserve-0ap3000000992897 |access-date=June 26, 2019 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=June 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190620213315/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000992897/article/bengals-place-andy-dalton-thumb-on-injured-reserve |url-status=live }}</ref> In 11 games in the 2018 season, Dalton finished with 2,566 passing yards, 21 touchdowns, and 11 interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Skinner |first=Richard |date=November 26, 2018 |title=Bengals' Dalton out for season with thumb injury |url=http://local12.com/sports/bengals/bengals-dalton-out-for-season-with-thumb-injury-andy-cincinnati-nfl-national-football-league-cleveland-browns-driskel-savage-quarterback-marvin-lewis-lazor |access-date=January 22, 2019 |website=WKRC |archive-date=January 23, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190123223158/https://local12.com/sports/bengals/bengals-dalton-out-for-season-with-thumb-injury-andy-cincinnati-nfl-national-football-league-cleveland-browns-driskel-savage-quarterback-marvin-lewis-lazor |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2019 season====
{{See also|2019 Cincinnati Bengals season}}
[[File:Andy Dalton 2019.jpg|thumb|200px|Dalton (right) in [[Huntington Bank Field|Cleveland]] in 2019]]
During Week 1 against the [[Seattle Seahawks]], Dalton threw for a career-high 418 yards and two touchdowns in the 20–21 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 8, 2019 |title=Close call: Seahawks hold off Dalton, Bengals for 21–20 win |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127995 |access-date=September 8, 2019 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=September 9, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190909070119/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127995 |url-status=live }}</ref> Following an 0–8 start to the season, Bengals head coach [[Zac Taylor]] announced that he would bench Dalton and start rookie [[Ryan Finley (American football)|Ryan Finley]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Jaggi |first=Tommy |date=October 29, 2019 |title=Bengals Bench Andy Dalton: Should They Trade Him? |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/bengals/news/bengals-andy-dalton-benched |access-date=October 29, 2019 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |archive-date=October 29, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191029175909/https://www.si.com/nfl/bengals/news/bengals-andy-dalton-benched |url-status=live }}</ref> After three games and losses with Finley, Dalton was renamed the starting quarterback on November 25, 2019, for their upcoming game against the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=November 25, 2019 |title=Bengals starting Andy Dalton at QB against Jets |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001080731/article/bengals-starting-andy-dalton-at-qb-vs-jets |access-date=September 22, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}{{dead link|date=June 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> In the game, he threw for 243 yards and a touchdown as the Bengals won their first game of the season by a score of 22–6.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 1, 2019 |title=Dalton returns and leads Bengals to 1st win, 22–6 over Jets |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128057 |access-date=December 1, 2019 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |archive-date=December 2, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191202101605/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128057 |url-status=live }}</ref> In Week 15 against the [[New England Patriots]], Dalton threw for 151 yards, a touchdown, and four interceptions during the 34–13 loss. This was Dalton's fourth career game with four interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 15, 2019 |title=Brady throws 2 TDs, Patriots beat Bengals to clinch playoffs |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127955 |access-date=December 15, 2019 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |archive-date=December 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191217101611/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127955 |url-status=live }}</ref> During a Week 16 road matchup against the [[Miami Dolphins]], he threw for 396 yards and four touchdowns. Dalton scored 16 points in the final 29 seconds of regulation to force an overtime that the Bengals ultimately lost 38–35 to clinch the NFL's worst record.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 22, 2019 |title=Dolphins survive late collapse and beat Bengals in OT, 38–35 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127910 |access-date=September 22, 2020 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |language=en |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=December 25, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191225124520/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127910 |url-status=live }}</ref> In the regular-season finale against the [[Cleveland Browns]], Dalton threw for 190 yards, a touchdown, and an interception. In addition, he had eight carries for 10 yards and a touchdown during the 33–23 win. After the game, Dalton said that if it was his last game as a Bengal, "It was good to end it taking a knee."<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 29, 2019 |title=Fond farewell: Andy Dalton leads Bengals over Browns 33–23 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127978 |access-date=December 29, 2019 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |archive-date=December 30, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191230182411/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127978 |url-status=live }}</ref> Dalton appeared in 13 games in the 2019 season and recorded 3,494 passing yards, 16 touchdowns, and 14 interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Dalton 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaltAn00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=January 1, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 2, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200102001145/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaltAn00/gamelog/2019/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On April 30, 2020, after nine seasons with the franchise, the Bengals released Dalton after selecting [[Joe Burrow]] as the first overall pick in the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 30, 2020 |title=Bengals Release Andy Dalton |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-release-andy-dalton |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200813181029/https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-release-andy-dalton |archive-date=August 13, 2020 |access-date=June 17, 2020 |website=Bengals.com}}</ref>

====2023 season====

{{See also|2024 Carolina Panthers season}}
On September 16, 2024, after the Panthers fell to 0–2 and Young continued to struggle, Dalton was named the starting quarterback.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Newton |first=David |date=September 16, 2024 |title=Sources: Panthers bench Young, to start Dalton |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/41288868/sources-andy-dalton-replacing-bryce-young-panthers-qb |access-date=September 23, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref> In his first start against the [[Las Vegas Raiders]], Dalton threw for over 300 yards and three touchdowns, leading the Panthers to scores on seven of their 12 possessions as they won 36–22.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Owens |first=Jason |date=September 22, 2024 |title=Panthers' offense comes alive in blowout of Raiders with Andy Dalton in place of Bryce Young |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/panthers-offense-comes-alive-in-blowout-of-raiders-with-andy-dalton-in-place-of-bryce-young-232048697.html |access-date=September 22, 2024 |work=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref> On October 22, Dalton and his family were involved in a car accident.<ref name="u699">{{cite web |last=DeArdo |first=Bryan |title=Panthers' Andy Dalton and his family involved in car accident, but no one required emergency medical transport |website=CBSSports.com |date=September 24, 2024 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/panthers-andy-dalton-and-his-family-involved-in-car-accident-but-no-one-required-emergency-medical-transport/ |access-date=October 23, 2024}}</ref> No one in the vehicle required emergency medical transport, but Dalton sustained an injury to the thumb on his throwing hand, ruling him out for the Panthers' Week 8 matchup against the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Newton |first=David |date=October 23, 2024 |title=Panthers' Bryce Young to start after Dalton hurts thumb in crash |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/41964652/panthers-bryce-young-start-dalton-hurts-thumb-crash |access-date=October 23, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Although Dalton recovered, Young remained the Panthers' starter for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Newton |first=David |title=Will Andy Dalton return to back up Bryce Young on Panthers? |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/42929726/nfl-carolina-panthers-andy-dalton-bryce-young-free-agent |access-date=January 11, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |date=December 13, 2024}}</ref>

====2025 season====
{{See also|2025 Carolina Panthers season}}
On February 18, 2025, Dalton signed another two-year contract extension with the Panthers, making it his third season with the team. His contract was worth $8 million and has a maximum value of $10 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Newton |first=David |date=February 18, 2025 |title=Panthers re-sign QB Dalton to two-year contract |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/43907563/source-panthers-backup-qb-andy-dalton-agree-2-year-deal |access-date=February 18, 2025 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> During the Panthers week 2 preseason game against the [[Houston Texans]], Dalton would leave late in the first quarter early due to an elbow injury sustained when he was hit by Texans [[linebacker]] [[Danielle Hunter]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Rizzuti |first=Anthony |title=Panthers QB Andy Dalton exits game vs. Texans with right elbow injury |work=Panthers Wire |publisher=USA Today |date=2025-08-16 |url=https://pantherswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/panthers/2025/08/16/panthers-texans-nfl-preseason-andy-dalton-injury/85691501007/ |access-date=2025-12-20}}</ref> Dalton appeared in four games in the 2025 season, passing for 293 yards, 1 TD and 1 INT. He made one start, which came in a Week 8 loss against the Buffalo Bills.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Dalton 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DaltAn00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-01-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

=== Philadelphia Eagles ===
On March 24, 2026, Dalton was traded to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in exchange for a 2027 seventh-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Gantt|first=Darin|title=Andy Dalton trade to the Eagles becomes official|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/andy-dalton-trade-to-the-eagles-becomes-official-future-seventh-rounder|website=panthers.com|date=March 24, 2026|access-date=March 24, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Dalton is a [[Christians|Christian]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cooley |first=Joshua |date=August 29, 2013 |title=Bengal Believer |url=http://www.fca.org/magazine/2013/08/29/bengal-believer |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160127083758/https://www.fca.org/magazine/2013/08/29/bengal-believer |archive-date=January 27, 2016 |website=FCA.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Stevenson |first=Stefan |date=December 25, 2010 |title=Andy Dalton provides a greater faith for TCU Horned Frogs |url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/college-sports/tcu-horned-frogs/20101225-andy-dalton-provides-a-greater-faith-for-tcu-horned-frogs.ece |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110804233726/https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/college-sports/tcu-horned-frogs/20101225-andy-dalton-provides-a-greater-faith-for-tcu-horned-frogs.ece |archive-date=August 4, 2011 |work=Dallas News}}</ref> On July 9, 2011, he married his longtime girlfriend, Jordan Jones, whom he met at [[Texas Christian University|TCU]]. In July 2014, Jones gave birth to the couple's first son.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marcum |first=Jason |date=July 1, 2014 |title=Andy Dalton's wife give Birth to baby boy |url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2014/7/1/5861822/andy-dalton-and-wife-give-birth--baby-boy |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=cincyjungle.com |archive-date=August 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180814001958/https://www.cincyjungle.com/platform/amp/2014/7/1/5861822/andy-dalton-and-wife-give-birth--baby-boy |url-status=live }}</ref> Their second son was born in March 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stevens |first=Matthew |date=March 19, 2017 |title=Andy Dalton and wife welcome second child |url=https://bengalswire.usatoday.com/2017/03/19/andy-dalton-welcomes-his-second-child/ |access-date=August 13, 2018 |work=Bengals Wire |publisher=USA Today |archive-date=August 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180814001756/https://bengalswire.usatoday.com/2017/03/19/andy-dalton-welcomes-his-second-child/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Their third child, a daughter, was born in January 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Beighle |first=Nathan |date=January 13, 2019 |title=Andy, Jordan Dalton welcome third child |url=https://bengalswire.usatoday.com/2019/01/13/andy-jordan-dalton-welcome-third-child/ |website=bengalswire.com |publisher=USA Today |access-date=July 8, 2019 |archive-date=January 14, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190114213140/https://bengalswire.usatoday.com/2019/01/13/andy-jordan-dalton-welcome-third-child/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Dalton and his wife founded the Andy & Jordan Dalton Foundation, which aims to help families and children in need. After Dalton helped the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] defeat the [[Baltimore Ravens]] 31–27 in Week 17 of the [[2017 NFL season|2017 season]], which allowed the [[Buffalo Bills]] to enter the playoffs, many Bills fans donated to his foundation in gratitude for helping their team snap their 17-year playoff drought. In less than a week, donations exceeded $360,000 from over 16,000 donors. Most donations were in the amount of $17, which symbolized the 17-year playoff drought that ended with the Bengals' victory over the Ravens. Dalton and his wife thanked Buffalo Bills fans by renting five billboards in the Buffalo area that read "Thank you, Buffalo, and good luck."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Young |first=Shalize Manza |date=January 1, 2018 |title=Bills fans thanking Bengals, Dalton with donations |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/bills-fans-thanking-bengals-andy-dalton-donations-foundation-202541480.html |access-date=November 20, 2019 |work=Yahoo! Sports |archive-date=April 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401145113/https://sports.yahoo.com/bills-fans-thanking-bengals-andy-dalton-donations-foundation-202541480.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kahler |first=Kalyn |date=January 11, 2018 |title=Bills Fans' Generosity: Meet the Families Being Helped by Donations to Andy Dalton's Foundation |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2018/01/11/buffalo-bills-fans-andy-dalton-foundation-donations |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=SI.com |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115001338/https://www.si.com/nfl/2018/01/11/buffalo-bills-fans-andy-dalton-foundation-donations |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lynch |first=Kaley |date=January 3, 2018 |title=Bengals QB Andy Dalton and wife Jordan thank Bills fans with billboards |url=https://www.wivb.com/news/bengals-qb-andy-dalton-and-wife-jordan-thank-bills-fans-with-billboards/ |access-date=January 14, 2018 |website=wivb.com |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115184525/http://wivb.com/2018/01/03/bengals-qb-andy-dalton-and-wife-jordan-thank-bills-fans-with-billboards/amp/ |url-status=live }}</ref> 

He has been nicknamed the "Red Rifle", a reference to both his throwing arm strength and his hair color.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Phil |date=September 15, 2014 |title=Andy Dalton Doesn't Need Your Love |url=https://www.si.com/vault/2014/09/15/106634572/andy-dalton-doesnt-need-your-love |access-date=December 30, 2017 |website=SI.com |archive-date=December 31, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171231004210/https://www.si.com/vault/2014/09/15/106634572/andy-dalton-doesnt-need-your-love |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Fowler |first=Jeremy |date=June 3, 2016 |title=So when did Andy Dalton get more famous than Ben Roethlisberger? |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/pittsburgh-steelers/post/_/id/19028/so-when-did-andy-dalton-get-more-famous-than-ben-roethlisberger |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180801190353/https://www.espn.com/blog/pittsburgh-steelers/post/_/id/19028/so-when-did-andy-dalton-get-more-famous-than-ben-roethlisberger |archive-date=August 1, 2018 |access-date=December 30, 2017 |url-status=live |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

'''Andrew Victor Sendejo''' (born September 9, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Rice Owls football|Rice Owls]], and was signed by the [[Sacramento Mountain Lions]] of the [[United Football League (2009–12)|United Football League]] (UFL) as a [[free agent]] in 2010. Sendejo was also in uniform for the [[Dallas Cowboys]], [[New York Jets]], [[Philadelphia Eagles]], [[Minnesota Vikings]], [[Cleveland Browns]], and [[Indianapolis Colts]].

==Early life==
Sendejo is a 2006 graduate of [[Smithson Valley High School]] in [[Spring Branch, Houston|Spring Branch]], northeast of [[San Antonio, Texas]]. He was a two-time All-San Antonio area selection for coach Larry Hill. Also a two-time honorable mention All-State pick, and a two-time All-District 26-5A honoree. As a senior, he had 75 [[tackle (football move)|tackles]] (3 for loss), four [[interceptions]], eight pass deflections, one forced [[fumble]] and one fumble recovery, helping lead the Rangers to a 13–2 record and the Class 5A semifinals. He was named Comal County defensive player of the year for his  senior season efforts. He was also a regional finalist and academic All-district. Sendejo selected Rice over [[Tulane Green Wave football|Tulane]], [[Army Black Knights football|Army]], [[North Texas Mean Green football|North Texas]], [[Northwestern Wildcats football|Northwestern]] and [[New Mexico Lobos|New Mexico]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.riceowls.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/sendejo_andrew00.html | title=Rice Owls bio | access-date=February 19, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130525074910/http://www.riceowls.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/sendejo_andrew00.html | archive-date=May 25, 2013 | url-status=dead }}</ref>
 
In addition to [[american football|football]], Sendejo also lettered in [[Association football|soccer]], where he was twice a second-team All-district selection and academic All-district pick, helping Smithson Valley to the district and bi-district championships. He also participated in [[track & field]] for the Rangers; at the 2004 District 27-5A Championships, he placed third in the 400-meter dash (52.80 seconds), sixth in the [[triple jump]] (12.04m or 39'4") and fifth in the [[pole vault]] (3.53m or 11'6"). As a junior in 2005, he posted a personal-best time of 52.02 seconds in the [[400-meter dash]] at the Texas State High School Invitational.

==College career==
At [[Rice University|Rice]], Sendejo saw his senior season come to an early conclusion after suffering a severe high ankle sprain at [[East Carolina Pirates football|East Carolina]] that required surgery. He was a Preseason All [[Conference USA|C-USA]] pick by conference coaches and a three-year starter who opened the season as the national leader among active players in solo tackles and also ranked in the top 10 among active players in career total tackles, career interceptions and interception returns for touchdowns. He was a Second-team All [[Conference USA|C-USA]] preseason selection by the media in a poll conducted by the [[New Orleans Times-Picayune]]. He also earned an Honorable Mention All [[Conference USA|C-USA]] honors from league coaches even with a shortened senior season, and was named one of 12 finalist for the 2009 [[Wuerffel Trophy]], which honors the college football player who best combines exemplary community service with outstanding academic and athletic achievement. He was a three-time [[ESPN The Magazine]] District VI academic honoree as well as a three-time [[Conference USA|C-USA]] All Academic Football team with a 3.55 [[Grading (education)|GPA]] in [[sports management]].

===2006 season===
{{see also|2006 Rice Owls football team}}

A starter from the first whistle of the season who went on to earn honorable mention freshman [[All-American]] recognition from [[The Sporting News]] and [[Conference USA|C-USA]] all-freshman honors from the media, Sendejo made 10 starts on the season in 11 played games, missing just the [[UAB Blazers football|UAB]] game with an injury. He finished fifth on the team with 49 total [[tackle (football move)|tackles]] from the Spur position, tied for fourth on the squad with seven tackles for loss and was second on the team by forcing three [[fumbles]]. He forced one fumble and recovered a second to set up a touchdown for the Owls against [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane football|Tulsa]]. He opened the season with a 13-yard [[quarterback sack|sack]] of [[Kevin Kolb]] of [[Houston Cougars football|Houston]] and closed it with a seven-yard sack of Justin Willis of [[SMU Mustangs football|SMU]].

===2007 season===
{{see also|2007 Rice Owls football team}}

As a sophomore in 2007, Sendejo led the team with 107 [[tackle (football move)|tackles]] and five [[interceptions]]. His five interceptions were the most by an Owl since [[Dan Dawson]] tied the school record with seven in 2000 and match the third-best total by an Owl in a season. He earned honorable mention All [[Conference USA|C-USA]] honors by the coaches and third-team All conference mention by [[Phil Steele]]. Also named Academic All-Conference and All-District VI for his work in the classroom as well. He closed the season strongly, registering back-to-back double figure tackle efforts against [[Tulane Green Wave football|Tulane]] (11) and [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane football|Tulsa]] (13). He posted four double figure games on the season, including a career-best 18-tackle day at [[Marshall Thundering Herd football|Marshall]], the most by an Owl since Jeff Vanover was credited with 18 against SMU in 2001. He was named [[Conference USA|C-USA]] Defensive Player of the Week against [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles football|Southern Miss]] after picking off a pair of passes, forcing a fumble, and registering seven tackles, becoming the first Owl to pick off more than one pass in a game since Dan Dawson picked off three vs. Hawaii back in 2000. He was credited with eight tackles, shared a tackle for loss, forced and recovered a fumble and broke up a pass at [[Houston Cougars football|Houston]]. He returned his interception against [[SMU Mustangs football|SMU]] 31 yards for a score for his first career [[touchdown]].

===2008 season===
{{see also|2008 Rice Owls football team}}

Sendejo was an honorable mention All [[Conference USA|C-USA]] pick by the coaches, second-team pick by the [[Houston Chronicle]], while [[Phil Steele]] placed him on his first-team, All-conference unit. He led the Owls with 94 total [[tackle (football move)|tackles]] despite missing nearly three full games with a high ankle sprain. He also totaled 89 yards in returns, bringing back an interception 55 yards for a [[touchdown]] and returning a fumble 34 yards to set up a second score. That interception return was his second of his career for a score, with both coming against SMU. He was fifth in [[Conference USA|C-USA]] stats with 8.55 tackles per game (51st nationally) and 22nd in [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] stats with 5.4 solo tackles per game. He opened the year by earning [[Conference USA|C-USA]] Defensive Player of the Week honors for his game vs. [[SMU Mustangs football|SMU]]. He had back-to-back 13-tackle efforts at [[Memphis Tigers football|Memphis]] and [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt]], then was credited with a season-high 17 tackles at [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas]], one shy of his career-high of 18 set in 2007 at [[Marshall Thundering Herd football|Marshall]]. He saw his streak of double-figure tackle games end at three when he was credited for three stops against [[North Texas Mean Green football|North Texas]]. In that game, he made his debut as the Owls' [[kickoff specialist|punt returner]], fielding a pair for no gain, then returned his third for a gain of 21. He got injured early in the [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane football|Tulsa]] game and did not record a tackle. He missed the [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles football|Southern Miss]] game, breaking a streak of 24 consecutive games played (23 starts). He also missed the [[Tulane Green Wave football|Tulane]] game, and then returned to action against [[UTEP Miners football|UTEP]] and led the Owls with eight tackles. He closed out the regular season by recording his fifth double-figure tackle game of the year with 13 vs. [[Houston Cougars football|Houston]]. It was his ninth career double-figure tackle game.

===2009 season===
{{see also|2009 Rice Owls football team}}

As a senior, Sendejo was named to [[Phil Steele]]'s Midseason All [[Conference USA|C-USA]] Third-team. He was able to play in only 7 games, after his season was cut short by a high ankle injury that required surgery. He was tied for sixth in the nation with 6.4 unassisted tackles per game at the time of his injury. He moved into a tie for second on the Owls' career tackle chart with nine stops at [[East Carolina Pirates football|ECU]], and jumped four spots on the tackling chart with 17 tackles vs. [[Navy Midshipmen football|Navy]], matching the second highest game total of his career. It was his 11th career double-figure tackle game. He was the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] career active leader with 216 career solo [[tackle (football move)|tackles]] ([[Sean Weatherspoon]] of [[Missouri Tigers football|Missouri]] was second with 199) before he got hurt. He ranked fourth in [[Conference USA|C-USA]] and 14th in the nation with a 14.3 yard average per punt return before his injury. He returned two punts for 65 yards vs. [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt]], including a career best 47 yarder, the longest by an Owl since 1998 when [[LaDouphyous McCalla]] returned one 51 yards against Colorado State. He missed part of the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders football|Texas Tech]] game after injuring a wrist, but returned to finish the game. He recorded his 10th career double-digit tackle total in the opener at [[UAB Blazers football|UAB]] with 15 stops. He finished his college career with 318 tackles (second in school history), 9 interceptions (seventh in school history), 2 sacks and 7 forced fumbles.
