===Dallas Cowboys===
====2010====
On November 24, 2010, the [[Dallas Cowboys]] signed Sendejo to a two-year, $725,000 contract to join their [[practice squad]] as an [[unrestricted free agent]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cowboys add safety Andrew Sendejo to practice squad |url=http://cowboysblog.dallasnews.com/archives/2010/11/cowboys-add-safety-andrew-send.html |publisher=Dallas News |date=November 24, 2010 |access-date=November 24, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101125205848/http://cowboysblog.dallasnews.com/archives/2010/11/cowboys-add-safety-andrew-send.html |archive-date=November 25, 2010 }}</ref><ref name="spotrac">{{cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Andrew Sendejo contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/minnesota-vikings/andrew-sendejo-8036/ |access-date=June 13, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref> On November 29, 2010, Sendejo was promoted to the active roster.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cowboys promote safety, cut defensive end |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4675006/cowboys-promote-safety-cut-defensive-end |publisher=ESPN Dallas |date=November 29, 2010 |access-date=November 29, 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101201044818/http://espn.go.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4675006/cowboys-promote-safety-cut-defensive-end| archive-date= December 1, 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> On December 12, 2010, Sendejo made his NFL debut during a 30–27 loss against the [[2010 Philadelphia Eagles|Philadelphia Eagles]]. On December 19, 2010, Sendejo recorded his first career tackle on kick returner [[Brandon Banks]] during a 33–30 victory against the [[2010 Washington Redskins|Washington Redskins]]. Sendejo and teammate [[Sam Hurd]] tackled Banks on a 22-yard kick return in the second quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 15-2010: Washington Redskins @ Dallas Cowboys |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2010121905/2010/REG15/redskins@cowboys |access-date=June 13, 2018 |website=NFL.com |date=December 19, 2010 }}</ref> He finished his rookie season with one tackle in two games.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cowboys Future Focus: S Andrew Sendejo |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4677341/cowboys-future-focus-s-andrew-sendejo |access-date=June 13, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |date=January 19, 2011 }}</ref>

Throughout training camp, Sendejo competed for a roster spot as a backup safety against Collin Zych and [[Danny McCray]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Cowboys still in play for a safety |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas-cowboys/post/_/id/4681241/cowboys-still-in-play-for-a-safety |access-date=June 13, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |author=Watkins, Calvin |date=August 2, 2011}}</ref> On September 3, 2011, the Dallas Cowboys waived Sendejo as part of their final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Andrew Sendejo move to Jets a coincidence? |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4683092/andrew-sendejo-move-to-jets-a-coincidence |access-date=June 13, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |author=Archer, Todd |date=September 5, 2011}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
On September 4, 2011, the [[New York Jets]] claimed Sendejo off of waivers and signed him to their active roster.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jets awarded four players off waivers, including QB Kevin O'Connell; cut Aaron Maybin|url=http://www.nj.com/jets/index.ssf/2011/09/jets_claim_center_colin_baxter.html|work=The Star-Ledger|publisher=Advance Publications|author=Vrentas, Jenny|date=September 4, 2011|access-date=September 4, 2011}}</ref> His signing was marred in minor controversy as it was speculated the New York Jets signed him in a bid to gain intelligence of the Dallas Cowboys' defense. At the time, the New York Jets' head coach was [[Rex Ryan]] and his twin brother, [[Rob Ryan]], was the Dallas Cowboys' defensive coordinator. Cowboys' quarterback [[Tony Romo]] stated during a press conference that Rob Ryan had made minor adjustments to the defense to prevent any information to possibly be passed on to the Jets. On September 13, 2011, the New York Jets waived Sendejo.<ref name="waive">{{cite web |title=Jets waive S Andrew Sendejo from active roster, cut LB Matthias Berning from practice squad |url=http://www.nj.com/jets/index.ssf/2011/09/jets_waive_s_andrew_sendejo_fr.html |access-date=June 13, 2018 |website=NJ.com |author=Orr, Connor |date=September 13, 2011}}</ref> The following day, Sendejo was signed to the Jets' practice squad after clearing waivers. On September 27, 2011, the Jets released Sendejo from their practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Former Cowboy Andrew Sendejo helped Jets confirm some of Dallas' tendencies|url=https://www.chatsports.com/new-york-jets/a/source/former-cowboy-andrew-sendejo-helped-jets-confirm-some-of-dallas-tendencies-4561640 |access-date=June 13, 2018 |website=ChatSports.com |date=September 8, 2011}}</ref> After his release, Sendejo verified that the Jets coaching staff had in fact asked him about the Dallas Cowboys' defense, but mainly asked him to verify some tendencies.<ref name="waive"/>

===Minnesota Vikings===
====2011====
On November 29, 2011, the [[Minnesota Vikings]] signed Sendejo to a two-year, $900,000 contract.<ref name="spotrac"/> On December 11, 2011, Sendejo made his Minnesota Vikings' debut and recorded one solo tackle during their 34–28 loss at the [[2011 Detroit Lions|Detroit Lions]] in Week 14. He was inactive as a healthy scratch the following week before appearing in the last two regular season games.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Andrew Sendejo (2011) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrewsendejo/2525323/gamelogs?season=2011 |access-date=June 13, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the 2011 season with three combined tackles (two solo) in three games and zero starts.<ref name="career">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Andrew Sendejo (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrewsendejo/2525323/careerstats |access-date=June 13, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2012====
Sendejo entered training camp and competed for a roster spot as a backup safety against [[Jamarca Sanford]], [[Robert Blanton]], and [[Eric Frampton]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings Roster 2012: Latest News, Cuts, Preseason Predictions |url=https://www.bleacherreport.com/1280836-minnesota-vikings-roster-2012-latest-news-cuts-preseason-predictions.html |access-date=June 13, 2018 |website=bleacherreport.com |author=Arcand, Tim |date=August 4, 2011 }}{{dead link|date=May 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Head coach [[Leslie Frazier]] named Sendejo the third strong safety on the depth chart to begin the regular season, behind rookie [[Harrison Smith]] and Jamarca Sanford.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vikings Depth Chart: Minnesota Updates Depth Chart As Week 1 Nears |url=https://www.minnesota.sbnation.com/platform//minnesota-vikings/2012/9/5/3295529/vikings-depth-chart-2012-week-1 |access-date=June 13, 2018 |website=Minnesota.Sbnation.com |author=Sargent, Jordan |date=September 5, 2012 }}{{Dead link|date=September 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

He was inactive for the [[2012 Minnesota Vikings|Minnesota Vikings']] season-opening 26–23 victory against the [[2012 Jacksonville Jaguars|Jacksonville Jaguars]] after sustaining an ankle injury during the preseason.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vikings Roster Back To Full Strength Heading Into Week 2 |url=https://minnesota.sbnation.com/minnesota-vikings/2012/9/12/3323816/vikings-injury-update-week-2 |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=minnesota.sbnation.com |author=Ryan, Dave |date=September 12, 2012}}</ref> He missed another two games (Weeks 4–5) after aggravating his ankle injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Christian Ponder Finds His Way Onto The Minnesota Vikings Injury Report |url=http://minnesota.cbslocal.com/2012/09/29/christian-ponder-finds-his-way-onto-the-minnesota-vikings-injury-report/ |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=minnesota.cbslocal.com |author=Gunther, Joseph |date=September 29, 2012}}</ref> In Week 7, he made a solo tackle on [[Patrick Peterson]] during a five-yard punt return in the third quarter of a 21–14 win against the [[2012 Arizona Cardinals|Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 7-2012: Arizona Cardinals @ Minnesota Vikings |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2012102101/2012/REG7/cardinals@vikings |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=NFL.com |date=October 21, 2012 }}</ref> Sendejo played primarily on special teams in 2012 and finished the season with six solo tackles in 13 games and zero starts.<ref name="career"/> The Minnesota Vikings finished second in the [[NFC North]] with a 10–6 record and earned a wildcard berth. On January 5, 2013, Sendejo appeared in his first career playoff game and recorded a season-high two combined tackles during a 24–10 loss at the [[2012 Green Bay Packers|Green Bay Packers]] in the NFC Wildcard Game.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Post 19-2012: Minnesota Vikings @ Green Bay Packers |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013010501/2012/POST18/vikings@packers |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2013====
Sendejo became an exclusive rights free agent in 2013 and was required to re-sign with the Vikings if he was offered a contract. On March 15, 2013, the Minnesota Vikings signed Sendejo to a one-year, [[United States dollar|$]]630,000 contract for the 
required veteran league minimum.<ref>{{cite web |title=Breaking Down the Contract Needed to Re-Sign Every Minnesota Vikings Free Agent |url=https://www.bleacherreport.com/1547211-breaking-down-the-contract-needed-to-re-sign-every-minnesota-vikings-free-agent.html |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=BleacherReport.com |author=Stensrud, Matthew |date=March 1, 2013 }}{{dead link|date=May 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

Throughout [[training camp]], Sendejo competed to be the starting strong safety against [[Mistral Raymond]], Robert Blanton, Jamarca Sanford, Brandan Bishop, and [[Darius Eubanks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings 2013 Training Camp: Day Twelve Notebook |url=https://www.dailynorseman.com/2013/8/12/4613962/minnesota-vikings-2013-training-camp-day-twelve-notebook-nfl |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=dailynorseman.com |author=Hasan, Arif |date=August 12, 2013}}</ref> Head coach Leslie Frazier officially named Sendejo a backup strong safety, behind Jamarca Sanford and Mistral Raymond, to start the regular season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Minnesota Vikings Depth Chart: 09/05/2013 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/150/MIN |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On September 19, 2013, the Minnesota Vikings signed Sendejo to a two-year, $2 million [[contract]] extension that includes $400,000 guaranteed and a [[signing bonus]] $200,000.<ref name="spotrac"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Andrew Sendejo agrees to 2-year extension with Minnesota Vikings |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/andrew-sendejo-agrees-to-2-year-extension-with-minnesota-viking-0ap2000000247273 |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=NFL.com |date=September 19, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=S Andrew Sendejo Contract Details |url=https://overthecap.com/s-andrew-sendej-contract-details/ |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=OvertheCap.com |author=Fitzgerald, Andrew |date=September 20, 2013}}</ref>

On September 29, 2013, Sendejo earned his first career start in place of Jamarca Sanford, who was inactive due to a [[hamstring]] injury.<ref name="fox">{{cite web |title=Foxsports.com: Andrew Sendejo Injury History |url=https://www.foxsports.com/nfl/jamarca-sanford-player-injuries |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=FoxSports.com}}</ref> Sendejo recorded four solo tackles in a 34–27 victory against the [[2013 Pittsburgh Steelers|Pittsburgh Steelers]] in London during their Week 4 contest. In Week 7, Sendejo made his first start at free safety and recorded six combined tackles during a 23–7 loss at the [[2013 New York Giants|New York Giants]]. He started nine consecutive games at free safety (Weeks 7–15) after Harrison Smith was placed on injured reserve/designation to return due to a turf toe injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Harrison Smith injury: Vikings S placed on injured reserve/designated for return list |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2013/10/18/4852178/harrison-smith-injury-vikings-injured-reserve |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=SBNation.com |author=Bien, Louis |date=October 18, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Minnesota Vikings Depth Chart: 12/01/2013 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/153/MIN |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On November 7, 2013, he collected a career-high 16 combined tackles (eight solo) in the Vikings' 34–27 victory against the [[2013 Washington Redskins|Washington Redskins]] in Week 10.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Andrew Sendejo (2013) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrewsendejo/2525323/gamelogs?season=2013 |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> The following week, Sendejo had 11 combined tackles (six solo) during a 41–20 loss at the [[2013 Seattle Seahawks|Seattle Seahawks]] in Week 11. On December 8, 2013, Sendejo recorded three combined tackles, two pass deflections, and made his first career interception in a 29–26 loss to the [[2013 Baltimore Ravens|Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Sendejo Emerges In Smith's Absence|url=http://www.vikings.com/news/blog/article-1/Sendejo-Emerges-In-Smiths-Absence/fdcbb5c0-8f79-4f3c-8fb2-bcc958d0f37c|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306180751/http://www.vikings.com/news/blog/article-1/Sendejo-Emerges-In-Smiths-Absence/fdcbb5c0-8f79-4f3c-8fb2-bcc958d0f37c|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 6, 2016|website=Vikings.com|date=January 14, 2014}}</ref> He intercepted a pass by quarterback [[Joe Flacco]] that was originally intended for tight end [[Ed Dickson]] in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 14-2013: Minnesota Vikings @ Baltimore Ravens| url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013120800/2013/REG14/vikings@ravens |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=NFL.com | date=December 8, 2013 }}</ref> He finished [[2013 NFL season|2013]] with a career-high 84 combined tackles (52 solo), two pass deflections, and an interception in 16 games and ten starts.<ref name="career"/> On December 30, 2013, the Minnesota Vikings fired head coach [[Leslie Frazier]] after they finished fourth in the NFC North with a 5–10–1 record.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vikings fire Leslie Frazier |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/10214415/minnesota-vikings-announce-leslie-frazier-head-coach |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |date=December 30, 2013}}</ref>

====2014====
On August 4, 2014, the Minnesota Vikings activated Sendejo off of their physically unable to perform list after he fully recovered from back surgery he underwent in April.<ref>{{cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings Roster |url=http://www.mnvikingscorner.com/2014/09/minnesota-vikings-roster-analysis.html?m=1 |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=mnvikingscorner.com |date=September 1, 2014}}</ref> He competed against [[Robert Blanton]] and [[Antone Exum]] to be the starting strong safety. Head coach [[Mike Zimmer]] named Sendejo the backup free safety, behind Harrison Smith, to start the 2014 regular season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Minnesota Vikings Depth Chart: 09/01/2014 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/162/MIN |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> In Week 15, he started in place of Blanton, who was unable to play due to a leg injury. Sendejo recorded six combined tackles, in Blanton's absence, as the Vikings lost 16–14 at the [[2014 Detroit Lions|Detroit Lions]]. Defensive coordinator [[George Edwards (American football)|George Edwards]] chose to keep Sendejo as the starting strong safety for the remaining two games (Weeks 16–17), although Blanton had recovered from his leg injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Andrew Sendejo Starts at Safety Even With Robert Blanton Active |url=https://thevikingage.com/2014/12/21/andrew-sendejo-starts-safety-even-robert-blanton-active/ |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=TheVikingAge.com |date=December 21, 2014}}</ref> On December 28, 2014, Sendejo collected a season-high nine combined tackles during a 13–9 win against the [[2014 Chicago Bears|Chicago Bears]] in Week 17.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Andrew Sendejo (2014) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrewsendejo/2525323/gamelogs?season=2014 |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the season with 27 combined tackles (20 solo) and a forced fumble in 16 games and three starts.<ref name="career"/>

====2015====
During training camp, Sendejo competed against Robert Blanton, Antone Exum, and [[Anthony Harris (safety)|Anthony Harris]] to retain the job as the starting strong safety.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Minnesota Vikings Depth Chart: 08/01/2015 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/174/MIN |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Mike Zimmer]] named Sendejo the starting strong safety to start the regular season, opposite free safety [[Harrison Smith]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Vikings: Andrew Sendejo to start at safety over Robert Blanton |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nfcnorth/post/_/id/71895/vikings-andrew-sendejo-to-start-at-safety-over-robert-blanton |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |author=Goesseling, Ben |date=September 14, 2015}}</ref>

He started in the [[2015 Minnesota Vikings|Minnesota Vikings']] season-opener at the [[2015 San Francisco 49ers|San Francisco 49ers]] and made three solo tackles and blocked a field goal in their 20–3 loss.<ref name="stats15"/> On the 49ers' opening drive, Sendejo blocked a 28-yard field goal attempt by kicker [[Phil Dawson]] and it was recovered by teammate [[Marcus Sherels]] at the Vikings' 44-yard line.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 1-2015: Minnesota Vikings @ San Francisco 49ers |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2015091401/2015/REG1/vikings@49ers |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=NFL.com |date=September 15, 2015 }}</ref> He was sidelined for the Vikings' Week 4 loss at the [[2015 Denver Broncos|Denver Broncos]] due to a knee injury. On November 8, 2015, Sendejo collected seven combined tackles, a pass deflection, and was credited with half a sack to mark the first of his career during a 21–18 overtime victory against the [[2015 St. Louis Rams|St. Louis Rams]] in Week 9. He sacked quarterback [[Nick Foles]] for an eight-yard loss with teammate [[Linval Joseph]] in the third quarter.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 9-2014: St. Louis Rams @ Minnesota Vikings |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2015110800/2015/REG9/rams@vikings |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=NFL.com |date=November 8, 2015 }}</ref> Sendejo aggravated his knee injury and was inactive for two more games (Weeks 13–14). In Week 16, he made three solo tackles, a pass deflection, and intercepted a pass by [[Eli Manning]] during a 49–17 win against the [[2015 New York Giants|New York Giants]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 16-2015: New York Giants @ Minnesota Vikings |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2015122706/2015/REG16/giants@vikings |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=NFL.com |date=December 28, 2015 }}</ref> On January 3, 2016, Sendejo collected a season-high 14 combined tackles (nine solo) in the Vikings' 20–13 win against the [[2015 Green Bay Packers|Green Bay Packers]] in Week 17.<ref name="stats15">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Andrew Sendejo (2015) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrewsendejo/2525323/gamelogs?season=2015 |access-date=June 14, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the [[2015 NFL season|2015 season]] with 74 combined tackles (58 solo), three passes defensed, and one interception in 13 games and 13 starts.<ref name="career"/> He ranked 78th among the 88 qualified safeties in 2015 from Pro Football Focus.<ref name="2016 extension"/>

The Minnesota Vikings finished the 2015 season first in the [[NFC North]] with an 11–5 record and earned a playoff berth. On January 10, 2016, Sendejo started his first career playoff game and made three solo tackles and a pass deflection during the Vikings' 10–9 loss to the [[2015 Seattle Seahawks|Seattle Seahawks]] in the NFC Wildcard Game.<ref name="stats15"/>

====2016====
On March 5, 2016, the Minnesota Vikings signed Sendejo to a four-year, $16 million contract that includes $3.95 million guaranteed.<ref name="2016 extension">{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/andrew-sendejo-agrees-to-four-year-deal-with-vikings-0ap3000000641519|title=Andrew Sendejo agrees to four-year deal with Vikings|first=Kevin|last=Patra|work=NFL.com|date=March 5, 2016|access-date=March 5, 2016}}</ref><ref name="spotrac"/>

On September 18, 2016, Sendejo collected a season-high 11 combined tackles (nine solo) during a 17–14 win against the [[2016 Green Bay Packers|Green Bay Packers]] in Week 2. In Week 5, he made six combined tackles, a pass deflection, and an interception in the Vikings' 31–13 win against the [[2016 Houston Texans|Houston Texans]]. The following game, Sendejo deflected a pass and made an interception during a 21–10 loss at the [[2016 Philadelphia Eagles|Philadelphia Eagles]] in Week 7.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Andrew Sendejo (2016) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrewsendejo/2525323/gamelogs?season=2016 |access-date=June 15, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was inactive for the Vikings' Week 8 loss at the [[2016 Chicago Bears|Chicago Bears]] after injuring his ankle the previous week.<ref name="fox"/> On December 31, 2016, the Minnesota Vikings placed Sendejo on injured reserve due to a knee injury he sustained in practice.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Place Sendejo on IR; Sign Fruechte to 53|url=http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Place-Sendejo-on-IR-Sign-Fruechte-to-53/6de89582-a01f-4803-aebd-a98d8aaccd7e|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202081554/http://www.vikings.com/news/article-1/Vikings-Place-Sendejo-on-IR-Sign-Fruechte-to-53/6de89582-a01f-4803-aebd-a98d8aaccd7e|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 2, 2017|author=Peters, Craig|website=Vikings.com|date=December 31, 2016}}</ref> Sendejo finished the [[2016 NFL season|2016 season]] with 69 combined tackles (45 solo), four pass deflections, two fumble recoveries, two interceptions, and was credited with half a sack in 14 games and 14 starts.<ref name="career"/> Sendejo earned an overall grade of 78.6 from Pro Football Focus in 2016.<ref>{{cite web |title=Grading the Graders (and Players): Vikings Defense |url=https://zonecoverage.com/2017/vikings/grading-the-graders-and-players-vikings-defense/ |access-date=June 15, 2018 |website=zonecoverage.com |author=Hasan, Arif |date=January 20, 2017}}</ref>

====2017====
Sendejo entered training camp slated as the starting strong safety. Head coach Mike Zimmer officially named Sendejo and Harrison Smith the starting safety duo to begin the 2017 regular season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Minnesota Vikings Depth Chart: 09/01/2017 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/199/MIN |access-date=June 15, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On September 24, 2017, Sendejo recorded five combined tackles, two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass attempt by quarterback [[Jameis Winston]] in the Vikings' 34–17 victory against the [[2017 Tampa Bay Buccaneers|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref name="stats17"/> The following week, he collected a season-high 11 combined tackles (five solo) during a 14–7 loss to the [[2017 Detroit Lions|Detroit Lions]] in Week 4.<ref name="stats17"/> He was inactive during a Week 6 win against the [[2017 Green Bay Packers|Green Bay Packers]] due to a [[groin]] injury.<ref name="fox"/> In Week 7, Sendejo delivered a helmet-to-helmet hit while tackling wide receiver [[Mike Wallace (American football)|Mike Wallace]] which caused Wallace to exit the game a due to a [[concussion]]. The next day, Sendejo was suspended one game for violating the league's player safety rules.<ref>{{cite web|title=Andrew Sendejo suspended one game for Wallace hit|url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000866198/article/andrew-sendejo-suspended-1-game-for-mike-wallace-hit|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171024100203/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000866198/article/andrew-sendejo-suspended-1-game-for-mike-wallace-hit|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 24, 2017|website=NFL.com|date=October 23, 2017}}</ref> On December 10, 2017, Sendejo recorded nine combined tackles, deflected a pass, and made an interception off a pass by [[Cam Newton]] in a 31–24 loss at the [[2017 Carolina Panthers|Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Andrew Sendejo (2017) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrewsendejo/2525323/gamelogs?season=2017 |access-date=June 15, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He completed the 2017 season with 80 combined tackles (54 solo), seven passes defensed, and two interceptions in 13 games and 13 starts.<ref name="career"/> [[Pro Football Focus]] gave Sendejo an overall grade of 86.8, which ranked 11th among all qualified safeties in [[2017 NFL season|2017]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Pro Football Focus: Andrew Sendejo |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/nfl/players/andrew-sendejo/6118 |access-date=June 15, 2018 |website=profootballfocus.com}}</ref>

The [[2017 Minnesota Vikings|Minnesota Vikings]] finished atop of their division with a 13–3 record and earned a first round bye. On January 10, 2018, Sendejo collected four solo tackles, deflected two passes, and made an interception during Minnesota's to 29–24 comeback victory against the [[2017 New Orleans Saints|New Orleans Saints]] in the NFC Divisional Round. He intercepted a pass attempt thrown by quarterback [[Drew Brees]] in the first quarter that was originally intended for wide receiver [[Ted Ginn Jr.]]<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 19-2017: New Orleans Saints @ Minnesota Vikings |website=[[NFL.com]] |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2018011401/2017/POST19/saints@vikings |access-date=June 15, 2018}}</ref> The following week, Sendejo collected four solo tackles as the Minnesota Vikings were routed 38–7 by the [[2017 Philadelphia Eagles|Philadelphia Eagles]] in the [[NFC Championship Game]].<ref name="stats17">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Andrew Sendejo (2017) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/andrewsendejo/2525323/gamelogs?season=2017 |access-date=June 15, 2018 | website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2018====
In 2018, Sendejo started the first five games before suffering a groin injury in Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles. He was inactive the next six games before being placed on injured reserve on November 27, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Place Safety Andrew Sendejo on the Injured Reserve|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-place-safety-andrew-sendejo-on-the-injured-reserve|website=Vikings.com|date=November 27, 2018}}</ref> On March 11, 2019, the Vikings declined the option on Sendejo's contract, making him an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-announce-roster-moves-031119|website=Vikings.com|date=March 11, 2019}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On March 18, 2019, the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] signed Sendejo to a one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McPherson |first=Chris |date=March 18, 2019 |title=Eagles agree to terms with S Andrew Sendejo |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-agree-to-terms-with-andrew-sendejo |access-date=2025-02-06 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> In week 2 against the [[Atlanta Falcons]], he recorded his second career sack on [[Matt Ryan (American football)|Matt Ryan]] in the 24–20 loss.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128124 |title=Jones scores late TD, leads Falcons past Eagles 24-20 |date=15 September 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=15 September 2019}}</ref> In week 6 against the [[Minnesota Vikings]], he recorded an interception off former teammate [[Kirk Cousins]] in the 38–20 loss.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128123 |title=Cousins, Diggs fly past Eagles in Vikings' 38-20 win |date=13 October 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=13 October 2019}}</ref> He was waived on November 5, 2019.<ref>{{cite news |author=McPherson, Chris |title=Eagles waive Andrew Sendejo |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-waive-andrew-sendejo |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |date=November 5, 2019 |access-date=November 5, 2019}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings (second stint)===
On November 6, 2019, Sendejo was claimed off waivers by the Minnesota Vikings.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Bringing Back S Andrew Sendejo|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-bringing-back-s-andrew-sendejo|author=Peters, Craig|website=Vikings.com|date=November 6, 2019}}</ref>
In Sendejo's first game back with the Vikings, he recorded a team high 7 tackles and intercepted a pass thrown by [[Brandon Allen (American football)|Brandon Allen]] in the 27–23 comeback win over the [[Denver Broncos]] in week 11.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128081 |title=Vikings overcome 20-0 deficit at half to beat Broncos 27-23 |date=November 17, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=November 17, 2019}}</ref>
In week 14 against the [[Detroit Lions]], Sendejo intercepted a pass thrown by rookie quarterback [[David Blough]] late in the fourth quarter to seal a 20–7 Vikings win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127926 |title=Defense delivers as Vikings sail past Lions 20-7 |date=December 8, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=December 8, 2019}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
On March 27, 2020, Sendejo signed a one-year contract with the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns add veteran Andrew Sendejo to growing safety room|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-add-veteran-andrew-sendejo-to-growing-safety-room|author=Gribble, Andrew|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=March 27, 2020}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the team on December 29,<ref>{{cite news |title=Browns place two on COVID-19 list |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-two-on-covid-19-list-x2927 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=December 29, 2020 |access-date=February 10, 2021}}</ref> and activated on January 7, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Browns make roster moves |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-make-roster-moves-x1464 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=January 7, 2021 |access-date=February 10, 2021}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On September 14, 2021, Sendejo was signed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Sign S Andrew Sendejo, Waive CB Chris Wilcox|url=https://www.colts.com/news/andrew-sendejo-signs-chris-wilcox-waived-sean-davis-released|website=Colts.com|date=September 14, 2021}}</ref>

([[Tempe, Arizona]]) | college = [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford]] (2012–2014) | draftyear = 2015 | draftround = 1 | draftpick = 13 | pastteams = * [[New Orleans Saints]] ({{NFL Year|2015}}–{{NFL Year|2023}}) * [[Las Vegas Raiders]] ({{NFL Year|2024}}) * [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] ({{NFL Year|2025}}) | status = | highlights = * 3× [[Pro Bowl]] ([[2019 Pro Bowl|2018]]–[[2021 Pro Bowl|2020]]) * [[Morris Trophy]] (2014) * First-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference football teams|All-Pac-12]] ([[2014 All-Pac-12 Conference football team|2014]]) * Second-team All-Pac-12 ([[2013 All-Pac-12 Conference football team|2013]]) | statseason = 2025 | statweek = 17 | statlabel1 = Games played | statvalue1 = 131 | statlabel2 = Games started | statvalue2 = 106 }} '''Andrus Jamerson Peat''' (born November 4, 1993) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[tackle (gridiron football position)|offensive tackle]]. He played the previous nine seasons for the [[New Orleans Saints]], which selected him in the first round of the [[2015 NFL draft]]. Before that, he played [[college football]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford Cardinal]]. As a high school senior, he was considered the best [[college football]] recruit by ''[[Sporting News]]''.{{cite journal |last1=McLaughlin |first1=Brian |year=2011 |title=Athletic bloodlines run deep for this big tackle |journal=Sporting News |issue=2012 Recruiting Guide |pages=52–53}} ==Early life== Peat was born in [[Mesa, Arizona]], the son of [[Todd Peat]] and Jana Peat. His father played for nine seasons in the [[National Football League]] for the [[Arizona Cardinals|St. Louis/Phoenix Cardinals]] and [[Oakland Raiders|Los Angeles Raiders]].{{cite news |author=Triplett, Mike |date=June 15, 2015 |title=Late bloomer: Saints' Andrus Peat had to wait before following dad's NFL path |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nfcsouth/post/_/id/60896/late-bloomer-saints-andrus-peat-had-to-wait-before-following-dads-nfl-path |access-date=June 20, 2020 |publisher=ESPN}}{{Cite web |title=Andrus Peat - Football 2012 |url=https://gostanford.com/sports/football/roster/player/andrus-peat |access-date=2025-12-07 |website=Stanford Cardinal - Official Athletics Website |language=en-US}} Peat attended [[Corona del Sol High School]] in [[Tempe, Arizona|Tempe]], [[Arizona]], where he was a [[Letterman (sports)|letterman]] in [[High school football|football]], [[basketball]] and [[Track and field|track]]. In basketball, he played as a [[center (basketball)|center]], leading his basketball team to win the Division 1 state championship as a senior.{{cite news |author=Newberg, Jamie |title=Andrus Peat just next in line |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/football/news/story?id=6587276 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=May 25, 2011 |access-date=December 23, 2011}} In [[track and field]], Peat competed as a [[shot putter]] and [[discus thrower]].[https://www.trackingfootball.com/players/andrus-peat-9014/ Players. Andrus Peat] Tracking Football {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129094514/https://www.trackingfootball.com/players/andrus-peat-9014/ |date=November 29, 2014 }} By May 2011, Peat received 38 scholarship offers from [[college football]] teams. {{As of|December 2011}}, [[Scout.com]] ranked him as a five-star recruit and the second-best [[offensive tackle]] in his class,{{cite web |title=Andrus Peat Profile |url=http://recruiting.scout.com/a.z?s=73&p=8&c=1&nid=4603743 |publisher=Scout.com |access-date=December 23, 2011}} [[Rivals.com]] rated him as a five-star recruit and the third-best offensive tackle in his class,{{cite web |title=Andrus Peat |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/player-Andrus-Peat-105073 |publisher=Rivals.com |access-date=December 23, 2011}} and [[ESPN]] graded him out at 83 overall and the 16th-best player in his class.{{cite web |title=Andrus Peat |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/player/_/id/116423/andrus-peat |publisher=ESPN |access-date=December 23, 2011}} He was considered the best recruit in his class by ''[[Sporting News]]''. He committed to [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford]] on February 1, 2012. He was offered scholarships from [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska]], [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State]], [[USC Trojans football|USC]], [[Arizona Wildcats football|Arizona]], [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA]], [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado]], [[LSU Tigers football|LSU]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]], [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State]], [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]], [[Washington Huskies football|Washington]], [[Kansas Jayhawks football|Kansas]], [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee]], [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn]], [[Arkansas Razorbacks football|Arkansas]], [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State]], [[Florida Gators football|Florida]], [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]], [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan]], [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas]], [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]], [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami]], and [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon]].{{Cite web |date=2012-02-01 |title=Andrus Peat announces for Stanford |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/ncfrecruiting/on-the-trail/insider/post/_/id/8938 |access-date=2024-01-31 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} ==College career== As a freshman, Peat played in 13 games and averaged 20 snaps per game.{{Cite web|url=https://gostanford.com/sports/football/roster/andrus-peat/7383|title=Andrus Peat - Football|website=Stanford University Athletics|accessdate=June 16, 2023}} He started all 14 games as a sophomore in 2013. As a junior in 2014, he won the [[Morris Trophy]] and was named an [[All-American]].{{Cite web|url=https://pac-12.com/news/2014/12/16/peat-and-orchard-named-35th-morris-trophy-winners.aspx|title=Peat and Orchard Named 35th Morris Trophy Winners {{pipe}} Pac-12|website=pac-12.com|date=December 16, 2014 |access-date=June 16, 2023}} After his junior season, Peat entered the [[2015 NFL draft]].{{Cite web |last=Lombardi |first=David |date=January 6, 2015 |title=Stanford left tackle Peat declares for draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/draft2015/story/_/id/12129592/stanford-andrus-peat-declares-draft |access-date=June 16, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} ==Professional career== At the 2015 [[NFL Combine]], commentator [[Mike Mayock]] appraised Peat's 40-yard dash, "He's got dancing feet with that lower body, it's unbelievable. '''Andrew J. Tiller''' (born March 13, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse Orange]].

==Early life==
Tiller played [[Guard (American football)|guard]] at [[Central Islip Senior High School]], where he graduated. In 2006, Tiller won Newsday's Zellner Award for being the best lineman in Suffolk County.

==College career==
Tiller played his first two seasons at [[Nassau Community College]] where he became a 2008 Junior College Gridwire All-American. He then transferred to [[Syracuse University]]. During the 2009 season, Tiller started in 3 of 10 total games in his junior year. During the 2010 season, Tiller played in all 13 games and made notable contributions to the Orange football team. He finished his senior season in 2011 starting in all 12 games. His performances while in SU earned him [[Letterman (sports)|three letters]]. While at Syracuse, Tiller was a [[Communication studies|Communications]] major.<ref>[https://cuse.com/sports/football/roster/andrew--tiller/8249 Syracuse Orange Football Profile]</ref>

==Professional career==

===New Orleans Saints (first stint)===
Tiller was selected in the sixth round, 179th overall, by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the [[2012 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/Saints-Select-G-Andrew-Tiller-in-Sixth-Round-/acd86bd4-56a2-4fbb-a366-aa9599136780|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611035037/http://www.neworleanssaints.com/news-and-events/article-1/Saints-Select-G-Andrew-Tiller-in-Sixth-Round-/acd86bd4-56a2-4fbb-a366-aa9599136780|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 11, 2015|title=Saints Select G Andrew Tiller in Sixth Round|accessdate=April 29, 2012}}</ref> He was released by the Saints on August 31, 2013.<ref>{{cite web | last=Cariello | first=Dave | title=Saints Release Andrew Tiller | website=Canal Street Chronicles|publisher=SB Nation | date=2013-08-31 | url=https://www.canalstreetchronicles.com/2013/8/31/4680578/nfl-roster-cuts-2013-saints-andrew-tiller | access-date=2025-07-13}}</ref>

===San Diego Chargers===
Tiller was signed by the [[San Diego Chargers]] to their [[practice squad]] on September 25, 2013, but was released on September 28, 2013. Tiller was re-signed to the Chargers' [[practice squad]] on October 1, 2013. On November 18, 2013, he was released by the Chargers.

===Green Bay Packers===
Tiller was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Green Bay Packers]] on November 20, 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.packersnews.com/article/20131120/PKR0101/131120029/Packers-shuffle-offensive-linemen-practice-squad?nclick_check=1 |title=Packers shuffle offensive linemen on practice squad | Packersnews | packersnews.com |access-date=November 20, 2013 |archive-date=October 18, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141018221840/http://www.packersnews.com/article/20131120/PKR0101/131120029/Packers-shuffle-offensive-linemen-practice-squad?nclick_check=1 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Tiller was released August 30, 2014. 
 
===San Francisco 49ers===
Tiller was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[San Francisco 49ers]] on October 18, 2014. He was cut by the 49ers in order for the 49ers to make their 53-man roster. He was then signed to the 49ers' practice squad on September 6, 2015. In the middle of the season, he was signed to the 53-man roster and played two games alternating snaps with [[Jordan Devey]].

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On May 10, 2017, Tiller signed with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs sign free agent guard Andrew Tiller|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/05/10/chiefs-sign-free-agent-guard-andrew-tiller/|author=Smith, Michael David|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=May 10, 2017}}</ref> He was waived on September 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs Roster Down to NFL Mandated 53|url=http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Roster-Down-to-NFL-Mandated-53/29056cc8-800b-4a3f-be18-d873f2470e6b|website=Chiefs.com|date=September 2, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180603165651/http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Roster-Down-to-NFL-Mandated-53/29056cc8-800b-4a3f-be18-d873f2470e6b|archivedate=June 3, 2018}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints (second stint)===
On January 4, 2018, Tiller signed a reserve/future contract with the Saints.<ref>{{cite web|title=Saints Sign G Andrew Tiller & DB Bradley Sylve To Futures Deals|url=http://nfltraderumors.co/saints-sign-g-andrew-tiller-db-bradley-sylve-futures-deals/|date=January 4, 2018}}</ref> He was released on September 1, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints make roster reductions to 53|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-make-roster-reductions-to-53|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=September 1, 2018}}</ref>

===Orlando Apollos===
In 2019, Tiller joined the [[Orlando Apollos]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Conner|first=Matt|url=https://arrowheadaddict.com/2019/02/06/alliance-american-football-former-chiefs-players-aaron-murray/|title=Aaron Murray, Seantavius Jones among former Chiefs in AAF|publisher=[[FanSided]]|work=Arrowhead Addict|date=February 6, 2019|accessdate=February 6, 2019}}</ref> The league ceased operations in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |last2=Wickersham |first2=Seth |date=June 13, 2019 |title=Inside the short, unhappy life of the Alliance of American Football |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26957796/inside-short-unhappy-life-alliance-american-football |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Vipers===
Tiller was selected in the 4th round in phase two in the [[2020 XFL draft]] by the [[Tampa Bay Vipers]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.xfl.com/en-US/articles/phase-2-offensive-line-draft-tracker |title=OFFENSIVE LINEMEN DRAFT TRACKER |website=XFL.com |date=October 15, 2019 |accessdate=October 16, 2019 |archive-date=October 16, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191016142541/https://www.xfl.com/en-US/articles/phase-2-offensive-line-draft-tracker |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] before the start of the regular season on February 1, 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=XFL Injured Reserve |url=https://www.xfl.com/en-US/xfl-injured-reserve |website=XFL.com |accessdate=February 6, 2020 |archive-date=February 6, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200206134624/https://www.xfl.com/en-US/xfl-injured-reserve |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was activated from injured reserve on February 28, 2020.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=XFLVipers |title=TRANSACTION ALERT |number=1233530403836833793 |date=February 28, 2020 |accessdate=February 28, 2020}}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Condotta, Bob |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |website=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 10, 2020 |accessdate=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

'''Andrew Norwell''' (born October 25, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]] and was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Carolina Panthers]] in 2014. Norwell has also played for the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] and the [[Washington Commanders]].

Norwell attended [[Anderson High School (Cincinnati, Ohio)|Anderson High School]] in [[Cincinnati, Ohio]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Ohio State University]] from 2010 to 2013. He started 39 of 50 games. During his true freshman year, Norwell was the primary backup at right tackle in 2010 and played in 11 games. He named to a Big Ten all-freshman team by Rivals.com. During his sophomore year, Norwell started 13 games and started at both the left guard and left tackle positions. He was named honorable mention all-Big Ten. During his junior season, Norwell played more downs than any player on offense with 862. The Ohio State coaches named him co-offensive lineman of the year. He helped Ohio State average 242.2 yards per game rushing, ranking 10th nationally in 2012, lead the Big Ten in scoring at 37.1 points per game, and was named first-team all-Big Ten. Norwell was named to the first-team all-Big Ten Conference for the second consecutive season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ohiostatebuckeyes.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/andrew_norwell_753549.html|title=OhioStateBuckeyes.com Andrew Norwell Bio :: The Ohio State University official athletic site :: Football|access-date=October 19, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141027035738/http://www.ohiostatebuckeyes.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/andrew_norwell_753549.html|archive-date=October 27, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He graduated in May 2014 with a degree in communications.

Despite his decorated college career, Norwell went [[undrafted free agent|undrafted]] in the [[2014 NFL draft]] and signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]] as a free agent. Norwell signed a three-year, $1.5 million contract on May 12, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers agree to terms with nine college free agents|url=http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-agree-to-terms-with-nine-college-free-agents/bbfe4c7c-4f0d-4977-9458-4e0f6f34a6ab|author=Strickland, Bryan|website=Panthers.com|date=May 12, 2014|access-date=April 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170417155431/http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-agree-to-terms-with-nine-college-free-agents/bbfe4c7c-4f0d-4977-9458-4e0f6f34a6ab|archive-date=April 17, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Norwell was inserted into the starting lineup in Week 7. Following Week 10, [[Pro Football Focus]] rated Norwell as the ninth best guard in the NFL, ahead of two other high-profile rookie guards, [[Zack Martin]] and [[Joel Bitonio]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/blog/2015/01/02/pff-preview-cardinals-panthers-wild-card-round/|title=News and Analysis for NFL and Fantasy Football - Pro Football Focus|website=www.profootballfocus.com}}</ref> His insertion into the starting lineup at left guard helped stabilize the offensive line, and over his last six games at left guard, [[Pro Football Focus]] rated Norwell as the fourth-best left guard in the NFL.<ref name="foxsports.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/carolinas/story/undrafted-norwell-quickly-morphs-into-invaluable-piece-on-panthers-o-line-052915|title=Undrafted Norwell quickly morphs into invaluable piece on Panthers' O-line - FOX Sports|date=May 29, 2015}}</ref> His emergence into the starting lineup helped the Panthers rank seventh in the NFL in rushing, including a league-leading 975 yards over the last five games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.panthers.com/team/roster/andrew-norwell/e0b5473e-b25f-41ec-a258-96cea54b2161/|title=Carolina Panthers: Andrew Norwell|access-date=May 20, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150509084600/http://www.panthers.com/team/roster/Andrew-Norwell/e0b5473e-b25f-41ec-a258-96cea54b2161|archive-date=May 9, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> He also helped the Panthers to back-to-back division titles for the first time since the formation of the [[NFC South]] division. Norwell was also among the least penalized players at the position and through the entire season, did not allow a single sack and only one quarterback hit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/blog/2015/01/22/2014-pff-all-nfc-south-team/|title=News and Analysis for NFL and Fantasy Football - Pro Football Focus|website=www.profootballfocus.com}}</ref><ref name="foxsports.com"/>

Through the first three games of the 2015 season, Norwell allowed only two quarterback pressures and one sack.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/blog/2015/09/28/no-car-grades-newton-shreds-saints/|title=News and Analysis for NFL and Fantasy Football - Pro Football Focus|website=www.profootballfocus.com}}</ref> Norwell was part of the Panthers team that played in [[Super Bowl 50]]. On March 7, 2017, the Panthers placed a second-round tender on Norwell, who was set to be a restricted free agent.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers tender Andrew Norwell|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-tender-Andrew-Norwell/068ee6b2-0001-4352-9559-8862dcaf179a|author=Henson, Max|website=Panthers.com|date=March 7, 2017}}</ref> On April 17, 2017, Norwell officially signed his tender with the Panthers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Andrew Norwell, two others sign tenders|url=http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Andrew-Norwell-two-others-sign-tenders/468ed981-c1be-4dc2-96f4-7b895589d04c|author=Strickland, Bryan|website=Panthers.com|date=April 17, 2017|access-date=April 17, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170418082055/http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Andrew-Norwell-two-others-sign-tenders/468ed981-c1be-4dc2-96f4-7b895589d04c|archive-date=April 18, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> Norwell started all 16 games at left guard, on his way to being named first-team All-Pro. He was also ranked as the third best guard in the league according to ''Pro Football Focus''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Andrew Norwell bio|url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/nfl/players/andrew-norwell/9126|website=ProFootballFocus.com}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
[[File:Andrew Norwell.png|thumb|Norwell with the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2019]]
On March 15, 2018, Norwell signed a five-year, $66.5 million contract with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] with $30 million guaranteed, which at the time made him the highest-paid guard in the league.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/guard-andrew-norwell-signs-with-jaguars-0ap3000000920814|title=Guard Andrew Norwell expected to sign with Jaguars|website=NFL.com|date=March 13, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/OFFICIAL-Norwell-signs/1f45034e-837d-4792-9c00-f939bc1c07a4|title=OFFICIAL: Norwell signs|work=Jaguars.com|date=March 15, 2018|first=John|last=Oehser|access-date=March 16, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180315173602/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/OFFICIAL-Norwell-signs/1f45034e-837d-4792-9c00-f939bc1c07a4|archive-date=March 15, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> He started the first 11 games at left guard before suffering an ankle injury in Week 12. He was placed on injured reserve on November 26, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars will put Andrew Norwell on injured reserve|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/11/26/jaguars-will-put-andrew-norwell-on-injured-reserve/|author=Alper, Josh|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=November 26, 2018}}</ref>

On November 28, 2020, Norwell was placed on injured reserve after suffering a forearm injury in Week 11.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jags LG Andrew Norwell placed on injured reserve|url=https://jaguarswire.usatoday.com/2020/11/28/jags-lg-andrew-norwell-placed-on-injured-reserve/|work=Jags Wire|publisher=USA Today|date=November 28, 2020}}</ref> On December 19, 2020, he was activated off of injured reserve. In March 2021, Norwell agreed to a contract restructuring that resulted in a pay cut and shortening the remainder of his contract to one year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jacksonville.com/story/sports/nfl/2021/03/15/jaguars-nfl-free-agency-live-updates/4700687001/|work=Jacksonville.com|title=Jaguars restructure Andrew Norwell's contract|first=John|last=Reid|date=March 15, 2021|accessdate=August 14, 2022}}</ref>

===Washington Commanders===
Norwell signed a two-year contract with [[Washington Commanders]] on March 17, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|work=Commanders.com|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-signed-g-andrew-norwell|title=Commanders signed G Andrew Norwell|date=March 17, 2022|accessdate=March 17, 2022|author=Washington Commanders Public Relations}}</ref> He was named the starting left guard in 2022, starting 16 games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Norwell 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/N/NorwAn01/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Norwell was placed on the [[physically unable to perform]] (PUP) list on May 30, 2023, due to an elbow injury, and was released on July 24, 2023.<ref>{{cite web | last=Alper | first=Josh | title=Commanders cut Cameron Dantzler, put Andrew Norwell on PUP list | website=NBC Sports | date=2023-05-30 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/commanders-cut-cameron-dantzler-put-andrew-norwell-on-pup-list | access-date=2025-03-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=2023-07-24 |title=Commanders release Andrew Norwell |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/commanders-release-andrew-norwell |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Norwell's older brother, [[Chris Norwell|Chris]], is the head football coach at [[Thomas More University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robbins |first=Adrienne |date=2015-02-19 |title=Former Ohio State football player Andrew Norwell working his way up the ranks in Carolina |url=https://www.thelantern.com/2015/02/former-ohio-state-football-player-andrew-norwell-working-his-way-up-the-ranks-in-carolina/ |access-date=2023-08-17 |website=The Lantern |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Ladelle Andrews Hamilton Jr.''' (born April 8, 1950) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] for three seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] and [[New Orleans Saints]]. He was selected by the Chiefs in the fourth round of the [[1972 NFL draft]] after playing [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]].

==Early life==
Hamilton played high school football at [[Ruston High School]] in [[Ruston, Louisiana]]. While at Ruston, he played receiver while his cousin, [[Bert Jones]], played quarterback.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/13670269/the_town_talk/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170910002750/https://www.newspapers.com/clip/13670269/the_town_talk/ | url-status=dead | archive-date=September 10, 2017 | title=A Quarterback the Fans Love | work=The Town Talk | date=November 13, 1969 | access-date=September 9, 2017 | author=Carter, Bill | pages=8}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=204809207 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170910003706/http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=204809207 | url-status=dead | archive-date=September 10, 2017 | title=In Focus: Field of Dreams | publisher=lsusports.net | agency=October 9, 2009 | access-date=September 9, 2017}}</ref>

==College career==
Hamilton played for the [[LSU Tigers football|Tigers]] at [[Louisiana State University]] from 1968 to 1971.<ref name="spr">{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andy-hamilton-1.html | title=Andy Hamilton | publisher=Sports Reference LLC | work=sports-reference.com | access-date=September 9, 2017}}</ref><ref name="fr"/> He played for LSU's freshman team in 1968.<ref name="fr">{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/221662928/?terms=%22Andy%2BHamilton%22%2BLSU | title=Bengals Smother TU Frosh | work=[[The Times (Shreveport)|The Times]] | date=November 23, 1968 | access-date=September 9, 2017 | pages=18}}</ref> Hamilton also played with Bert Jones at LSU.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/?spot=13670615 | title=Sun Bowl Notes | work=The Town Talk | date=December 19, 1971 | access-date=September 9, 2017 | pages=45}}</ref> He caught 109 passes for 2,141 yards and 18 touchdowns during his college career. He also rushed for 65 yards and 5 touchdowns.<ref name="spr"/> Hamilton set LSU career records for receptions, receiving yards, and receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.andthevalleyshook.com/2016/4/22/11487092/atvs-all-time-team-receivers | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170910010437/https://www.andthevalleyshook.com/2016/4/22/11487092/atvs-all-time-team-receivers | url-status=dead | archive-date=September 10, 2017 | title=ATVS All-Time Team: Receivers | publisher=andthevalleyshook.com | date=April 22, 2016 | access-date=September 9, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.lsusports.net/src/data/lsu/assets/docs/fb/pdf/06fbguide136-194.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=5200 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170910010438/http://www.lsusports.net/src/data/lsu/assets/docs/fb/pdf/06fbguide136-194.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=5200 | url-status=dead | archive-date=September 10, 2017 | title=Receptions/Total Offense Records | publisher=lsusports.net | access-date=September 9, 2017 | pages=138}}</ref> He tied an [[Orange Bowl]] record with 9 receptions in the [[1971 Orange Bowl]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/13671155/the_miami_news/ | title=Nebraska defense vents frustration | work=[[The Miami News]] | date=January 2, 1971 | access-date=September 9, 2017 | author=Harris, Elliott | pages=34}}</ref> He also tied an LSU record for touchdown catches in a game when he caught three in a victory against [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]] in 1971.<ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-43SPTBE2hwC&q=Andy+Hamilton+lsu+record+three+touchdowns+game+notre+dame&pg=PA91 | title=Greatest Moments in Lsu Football History | publisher=Sports Publishing LLC | author=Montet, Bud | year=2002 | pages=90–91| isbn=9781582615103 }}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Kansas City Chiefs===
Hamilton was selected by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] with the 97th pick in the [[1972 NFL draft]] and subsequently signed with the team.<ref name="A">{{cite web|url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/hami00200.html |title=ANDY HAMILTON |publisher=profootballarchives.com |access-date=November 19, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150908202133/http://www.profootballarchives.com/hami00200.html |archive-date=September 8, 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/51514482/ |title=No. 1 Draftee at White House |work=[[The Kansas City Times]] |date=February 2, 1972 |access-date=July 25, 2015 |pages=30 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150726021636/http://www.newspapers.com/newspage/51514482/ |archive-date=July 26, 2015 }}</ref> He missed the entire 1972 season due to a shoulder injury.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/13671439/the_times/ | title=On Playing a Waiting Game | work=[[The Times (Shreveport)|The Times]] | date=September 24, 1972 | access-date=September 9, 2017 | author=Robichaux, Gerry | pages=11}}</ref><ref name="Marshall">{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/217975191/?terms=andy%2Bhamilton%2Binjury%2Bchiefs | title=Chiefs' Andy Hamilton Still a 'Rookie' In Second Pro Season | work=[[The Times (Shreveport)|The Times]] | date=November 18, 1973 | access-date=September 9, 2017 | author=Marshall, Tom | pages=54}}</ref> He made his NFL debut on November 4, 1973, against the [[San Diego Chargers]]. He had missed the earlier parts of the season due to injuries.<ref name="Marshall"/> He played in five games for the Chiefs in 1973, catching 2 passes for 35 yards. He played in 10 games in 1974, catching 2 passes for 25  yards.<ref name="A"/> He was released by the Chiefs on September 16, 1975.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1893&dat=19750917&id=nO8hAAAAIBAJ&pg=6026,1678076&hl=en | title=Chiefs release Andy Hamilton | work=[[The Southeast Missourian]] | date=September 17, 1975 | agency=[[Associated Press]] | access-date=July 25, 2015}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
Hamilton played in 9 games for the [[New Orleans Saints]] during the 1975 season, catching 12 passes for 210 yards.<ref name="A"/>

== Personal Testimony in Tiger Stadium ==
In 1970, Hamilton spoke at the [[Billy Graham|Billy Graham Crusade]] in LSU's [[Tiger Stadium (Detroit)|Tiger Stadium]]. He gave witness to his Christian faith, saying: "One thing gives me more satisfaction [than winning] and that's knowing Jesus Christ is in my heart."<ref>{{Cite web|date=1970|title=1970 Billy Graham Crusade Tiger Stadium|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FP5WfdIHILw&t=216s|website=YouTube}}</ref> He was a member of the [[Fellowship of Christian Athletes]].

'''Andrew Stewart''' (born November 20, 1965) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] [[defensive end]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the fourth round of the [[1989 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Fresno City Rams|Fresno City]] and [[Cincinnati Bearcats football|Cincinnati]].<ref name="A">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchive.com/stew00400.html | title=ANDREW STEWART | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=May 10, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518072019/http://www.profootballarchives.com/stew00400.html | archive-date=2015-05-18 | url-status=dead }}</ref> He was also a member of the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], [[San Francisco 49ers]], [[Ottawa Rough Riders]], [[BC Lions]], [[Toronto Argonauts]], [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] and [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]].

==Early life and college==
Stewart attended Malverne High School in [[Malverne, New York]] and [[Uniondale High School]] in [[Uniondale, New York]].<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9NdjPXpetYoC&q=Andrew%20Stewart%20uniondale%20high&pg=PA30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181114093600/https://books.google.com/books?id=9NdjPXpetYoC&pg=PA30&lpg=PA30&dq=Andrew+Stewart+uniondale+high&source=bl&ots=yslTy2z0nY&sig=7JrKROGh6DeX-ohob84ib3i5ekw&hl=en&sa=X&redir_esc=y%23v=onepage&q=Andrew%20Stewart%20uniondale%20high&f=false |url-status=dead |archive-date=2018-11-14 |title=The Story of Two Brothers: Alexander & Andrew Stewart Former NFL Pro Football Players |publisher=Xlibris Corporation |author=[[Alex Stewart (American football)|Alexander Stewart]] |year=2009 |pages=30 | isbn=978-1-4628-1970-6 }}{{Self-published inline|certain=yes|date=January 2018}}</ref><ref name="fresno"/>

Stewart played for the [[Fresno City Rams]] of [[Fresno City College]] in 1985.<ref name="A"/><ref name="fresno">{{cite web|url=http://www.fresnocitycollege.edu/index.aspx?page=3236 |title=Rams in the Pros |publisher=fresnocitycollege.edu |accessdate=October 1, 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20161002010045/http://www.fresnocitycollege.edu/index.aspx?page=3236 |archivedate=October 2, 2016 }}</ref>

Stewart played for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats football|Cincinnati Bearcats]] of the [[University of Cincinnati]] from 1986 to 1988, recording career totals of 36 tackles for loss and sixteen sacks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gobearcats.com/sports/m-footbl/archive/tackling.html |title=Tackling Records |publisher=gobearcats.com |accessdate=October 1, 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001201132/http://www.gobearcats.com/sports/m-footbl/archive/tackling.html |archivedate=October 1, 2015 }}</ref> He set the school's single season sack record with nine in 1987.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conferenceusa.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/120101aab.html |title=UC Accepts Motor City Bowl Bid Following Win |publisher=conferenceusa.com |date=December 1, 2001 |accessdate=October 1, 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001200855/http://www.conferenceusa.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/120101aab.html |archivedate=October 1, 2015 }}</ref> He also played in the [[East–West Shrine Game]] and [[Senior Bowl]].{{citation needed|date=August 2019}}

==Professional career==

===National Football League===
Stewart was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] with the 107th pick in the [[1989 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1989 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1989/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He won the [[Maurice Bassett]] Award in 1989. The Award is given to the Browns' most outstanding rookie in training camp as voted by the local media.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://cle.247sports.com/Bolt/Shelton-is-Clevelands-top-rookie-in-camp-39101134 | title=Shelton is Cleveland's top rookie in camp | publisher=cle.247sports.com | date=September 2, 2015 | accessdate=August 13, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160131195722/http://cle.247sports.com/Bolt/Shelton-is-Clevelands-top-rookie-in-camp-39101134 | archive-date=January 31, 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref>  He played in all 16 games for the Browns during the [[1989 NFL season|1989 season]], recording three sacks.<ref name="A"/> Stewart was released by the Browns on November 28, 1990, after having spent the prior three months on injured reserve due to an [[Achilles tendon]] injury.<ref name="B">{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1991-10-02-sp-2892-story.html |title=Lost Job Blamed on Agent : NFL: Defensive end Andrew Stewart alleges that he was cut because he dumped Bruce Allen. |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=October 2, 1991 |access-date=May 10, 2015 |author1=Robbins, Danny  |author2=Almond, Elliot |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150511012135/http://articles.latimes.com/1991-10-02/sports/sp-2892_1_bruce-allen |archive-date=May 11, 2015 }}</ref> He signed with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] during the 1991 off-season. He suffered a torn knee ligament July 31, 1991, and missed the [[1991 NFL season|1991]] and [[1992 NFL season|1992 seasons]].<ref name="B"/><ref name="C">{{cite web | url=http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/story/andrew-stewart-nfl-pension-plan-wins-lawsuit-disability-benefits-062012 | title=Stewart wins suit, earns NFL pension | work=foxsports.com | date=June 20, 2012 | accessdate=September 21, 2017 | author=Perez, A.J. | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160609215553/http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/story/andrew-stewart-nfl-pension-plan-wins-lawsuit-disability-benefits-062012 | archivedate=June 9, 2016 | url-status=dead}}</ref> Stewart was signed by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] after his contract with the Bengals ran out. He suffered a right hand injury during a preseason game in 1993.<ref name="C"/> He was released by the team later in 1993.<ref name="D">{{cite web|url=http://www.ydr.com/newsfull/ci_5998662 |title=He did his time, yet he waits |publisher=ydr.com |date=May 27, 2007 |accessdate=October 2, 2015 |author =Clarke, Caryl |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002022246/http://www.ydr.com/newsfull/ci_5998662 |archivedate=October 2, 2015 }}</ref>

===Canadian Football League===
Stewart was signed with the [[Ottawa Rough Riders]] in October 1993 and played in six games for the team during the [[1993 CFL season|1993 season]].<ref name="E">{{cite web|url=http://www.cflapedia.com/Players/s/stewart_andrew.htm |title=Andrew Stewart |work=cflapedia.com |accessdate=May 10, 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150511015711/http://www.cflapedia.com/Players/s/stewart_andrew.htm |archivedate=May 11, 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/1993cflott.html | title=1993 Ottawa Rough Riders | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=October 1, 2015}}</ref> He was traded to the [[BC Lions]] in June 1994 with [[Angelo Snipes]] and [[Denny Chronopoulos]] for [[Kent Warnock]] and BC's second round pick in the [[1995 CFL draft]]. He played two seasons for the Lions, earning CFL Northern All-Star honors in 1995 when he recorded five sacks.<ref name="E"/><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/1994cflbc.html | title=1994 British Columbia Lions | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=October 1, 2015}}</ref> The Lions won the [[82nd Grey Cup]] against the [[Baltimore Football Club]] on November 27, 1994.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cfl.ca/page/his_greycup_recap1994 |title=1994 – B.C. Lions 26, Baltimore 23 |publisher=cfl.ca |accessdate=August 13, 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130819192724/http://cfl.ca/page/his_greycup_recap1994 |archivedate=August 19, 2013 }}</ref> Stewart signed with the [[Toronto Argonauts]] for the [[1996 CFL season|1996 season]] and played for the team from 1996 to 1997, compiling eight sacks in 1997.<ref name="E"/> He won back to back Grey Cups with the team in 1996 and 1997. He was traded to the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] in May 1998 and was released by the Roughriders in May 1999.<ref name="E"/><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/1998cflsas.html | title=1998 Saskatchewan Roughriders | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=October 1, 2015}}</ref> Stewart signed with the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] and played for them during the [[1999 CFL season|1999 season]].<ref name="E"/>

He retired from football in 2001.<ref name="D"/>

==Personal life==
Andrew's brother [[Alex Stewart (American football)|Alex]] also played football.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1989-04-24-sp-1761-story.html |title=Titans' Stewart Bypassed in NFL's First Five Rounds |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=April 24, 1989 |access-date=23 May 2015 |author=Norwood, Robyn |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150523160553/http://articles.latimes.com/1989-04-24/sports/sp-1761_1_nfl-s-first-five-rounds-andrew-stewart-all-star |archive-date=23 May 2015 }}</ref> In 1991, Andrew claimed that he was released by the Browns after not retaining agent Bruce Allen.<ref name="B"/> In 2012, a judge ordered the [[Bert Bell]]/[[Pete Rozelle]] NFL Player Retirement Plan to provide disability benefits to Stewart after he had initially been refused an NFL pension.<ref name="C"/> In 2016, Stewart was diagnosed with [[cancer]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Black|first1=Debra|title=Ailing athlete, who had been deported to his native Jamaica, is desperate to join wife and children in Canada and to undergo special cancer treatment.|url=https://www.thestar.com/news/immigration/2016/04/04/former-argo-fighting-to-return-to-canada-for-life-saving-cancer-treatment.html|accessdate=April 5, 2016|work=The Toronto Star|date=April 4, 2016}}</ref>

'''Andy A. Gallik''' (born September 24, 1991)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=May 12, 2015 |title=A closer look at Titans rookie Andy Gallik |url=http://www.tennessean.com/story/titansinsider/2015/05/12/titans-andy-gallik-boston-college/27170679/ |access-date=September 10, 2015 |website=The Tennessean}}</ref> is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). '''Andy Janovich''' (born May 23, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska Cornhuskers]], and was selected in the sixth round of the [[2016 NFL draft]] by the [[Denver Broncos]]. Janovich played for the Broncos, [[Cleveland Browns]], and [[Houston Texans]].

Janovich played the entirety of his rookie contract with the Broncos before he was traded to the Browns during the [[2020 NFL season|2020 NFL offseason]], where he played with the Browns for 2 seasons (Janovich had previously signed a contract extension to remain with Denver during the 2019 season). He signed with the Texans as a free agent in the [[2022 NFL season|2022 NFL offseason]] and was released prior to the start of the regular season. Janovich retired from professional football in January 2023 after not playing during the 2022 season.

==Early life==
Janovich attended and played [[high school football]] at Gretna High School.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Groke |first=Nick |date=August 6, 2016 |title=Andy Janovich is the "Hammerhead," Gary Kubiak's new, not-so-secret Broncos weapon |language=en-US |work=The Denver Post |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2016/08/05/andy-janovich-is-the-hammerhead-gary-kubiaks-new-not-so-secret-broncos-weapon/ |access-date=April 15, 2018}}</ref>

==College career==
Janovich played [[college football]] at the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]], where he spent the majority of his playing time on [[special teams]] and alternating at [[Fullback (American football)|fullback]] with C. J. Zimmerer, primarily in blocking roles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Janovich College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andy-janovich-1.html |access-date=April 15, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> His touches were few and far between until the [[2015 Nebraska Cornhuskers football team|2015 season]], where he was fourth in total rushing yards with 265 rushing yards (6.3 yards per [[Carry (gridiron football)|carry]]), 3 rushing [[touchdowns]], and two [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 58 yards; he also led the team on special teams tackles with 13 (11 solo).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Janovich 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andy-janovich-1/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=April 15, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
Janovich was one of four Nebraska Cornhuskers and one of five fullbacks to attend the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharp |first=Katie |date=February 11, 2016 |title=Here's the complete list of players invited to the 2016 NFL Combine, led by 14 from Ohio State |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2016/2/11/10967624/2016-nfl-scouting-combine-invited-players-list-ohio-state |access-date=December 23, 2017 |website=sbnation.com}}</ref> He tied [[Northwestern Wildcats football|Northwestern's]] [[Dan Vitale]] for first in the [[bench press]] among all running backs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brady |first=James |date=February 26, 2016 |title=2016 NFL Combine results: Full numbers, times for running back workouts, drills |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2016/2/26/11120566/nfl-combine-results-2016-running-back-drills-workouts |access-date=December 23, 2017 |website=SBNation.com}}</ref> On March 4, 2016, he participated at Nebraska's [[pro day]], but opted to not perform drills and only meet with team representatives and scouts.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 3, 2016 |title=Huskers Impress at Pro Day |url=http://www.huskers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=100&ATCLID=210772887 |access-date=December 23, 2017 |website=Huskers.com}}</ref> At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, Janovich was projected to be a seventh round pick or a priority undrafted free agent. He was ranked as the seventh best fullback in the draft by NFLDraftScout.com.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Janovich, DS #7 FB, Nebraska |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=105217&draftyear=2016&genpos=FB |access-date=December 23, 2017 |website=nfldraftscout.com}}</ref>
