===Denver Broncos===
====2016====
The [[Denver Broncos]] selected Janovich in the sixth round (176th overall) of the [[2016 NFL draft]]. He was the first of three fullbacks selected in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/draft.htm |access-date=April 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On May 13, 2016, the Broncos signed Janovich to a four-year, $2.5 million contract that included a [[signing bonus]] of $164,309.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Andy Janovich contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/denver-broncos/andy-janovich-19130/ |access-date=December 23, 2017 |website=spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]], he competed against veteran [[Juwan Thompson]] for the starting fullback position. He made his professional regular season debut in the Broncos' season-opener against the [[Carolina Panthers]] and scored a 28-yard touchdown on his first career carry during the 21–20 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Phillips |first=Ryan |date=September 8, 2016 |title=Andy Janovich Scores Touchdown On First NFL Carry |url=http://thebiglead.com/2016/09/08/andy-janovich-scores-touchdown-on-first-nfl-carry/ |access-date=September 13, 2016 |website=The Big Lead}}</ref> On September 25, 2016, he earned his first career start and had one carry for two-yards during a 29–17 victory over the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denver Broncos at Cincinnati Bengals – September 25th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609250cin.htm |access-date=April 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On November 30, 2016, Janovich was placed on [[injured reserve]] after having ankle surgery.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Swanson, Ben |date=November 30, 2016 |title=FB Andy Janovich headed to injured reserve |url=http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/FB-Andy-Janovich-headed-to-injured-reserve/6c571231-8c48-47f4-868e-ef17104ed639 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161201095444/http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/FB-Andy-Janovich-headed-to-injured-reserve/6c571231-8c48-47f4-868e-ef17104ed639 |archive-date=December 1, 2016 |access-date=December 1, 2016 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> He finished the {{NFL Year|2016}} season with four carries for 33 rushing yards in 11 games and five starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Janovich 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JanoAn00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=April 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2017–2019====
Janovich entered the 2017 season slated as the starting fullback under new head coach [[Vance Joseph]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Denver Broncos' depth chart: 10/01/2017 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/197/DEN |access-date=December 23, 2017 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On October 22, 2017, he had one carry for a three-yard gain and caught the first two passes of his career for 14 yards during a 21–0 loss to the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denver Broncos at Los Angeles Chargers – October 22nd, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710220sdg.htm |access-date=April 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On December 10, 2017, he scored a one-yard rushing touchdown in the Broncos' 23–0 win over the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Jets at Denver Broncos – December 10th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712100den.htm |access-date=April 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2017 season, he finished with six carries for 12 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown to go along with four receptions for 35 receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Janovich 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JanoAn00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=April 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In 2018, Janovich played all 16 games (7 starts), recording eight receptions for 112 yards with one touchdown and rushing twice for five yards. On December 30, 2018, Janovich caught his first career receiving touchdown on a 20-yard pass from quarterback [[Case Keenum]] in a loss to the Chargers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Janovich 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JanoAn00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=August 28, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On October 11, 2019, Janovich signed a three-year, $5.7 million contract extension with the Broncos.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 11, 2019 |title=Broncos sign FB Andy Janovich to 3-year, $5.7M extension |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/broncos-ink-andy-janovich-to-3-year-5-7m-extension-0ap3000001064503 |access-date=August 28, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> In Week 11, Janovich suffered a dislocated elbow injury and was ruled out for the rest of the year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Klis |first=Mike |date=November 17, 2019 |title=Broncos notes: Janovich suffers season-ending elbow injury |url=https://www.9news.com/article/sports/nfl/denver-broncos/mike-klis/broncos-notes-janovich-suffers-season-ending-elbow-injury/73-ee71cf2d-5dd3-4fc7-8f85-86e1bf869306 |access-date=August 28, 2023 |website=9News}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on November 19.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=November 19, 2019 |title=Broncos sign TE Orson Charles, place FB Andy Janovich on IR |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-te-orson-charles-place-fb-andy-janovich-on-ir |access-date=August 28, 2023 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> He appeared in seven games and recorded five receptions for 42 receiving yards and had one rushing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Janovich 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JanoAn00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=January 29, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
Janovich was traded to the [[Cleveland Browns]] on March 20, 2020, in exchange for the Browns' seventh-round pick in the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gribble |first=Andrew |date=March 20, 2020 |title=Browns acquire FB Andy Janovich in trade with Broncos |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-acquire-fb-andy-janovich-in-trade-with-broncos |access-date=August 28, 2023 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the team on November 16, 2020,<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 16, 2020 |title=Browns place FB Andy Janovich on reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-fb-andy-janovich-on-reserve-covid-19-list |access-date=December 23, 2020 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref> and activated on November 30.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Risdon |first=Jeff |date=November 30, 2020 |title=Browns activate FB Andy Janovich from reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://brownswire.usatoday.com/2020/11/30/browns-activate-fb-andy-janovich-from-reserve-covid-19-list/ |access-date=December 23, 2020 |website=Browns Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

On October 12, 2021, Janovich was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns place 3 players on IR, make other roster moves|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-3-players-on-ir-make-other-roster-moves|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=October 12, 2021|access-date=October 14, 2021|archive-date=October 12, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211012172032/https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-3-players-on-ir-make-other-roster-moves|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was activated on November 6.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spayde |first=Andrew |date=November 6, 2021 |title=Browns Activate FB Andy Janovich & C Nick Harris, Place T Jack Conklin on IR |url=https://247sports.com/nfl/cleveland-browns/article/browns-activate-fb-andy-janovich-c-nick-harris-place-t-jack-conk-174618341/ |access-date=August 28, 2023 |website=247Sports |language=en}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On March 25, 2022, Janovich signed with the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 25, 2022 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (3-25-2022) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-3-25-2022 |access-date=May 15, 2023 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> He was released on August 21, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 21, 2022 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (8-21-2022) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-8-21-2022 |access-date=May 15, 2023 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref>

Janovich announced his retirement from the NFL on January 2, 2023.

==Personal life==
Janovich is the son of Ron and Brenda Janovich. He was raised in [[Gretna, Nebraska]] and attended Gretna High School, where he starred in [[high school football|football]] and wrestling. In 2010–2011, Janovich won the Nebraska Class B 189-pound title, with a 53–0 record. In 2011–2012, Janovich won the 220-pound title, finishing at 46–0.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Janovich |url=http://www.huskers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205371865 |access-date=January 29, 2020 |website=Nebraska Cornhuskers Athletics}}</ref> Andy is of Lithuanian, German, and Irish descent.{{citation needed|date=December 2016}}
Andy married his college girlfriend, Madison McConkey, in February 2018. Madison filed for divorce July 25, 2024.

After his retirement from football, Janovich started a roofing company sporting his name, Andy Janovich Roofing, stylizing the "N" in the middle of his surname to callback to his alma mater. The company does a variety of roofing services, but is prolific in their advertising for emergency and storm damage repairs.<ref name="AJRoofing">{{cite web |last1=Janovich |first1=Andy |title=Omaha Roofing |url=https://www.andyjanovichroofingne.com/ |website=Andy Janovich Roofing |access-date=27 September 2025}}</ref>

'''Andrew Clark Provence''' (born March 8, 1961) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive lineman]] for five seasons with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the Falcons in the third round of the [[1983 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina Gamecocks]].<ref name="B">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/prov00200.html | title=ANDREW PROVENCE | website=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=June 30, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160816212556/http://www.profootballarchives.com/prov00200.html | archive-date=2016-08-16 | url-status=dead }}</ref> Provence was also a member of the [[Denver Broncos]].

==Early life==
Provence was a three-year starter at [[Benedictine Military School]] in [[Savannah, Georgia]]. He was named to the [[Savannah News-Press]] All-City team in 1977 and 1978. He also earned All-State honors in 1978. Provence was inducted into the Greater Savannah Athletic Hall of Fame in 1995.<ref name="C">{{cite web|url=http://gsahof.com/Athlete-Inductees/Inductees/Provence-Andrew |title=Provence, Andrew - Football, 1995 |website=gsahof.com |accessdate=June 30, 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701014425/http://gsahof.com/Athlete-Inductees/Inductees/Provence-Andrew |archivedate=July 1, 2016 }}</ref>

==College career==
Provence played for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina Gamecocks]] of the [[University of South Carolina]] from 1979 to 1982. He recorded ten sacks his senior year in 1982, setting the school's single season sack record. He led the Gamecocks in tackles in 1981 and 1982.<ref name="A"/> Provence was named an [[All-American]] by ''[[The Sporting News]]'' while garnering [[Associated Press]] Third-team All-American and [[Gannett News Service]] Second-team All-American accolades in 1982.<ref name="A"/><ref name=GNS>{{cite news|title=Elway, Walker head Gannett all-star squad |author=Joel Buchsbaum |newspaper=Poughkeepsie (NY) Journal |date=November 25, 1982 |page=50 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/4574852/elway_walker_head_gannett_allstar/ |via=Newspapers.com |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701015346/https://www.newspapers.com/clip/4574852/elway_walker_head_gannett_allstar/ |archivedate=July 1, 2016 }} {{Open access}}</ref> He also played in the [[Senior Bowl]] after his senior year. He recorded 401 total tackles, 35.0 tackles for loss and 26.0 sacks during his college career.<ref name="A">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/sec/post/_/id/15463/sec-2010-legends-class-announced |title=SEC 2010 Legends class announced |website=[[ESPN]] |date=October 16, 2010 |access-date=June 30, 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701004726/http://espn.go.com/blog/sec/post/_/id/15463/sec-2010-legends-class-announced |archive-date=July 1, 2016 }}</ref> Provence was named to South Carolina's Modern Era All-Time Team. He was inducted into the University of South Carolina Athletic Hall of Fame in 2010.<ref name="A"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamecocksonline.com/genrel/072910aaa.html |title=Eight To Be Inducted Into Hall of Fame |website=gamecocksonline.com |date=July 29, 2010 |accessdate=June 30, 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701004526/http://www.gamecocksonline.com/genrel/072910aaa.html |archivedate=July 1, 2016 }}</ref> He was named to the [[SEC Football Legends]] Class of 2010.<ref name="A"/>

==Professional career==
Provence was selected by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] with the 75th pick in the [[1983 NFL draft]]. He played in 69 games, starting sixteen, for the team from 1983 to 1987 and accumulated five career sacks.<ref name="B"/> He was named to the NFL All-Rookie Team by the [[Pro Football Writers of America]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/101297974/ |title=Dickerson Heads NFL Rookie Team |work=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |date=January 22, 1984 |accessdate=June 30, 2016 |pages=26 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701015156/https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/101297974/ |archivedate=July 1, 2016 }}</ref>

Provence was traded to the [[Denver Broncos]] in May 1988 for a tenth round pick in the [[1989 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://articles.philly.com/1988-05-11/sports/26259942_1_spurs-officials-angelo-drossos-lee-heads |title=Black Businessman Negotiating To Buy Spurs |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/199001280den.htm | title=SUPER BOWL XXIV | publisher=Sports Reference LLC | work=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=June 30, 2016}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Provence has worked as a mental health counselor since August 1990, months after retiring from the NFL.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lostlettermen.com/andrew-provence-works-as-therapist/ |title=Andrew Provence Works As Therapist |website=lostlettermen.com |date=May 25, 2011 |accessdate=June 30, 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701013245/http://lostlettermen.com/andrew-provence-works-as-therapist/ |archivedate=July 1, 2016 }}</ref><ref name="D"/> He also has a [[master's degree]] in professional counseling from [[Liberty University]] and is an ordained minister.<ref name="D">{{cite web|url=https://sc.edu/uofsc/posts/2016/05/aaron_provence_ion_channels.php#.W4M1ARMpCf0
|title=Channeling research success|access-date=2018-08-27|date=2016-05-20|publisher=[[University of South Carolina]]|first1=Steven|last1=Powell}}</ref><ref name="C"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://give.cru.org/0664453 |title=Andrew and Angie Provence |website=give.cru.org |accessdate=June 30, 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701014704/https://give.cru.org/0664453 |archivedate=July 1, 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.newstartcounseling.com/staff_bios/andrew-provence.html |title=Andrew Provence, MA, LPC |website=newstartcounseling.com |accessdate=June 30, 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701014726/http://www.newstartcounseling.com/staff_bios/andrew-provence.html |archivedate=July 1, 2016 }}</ref>

'''Andy Jones''' (born June 28, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Jacksonville Dolphins football|Jacksonville Dolphins]].

==Early life==
Jones attended [[East Ridge High School (Florida)|East Ridge High School]], where he played as a [[wide receiver]] and became a starter until his senior season.

After graduation he enrolled at [[Football Championship Subdivision|Division I-AA]] [[Jacksonville University]], which was a part of the non-athletic-scholarship [[Pioneer Football League]].

Jones became a starter as a sophomore, registering 31 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] (third on the team) for 457 yards (14.7-yard average per catch) and 2 [[touchdown]]s in 11 games (8 starts). The next year, he had 46 receptions (tied for the team lead) for 684 yards (led the team) and 7 [[touchdown]]s.

As a senior, he led the team with 60 receptions for 890 yards and 8 [[touchdown]]s. He finished his college career with 144 receptions for 2,120 yards and 17 [[touchdown]]s.

==Professional career==
===Dallas Cowboys===
On May 6, 2016, Jones was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Dallas Cowboys]], after a strong showing at the [[University of Florida]]'s Pro Day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cowboys Make Five Roster Moves; Announce Undrafted Free Agents|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/05/06/cowboys-make-five-roster-moves-announce-undrafted-free-agents|author=Helman, David|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=May 6, 2016|access-date=September 4, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905095847/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/05/06/cowboys-make-five-roster-moves-announce-undrafted-free-agents|archive-date=September 5, 2017}}</ref> Taking advantage that [[Dez Bryant]] was still recuperating from previous injuries, he was able to use the extra practice time to have some notable performances in [[Training camp (National Football League)|training camp]]. Unfortunately, he couldn't translate that production into the preseason games and was waived on September 3, 2016 and was signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Three Former Draft Picks Among Cowboys' Cuts; McFadden Moved To NFI|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/09/03/three-former-draft-picks-among-cowboys-cuts-mcfadden-moved-nfi|last=Helman|first=David|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=September 3, 2016|access-date=September 4, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180222185931/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/09/03/three-former-draft-picks-among-cowboys-cuts-mcfadden-moved-nfi|archive-date=February 22, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Cowboys Sign Sanchez, Release Showers; 7 Added To Practice Squad |url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/09/04/cowboys-sign-sanchez-release-showers-7-added-practice-squad |last=Helman |first=David| website=DallasCowboys.com|date=September 4, 2016|access-date=September 4, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170815024810/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/09/04/cowboys-sign-sanchez-release-showers-7-added-practice-squad|archive-date=August 15, 2017}}</ref>

After spending his entire rookie season on the practice squad, Jones signed a reserve/future contract with the Cowboys on January 17, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dallas Cowboys sign TE Rico Gathers, WR Andy Jones to futures contracts|url=https://www.all22.com/dallas-cowboys/dallas-cowboys-sign-te-rico-gathers-wr-andy-jones-futures-contracts|website=All22.com|author=Knox, Stephen|date=January 17, 2017|accessdate=September 4, 2017}}</ref> In training camp, Jones was passed on the [[depth chart]] by rookie wide receiver [[Noah Brown (American football)|Noah Brown]] and was waived on September 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cowboys Make 38 Moves, One Trade To Reach 53; Kellen Moore Released|url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-make-38-moves-one-trade-to-reach-53-kellen-moore-released-439246|author=Phillips, Rob|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=September 2, 2017}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On September 3, 2017, Jones was claimed off waivers by the [[Houston Texans]], who had scouted him when they were forced by the aftermath of [[Hurricane Harvey]] to spend three days practicing in the [[Dallas Cowboys]]' facilities.<ref>{{cite web|title=Texans claim Andy Jones, waive Akeem Hunt|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-claim-andy-jones-waive-akeem-hunt-19310705|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=September 3, 2017}}</ref> The Texans acquired him to improve their depth, after having only four receivers on the roster and knowing that [[Will Fuller]] was going to miss 3 games while recovering from a broken [[collarbone]]. He appeared in his first NFL career game against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]. He was waived on September 13 and later re-signed to the active roster on September 18.<ref>{{cite web|title=Transactions: Texans sign Evan Baylis|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/transactions-texans-sign-evan-baylis-19365946|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=September 13, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=TRANSACTIONS: Texans sign Andy Jones, Jah Reid|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/transactions-texans-sign-andy-jones-jah-reid-19403097|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=September 18, 2017}}</ref> He was passed on the depth chart by rookie [[Chris Thompson (wide receiver)|Chris Thompson]] and was released on September 27, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=TRANSACTIONS: Texans sign Chris Thompson|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/transactions-texans-sign-chris-thompson-19460274|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=September 27, 2017}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
On September 30, 2017, Jones was signed to the [[Detroit Lions]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions sign LB Thurston Armbrister to active roster and place G Zac Kerin on IR|url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-sign-LB-Thurston-Armbrister-to-active-roster-and-place-G-Zac-Kerin-on-IR/26b0a393-4376-420b-83cc-d41704ecf6a1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180206083102/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-sign-LB-Thurston-Armbrister-to-active-roster-and-place-G-Zac-Kerin-on-IR/26b0a393-4376-420b-83cc-d41704ecf6a1|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 6, 2018|website=DetroitLions.com|date=September 30, 2017}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 19, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions sign WR Andy Jones to active roster, place WR TJ Jones on IR|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-sign-wr-andy-jones-to-active-roster-place-wr-tj-jones-on-ir-20016253|website=DetroitLions.com|date=December 19, 2017}}</ref>

On September 1, 2018, Jones was placed on the [[physically unable to perform]] (PUP) list to start the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions establish 53-man roster|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-establish-53-man-roster|website=DetroitLions.com|date=September 1, 2018|access-date=September 3, 2018|archive-date=September 3, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180903215357/https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-establish-53-man-roster|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was activated off PUP on November 3, 2018, but was waived two days later and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions activate WR Andy Jones from Reserve/Physically Unable to Perform|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-activate-wr-andy-jones-from-reserve-physically-unable-to-perform|website=DetroitLions.com|date=November 3, 2018|access-date=November 3, 2018|archive-date=November 4, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181104035610/https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-activate-wr-andy-jones-from-reserve-physically-unable-to-perform|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Lions waive WR Andy Jones|url=https://lionswire.usatoday.com/2018/11/05/lions-waive-wr-andy-jones/|work=Lions Wire|publisher=USA Today|date=November 5, 2018}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on November 17, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions sign WR Andy Jones to active roster from practice squad|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-sign-wr-andy-jones-to-active-roster-from-practice-squad|website=DetroitLions.com|date=November 17, 2018}}</ref> He made his first career NFL reception on November 22 during the Thanksgiving day game against the [[Chicago Bears]]. He got his first touchdown reception on December 16 against the Bills. He appeared in 8 games with 3 starts, posting 11 receptions for 80 yards and one touchdown.

On August 31, 2019, Jones was waived/injured by the Lions and placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Detroit Lions establish 53-man roster|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/detroit-lions-establish-53-man-roster|website=DetroitLions.com|date=August 31, 2019}}</ref> He was waived from injured reserve with an injury settlement on September 2.

===Miami Dolphins===
On September 25, 2019, Jones was signed to the [[Miami Dolphins]] practice squad. He was released on November 1. On November 20, 2019, Jones was re-signed to their practice squad. He signed a [[futures contract]] with the team on December 31, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|work=MiamiDolphins.com|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-sign-eight-to-futures-contracts|title=Miami Dolphins Sign Eight To Futures Contracts|date=December 31, 2019}}</ref>

On April 18, 2020, Jones was waived by the Dolphins.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dolphins Waive Six Players |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-waive-six-players-april-18-2020 |website=MiamiDolphins.com |date=April 18, 2020 |accessdate=April 21, 2020}}</ref> Jones re-signed with the Dolphins on August 31, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dolphins Sign Andy Jones, Waive James Crawford|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-sign-andy-jones-waive-james-crawford|access-date=August 31, 2020|website=Miamidolphins.com|language=en-US}}</ref> He was waived again on September 5, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins Acquire Lynn Bowden, Make Roster Moves|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-acquire-lynn-bowden-make-roster-moves|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=September 5, 2020}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On June 1, 2021, Jones signed with the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=49ers Make a Series of Roster Moves|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-make-a-series-of-roster-moves|publisher=49ers.com|date=June 1, 2021|access-date=June 1, 2021}}</ref> On July 27, Jones was waived by San Francisco.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Announce a Series of Roster Moves ahead of the Start of Camp|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-announce-a-series-of-roster-moves-ahead-of-the-start-of-camp|website=49ers.com|date=July 27, 2021}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On August 4, 2021, Jones signed with the [[New York Giants]], but was waived four days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants sign TE Tommy Stevens, WR Andy Jones; OL Joe Looney retires|url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-sign-andy-jones-tommy-stevens-joe-looney-retires-mike-weber|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=August 4, 2021}}</ref>

'''Andrew Joseph Vollert''' (born March 15, 1995) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[tight end]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Weber State Wildcats football|Weber State]] in Ogden, Utah.<ref>[https://www.nfl.com/prospects/andrew-vollert?id=32462018-0002-5599-5790-082aae540268 NFL Combine Profile]</ref>

==College career==
Vollert played two seasons at [[San Jose State Spartans football|San Jose State]], followed by year at [[San Francisco City College]], before transferring to Weber State. He was an FCS All-American in 2016 and 2017 for the Wildcats, totaling 123 receptions for 1,613 yards and 12 touchdowns. He also played basketball at San Jose State in the 2014-15 season.

==Professional career==
===Arizona Cardinals===
Vollert signed with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] as an undrafted free agent on April 30, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals Bring In 24 Undrafted Rookies|url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Bring-In-24-Undrafted-Rookies-/f8689646-e129-4c37-8032-96da901235e1|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=April 30, 2018|access-date=May 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180502152124/https://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Cardinals-Bring-In-24-Undrafted-Rookies-/f8689646-e129-4c37-8032-96da901235e1|archive-date=May 2, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the preseason, he caught 8 of 9 targets for 55 yards.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/andrew-vollert/47198/stats?season=2018&weekGroup=PRE| title=Andrew Vollert | Indianapolis Colts TE | NFL and PFF stats }}</ref> He was waived on September 1, 2018 and was signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals Make Cuts To Reach 53-Man Roster|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-make-cuts-to-reach-53-man-roster-2018|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=September 1, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals Undergo Roster Changes, Build Practice Squad|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-undergo-roster-changes-build-practice-squad|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=September 2, 2018}}</ref> He is currently healthy and was released on October 31, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Arizona Cardinals sign Gabe Holmes, Vincent Valentine to practice squad|url=http://arizonasports.com/story/1719372/arizona-cardinals-sign-gabe-holmes-vincent-valentine-to-practice-squad/|website=ArizonaSports.com|date=October 31, 2018}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
On November 5, 2018, Vollert was signed to the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Andrew Vollert: Joins Bengals' practice squad|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/andrew-vollert-joins-bengals-practice-squad/|website=CBSSports.com|date=November 5, 2018}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Bengals on December 31, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals Sign Five To Reserve/Future Contracts|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-sign-five-to-reserve-future-contracts|website=Bengals.com|date=December 31, 2018}}</ref> The Bengals waived Vollert on May 22, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nfltraderumors.co/bengals-sign-ot-justin-evans-waive-te-andrew-vollert/|title=Bengals Sign OT Justin Evans, Waive TE Andrew Vollert|date=May 22, 2019}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
Vollert was claimed off waivers on May 23, 2019 by the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nfltraderumors.co/chargers-claim-te-andrew-vollert-off-waivers-from-bengals/|title=Chargers Claim TE Andrew Vollert Off Waivers From Bengals|author=Bouda, Nate|date=May 23, 2019}}</ref> After a strong start to camp, he suffered a torn ACL in the preseason and was placed on injured reserve on August 12, 2019. He had one catch for 25 yards before the injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Andrew Vollert will miss season with torn ACL|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/08/11/andrew-vollert-will-miss-season-with-torn-acl/|author=Williams, Charean|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=August 11, 2019}}</ref> He was waived on August 1, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Los Angeles Chargers Announce Roster Moves |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-announce-roster-moves |website=Chargers.com |date=August 1, 2020 |access-date=August 1, 2020}}</ref> His colorful release highlighted HBO's Hard Knocks Season 16 premier.

===Carolina Panthers===
On August 16, 2020, Vollert signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers sign Tommylee Lewis, Marken Michel, Andrew Vollert|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/carolina-signs-tommylee-lewis-marken-michel-andrew-vollert|author=Simmons, Myles|website=Panthers.com|date=August 16, 2020|access-date=August 16, 2020|archive-date=September 30, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200930093255/https://www.panthers.com/news/carolina-signs-tommylee-lewis-marken-michel-andrew-vollert|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was waived four days later.<ref>{{cite news |author=Weaver, Tim |title=Panthers waive tight end to make room for defensive end Jalen Jelks |url=https://pantherswire.usatoday.com/2020/08/20/panthers-waive-andrew-vollert-jalen-jelks-spot/ |website=USAToday.com |date=August 20, 2020 |access-date=August 20, 2020}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
Vollert was claimed off waivers by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] on August 21, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Colts Claim TE Andrew Vollert Off Waivers |url=https://www.colts.com/news/andrew-vollert-roster-moves-waivers-tight-end-carolina-panthers |website=Colts.com |date=August 21, 2020 |access-date=August 21, 2020}}</ref> He was waived on September 5, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Announce Final 2020 Roster Cuts|url=https://www.colts.com/news/chad-kelly-chase-mclaughlin-final-roster-cuts-2020-season|author=Walker, Andrew|website=Colts.com|date=September 5, 2020}}</ref> On December 23, 2020, Vollert re-signed with the Colts' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Practice Squad Moves: Colts Sign P Austin Rehkow & TE Andrew Vollert|url=https://www.colts.com/news/austin-rehkow-andrew-vollert-practice-squad-signing-transaction-2020|website=Colts.com|date=December 23, 2020}}</ref> On December 31, 2020, Vollert was released from the practice squad.<ref>{{cite news |title=Colts Sign T Jared Veldheer to Practice Squad |url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-t-jared-veldheer-to-practice-squad |website=Colts.com |date=December 31, 2020 |access-date=February 11, 2021}}</ref> On January 10, 2021, Vollert signed a reserve/futures contract with the Colts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Announce Two Extensions, 16 Reserve/Future Contracts|url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-announce-two-extensions-16-reserve-future-contracts|website=Colts.com|date=January 10, 2021}}</ref>

On August 31, 2021, Vollert was hit by a car and waived/injured and placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Announce Final 2021 Roster Cuts|url=https://www.colts.com/news/final-camp-roster-cuts-brett-hundley-shawn-davis-demichael-harris-will-holden|website=Colts.com|date=August 31, 2021}}</ref> He was released on September 9, 2021 with an injury settlement. Vollert announced his retirement from professional football at the conclusion of the 2021-2022 season.

'''Andrew Wylie''' (born August 19, 1994) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for the [[Washington Commanders]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Eastern Michigan Eagles football|Eastern Michigan Eagles]] and went undrafted in 2017, having short stints with the [[Indianapolis Colts]], [[Cleveland Browns]], and [[Los Angeles Chargers]] before signing with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], where he won [[Super Bowl LIV]] and [[Super Bowl LVII|LVII]].

==College career==
Wylie made 44 starts for the [[Eastern Michigan Eagles football|Eastern Michigan Eagles]] over the course of four seasons. He was named third-team All-[[Mid-American Conference]] his senior season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fishbain |first=Kevin |date=April 20, 2017 |title=PFW's NFL Draft 'late risers': Eastern Michigan OL Andrew Wylie |url=https://www.profootballweekly.com/2017/04/20/pfws-nfl-draft-late-risers-eastern-michigan-ol-andrew-wylie/axo0ca4/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181003222456/https://www.profootballweekly.com/2017/04/20/pfws-nfl-draft-late-risers-eastern-michigan-ol-andrew-wylie/axo0ca4/ |archive-date=2018-10-03 |access-date=October 3, 2018 |website=Pro Football Weekly}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
Wylie signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 15, 2017. He was released during final cuts on September 2, and was signed to the Colts' [[practice squad]] two days later. Wylie was released by the Colts on September 26.<ref name="Chiefs" />

===Cleveland Browns===
Wylie signed with the [[Cleveland Browns]]' practice squad on October 9, 2017. Wylie was released by the Browns on December 15.<ref name="Chiefs" />

===Los Angeles Chargers===
Wylie was signed to the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] practice squad on December 19, 2017, but was released eight days later.<ref name="Chiefs" />

===Kansas City Chiefs===
Wylie signed with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] the next day and was promoted to the active roster on January 8, 2018.<ref name="Chiefs">{{Cite web |title=Andrew Wylie |url=https://www.chiefs.com/team/players-roster/andrew-wylie/ |access-date=October 3, 2018 |publisher=Chiefs.com |archive-date=April 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200429153131/https://www.chiefs.com/team/players-roster/andrew-wylie/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He made his NFL debut on September 9, in the season opener against the [[2018 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Los Angeles Chargers – September 9th, 2018 – Snap counts |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201809090sdg.htm#all_vis_snap_counts |access-date=October 3, 2018 |publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> Wylie made his first career start on October 21, against the [[2018 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McDowell |first=Sam |date=October 21, 2018 |title=The Chiefs deliver several first-half messages to Bengals tough guy Vontaze Burfict |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article220422990.html |access-date=March 17, 2021 |website=The Kansas City Star}}</ref> Wylie played in all 16 games during the regular season and started the final ten games of the season after [[Laurent Duvernay-Tardif]] went down with a season-ending injury. At the end of the season the Chiefs gave Wylie the 2018 [[Kansas City Chiefs awards#Mack Lee Hill Award|Mack Lee Hill Award]] as the team's best first-year player.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldman |first=Charles |date=January 5, 2018 |title=Chiefs announce Derrick Thomas MVP, Mack Lee Hill award winners |url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2019/01/05/chiefs-mvp-rookie-of-year/ |access-date=January 5, 2018 |website=Chiefs Wire |publisher=[[USA Today]]}}</ref>

Wylie started 11 games for the Chiefs in 2019, missing five games due to injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wickliffe |first=Greg |date=February 3, 2020 |title=Andrew Wylie joins small list of Eastern Michigan Super Bowl champions |url=https://www.mlive.com/sports/ann-arbor/2020/02/andrew-wylie-joins-small-list-of-eastern-michigan-super-bowl-champions.html |access-date=February 4, 2020 |website=[[MLive.com]]}}</ref> Wylie suffered a high ankle sprain that caused him to miss the final two games of the regular season and all of the Chiefs' playoff games, including the team's win in [[Super Bowl LIV]] over the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brooks |first=Art |date=February 3, 2020 |title=Midland 'very excited' for EMU's Andrew Wylie, Super Bowl champ |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/2020/02/03/midland-very-excited-emus-andrew-wylie-super-bowl-champ/4649851002/ |access-date=February 4, 2020 |website=[[The Detroit News]]}}</ref>

Wylie signed a one-year [[exclusive-rights free agent]] contract with the Chiefs on April 20, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldman |first=Charles |date=April 20, 2020 |title=Chiefs ERFA's Andrew Wylie, Deon Yelder sign contract tenders |url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2020/04/21/kansas-city-chiefs-exclusive-rights-free-agents-andrew-wylie-deon-yelder-sign-contract-tenders/ |access-date=April 21, 2020 |website=USAToday.com}}</ref> He started 14 games at right guard during the regular season.<ref name=2021sign/> He missed the third game of the season due to a severe stomach illness and was rested for the final game of the regular season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/29997045/starting-right-guard-andrew-wylie-inactive-kansas-city-chiefs-suspected-appendicitis-source-says|title=Starting right guard Andrew Wylie inactive for Kansas City Chiefs with stomach illness|first=Adam|last=Teicher|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=September 28, 2020|access-date=May 18, 2021}}</ref> Wylie started the Chiefs' first two games of the postseason at right guard, but was shifted to right tackle for Kansas City's loss to the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in [[Super Bowl LV]] after starting tackle [[Eric Fisher (American football)|Eric Fisher]] tore his achilles in the [[AFC Championship Game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/chiefs-starting-two-backup-offensive-tackles-in-super-bowl-lv-the-skinny-on-mike-remmers-and-andrew-wylie/|title=Chiefs starting two backup offensive tackles in Super Bowl LV: The skinny on Mike Remmers and Andrew Wylie|first=Chris|last=Trapasso|website=[[CBS Sports]]|date=February 2, 2021|access-date=May 18, 2021}}</ref>

The Chiefs placed a [[restricted free agent]] tender on Wylie on March 17, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |author=Williams, Charean |title=Darious Williams only one of 26 RFAs in NFL to receive first-round tender |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/03/17/darious-williams-only-one-of-26-rfas-in-nfl-to-receive-first-round-tender/ |website=NBCSports.com |date=March 17, 2021 |access-date=March 17, 2021}}</ref> He signed the one-year contract on May 11.<ref name=2021sign>{{cite news |author=Simmons, Myles |title=Andrew Wylie signs restricted free agent tender |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/05/11/andrew-wylie-signs-restricted-free-agent-tender/ |website=NBCSports.com |date=May 11, 2021 |access-date=May 11, 2021}}</ref> He started seven games at right tackle in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2021 Kansas City Chiefs Roster & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/kan/2021_roster.htm |access-date=2023-12-21 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 17, 2022, Wylie re-signed with the Chiefs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |date=March 16, 2022 |title=Andrew Wylie returning to Chiefs on one-year deal |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/03/16/andrew-wylie-returning-to-chiefs-on-one-year-deal/ |access-date=2023-03-24 |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref> His performance in the [[2022 Kansas City Chiefs season|2022 regular season]] was criticized for his inconsistency due to surrendering 49 pressures and allowing nine sacks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/chiefs/news/kc-chiefs-set-to-lose-rt-andrew-wylie-to-washington-commanders-on-multi-year-deal|work=SI.com|title=Report: Chiefs Set to Lose Andrew Wylie to Commanders on Multi-Year Deal|
first=Jordan|last=Foote|date=March 13, 2023|accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2022/12/08/kansas-city-chiefs-andy-reid-eric-bieniemy-orlando-brown-jr-andrew-wylie-pressures-lucas-niang/|work=USAToday.com|title=Chiefs coaches show support for LT Orlando Brown Jr., RT Andrew Wylie|first=Charles|last=Goldman|date=December 8, 2022|accessdate=August 20, 2023}}</ref> Wylie started [[Super Bowl LVII]] and was part of an offensive line that gave up zero sacks against a vaunted [[Philadelphia Eagles]] defense, as the Chiefs won the game 38-35.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trotter |first=Jim  |date=February 13, 2023 |title=Chiefs' offensive linemen 'handled business' against Eagles' vaunted defensive front after week of doubts |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/chiefs-offensive-linemen-handled-business-against-eagles-vaunted-defensive-front |access-date=2023-03-24 |website=[[National Football League]]}}</ref>

'''Andy Isabella''' (born November 18, 1996) is an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[wide receiver]] for the [[Ottawa Redblacks]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[UMass Minutemen football|UMass Minutemen]],<ref name="umassbio">{{Cite web |title=No. 23 Andy Isabella |url=https://umassathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=8496 |access-date=April 27, 2019 |publisher=umassathletics.com}}</ref> and was selected by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] in the second round of the [[2019 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Isabella attended [[Mayfield High School (Ohio)|Mayfield High School]] in [[Mayfield, Ohio]].<ref name="h391">{{cite web |last=Connolly |first=John |title=UMass receiver Andy Isabella overcomes odds | website=Boston Herald | date=2017-09-09 | url=https://www.bostonherald.com/2017/09/09/umass-receiver-andy-isabella-overcomes-odds/ |access-date=2024-10-03}}</ref> Isabella ran track in high school.<ref name="r127">{{cite web |last=Noga |first=Joe |title=Mayfield sprinter Andy Isabella posts nation's top indoor track time in 60-meter dash |website=cleveland.com |date=2015-01-30 |url=https://www.cleveland.com/highschoolsports/article/mayfield-sprinter-andy-isabella-posts-nations-top-indoor-track-time-in-60-meter-dash/ |access-date=2024-10-03}}</ref> In his senior year of high school, Isabella won the state title in the 100-meter dash, beating fellow sprinter and future [[Cleveland Browns]] cornerback [[Denzel Ward]] in a close race.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lesmerises |first=Doug |date=March 2, 2019 |title=Mayfield's Andy Isabella beat Denzel Ward in high school track, can he beat his NFL combine 40 time? |url=https://www.cleveland.com/browns/2019/03/mayfields-andy-isabella-beat-denzel-ward-in-high-school-track-can-he-beat-his-nfl-combine-40-time.html |access-date=April 28, 2019 |website=cleveland.com}}</ref> He committed to the [[University of Massachusetts]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Malone |first=Daniel |date=August 20, 2015 |title=Five questions: Freshman speedster Andy Isabella looking to make impact for UMass football |url=http://www.masslive.com/umassfootball/index.ssf/2015/08/five_questions_freshman_speeds.html |access-date=2024-10-03 |website=masslive.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Podolski |first=Mark |title=How 6.72 seconds changed Mayfield grad Andy Isabella's football life |url=https://www.news-herald.com/sports/how-6-72-seconds-changed-mayfield-grad-andy-isabella-s-football-life/article_e8adeb76-2d14-5099-b19d-b4b65de64bbb.html |access-date=September 29, 2020 |work=The News-Herald }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Isabella is of Italian heritage.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Melo |first=Justin |date=February 14, 2019 |title=Meet Andy Isabella, the stud WR prospect with the huge numbers |url=https://draftwire.usatoday.com/2019/02/14/2019-nfl-draft-prospects-interviews-andy-isabella-umass/ |access-date=September 29, 2020 |work=The Draft Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

==College career==
Isabella played at UMass from 2015 to 2018. Initially recruited as a [[running back]], he converted to [[wide receiver]] his sophomore year. During his career he had 231 receptions for 3,526 yards and 30 [[touchdowns]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=No. 5 Georgia overwhelms UMass, but WR Andy Isabella holds his own |url=https://www.gazettenet.com/No-5-Georgia-overwhelms-UMass-but-WR-Andy-Isabella-holds-his-own-21626475}}</ref> As a senior, he was an [[All-American]] and was a finalist for the [[Fred Biletnikoff Award]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Podolski|first=Mark|title=Mayfield grad Andy Isabella finalist for Biletnikoff Award|url=https://www.news-herald.com/sports/mayfield-grad-andy-isabella-finalist-for-biletnikoff-award/article_4528509a-ec58-11e8-93f9-774ce16ca017.html|work=The News-Herald|access-date=December 6, 2018|archive-date=December 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181206235323/https://www.news-herald.com/sports/mayfield-grad-andy-isabella-finalist-for-biletnikoff-award/article_4528509a-ec58-11e8-93f9-774ce16ca017.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Podolski |first=Mark |title=Family rooting for Andy Isabella as Mayfield grad eyes Biletnikoff Award |url=https://www.news-herald.com/sports/family-rooting-for-andy-isabella-as-mayfield-grad-eyes-biletnikoff/article_694b5fbc-f8a6-11e8-9ccf-37e5ba596639.html |work=The News-Herald |access-date=December 6, 2018 |archive-date=December 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181206235133/https://www.news-herald.com/sports/family-rooting-for-andy-isabella-as-mayfield-grad-eyes-biletnikoff/article_694b5fbc-f8a6-11e8-9ccf-37e5ba596639.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2018, he led the country in receiving yards per game (141.5) and was named to the [[2018 College Football All-America Team]]. Isabella was [[Pro Football Focus]]'s highest rated wide receiver in college football, posting a season grade of 93.2.<ref name="o999">{{cite web |last=Gayle |first=Austin |title=Andy Isabella is much more than a slot receiver, can ‘do it all’ |work=PFF |date=2019-02-20 |url=https://www.pff.com/news/draft-andy-isabella-is-much-more-than-a-slot-receiver-can-do-it-all |access-date=2024-12-27}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
Isabella was drafted by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] with the 62nd overall pick in the second round of the draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2019/draft.htm |access-date=April 5, 2020 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> The Cardinals acquired this selection in a trade that sent [[Josh Rosen]] to the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vautour |first=Matt |date=April 27, 2019 |title=NFL Draft 2019: UMass' Andy Isabella drafted by Arizona Cardinals in second round |url=https://www.masslive.com/patriots/2019/04/nfl-draft-2019-umass-andy-isabella-drafted-by-arizona-cardinals-in-second-round.html |access-date=April 27, 2019 |website=masslive.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=April 26, 2019 |title=Josh Rosen Traded To Dolphins; Cardinals Take Andy Isabella |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/josh-rosen-traded-to-dolphins-for-second-round-pick |website=AZCardinals.com}}</ref> In Week 9 against the [[San Francisco 49ers]], Isabella caught one pass for an 88-yard [[touchdown]] in the 28-25 loss. This was Isabella's first career receiving touchdown in the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 31, 2019 |title=Garoppolo throws 4 TD passes, 49ers beat Cardinals 28-25 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127908 |access-date=October 31, 2019 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> He finished his rookie season with nine receptions for 189 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Isabella 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/I/IsabAn00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=September 29, 2020 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

In Week 3 of the 2020 season, Isabella recorded four receptions for 47 receiving yards and two touchdowns in the 26–23 loss to the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Lions at Arizona Cardinals - September 27th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009270crd.htm |access-date=September 29, 2020 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

Isabella entered the 2021 season sixth on the Cardinals wide receiver depth chart, and only had one catch the entire season and was inactive for half the season.

On October 4, 2022, the Cardinals waived Isabella.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=October 4, 2022 |title=Cardinals Release Andy Isabella; Sign Center Billy Price |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-move-on-from-andy-isabella-sign-center-billy-price |access-date=October 4, 2022 |website=www.azcardinals.com}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
On October 10, 2022, Isabella signed with the [[practice squad]] of the [[Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Andy Isabella Officially Signed to Ravens Practice Squad|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/andy-isabella-signing-ravens-practice-squad|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=October 10, 2022}}</ref> On December 31, Isabella was elevated to Baltimore's active roster for their Week 17 game against the [[2022 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]]. On January 2, 2023, Isabella was placed back on Baltimore's practice squad after a thigh injury in the game. On January 14, Isabella was elevated to Baltimore's active roster again for their playoff game against the [[2022 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]]. 

Isabella signed a reserve/future contract with Baltimore on January 19, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Comeaux |first=Jonathan |date=January 19, 2023 |title=Ravens Sign WR Andy Isabella to Futures Deal |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/ravens-sign-wr-andy-isabella-to-futures-deal/ |access-date=May 18, 2023 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co}}</ref> He was released by the Ravens on July 25.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mink |first=Ryan |date=July 25, 2023 |title=Ravens Bring Back Wide Receiver Makai Polk |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/makai-polk-ravens-sign-waivers-wide-receiver-giants |access-date=2024-10-03 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref>

He signed a reserve/future contract with Buffalo on January 22, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=White |first=Alec |date=January 22, 2024 |title=Bills sign 11 players to Reserve/Futures contracts |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-sign-11-players-to-reserve-futures-contracts |access-date=2024-10-03 |website=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref> Isabella was released by the Bills on August 27.<ref>{{Cite web |last=White |first=Alec |date=August 27, 2024 |title=Buffalo Bills made these moves to get to initial 53-man roster {{!}} 2024 |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/buffalo-bills-made-these-moves-to-get-to-initial-53-man-roster |access-date=2024-10-03 |website=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref>

'''Andrew Van Ginkel''' (born July 1, 1995) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Minnesota Vikings]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[South Dakota Coyotes]] before transferring to the [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin Badgers]]. Van Ginkel was selected by the [[Miami Dolphins]] in the fifth round of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Galloway |first=Jason |date=November 16, 2018 |title=With ankle injury behind him, Badgers outside linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel ready to show what he's capable of over season's final stretch |url=https://madison.com/wsj/sports/college/football/with-ankle-injury-behind-him-badgers-outside-linebacker-andrew-van/article_0f19882b-4944-5ede-8216-d80dc363b85a.html |access-date=September 4, 2019 |website=[[Wisconsin State Journal]] |publisher=[[Lee Enterprises]]}}</ref>

==Early life==
Van Ginkel attended Rock Valley Community High School in [[Rock Valley, Iowa]], where he played [[high school football|football]] for the Nighthawks, a consolidated team shared with [[Boyden–Hull High School]], as a quarterback and defensive back.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Siebring |first=Owen |date=April 30, 2019 |title=BHRV product Van Ginkel realizes NFL dream |publisher=KMEG |url=https://siouxlandnews.com/sports/content/bhrv-product-van-ginkel-realizes-nfl-dream |access-date=April 5, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=March 10, 2020 |title=From a Nighthawk to a Dolphin and back to fans |work=Sioux County Index Reporter |url=http://siouxcountyindex.com/from-a-nighthawk-to-a-dolphin-and-back-to-fans/ |access-date=March 17, 2020}}</ref> He did not participate in recruiting camps following his senior year of high school football, and did not attract attention from many large schools.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Galloway |first=Jason |date=November 16, 2018 |title=With ankle injury behind him, Badgers outside linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel ready to show what he's capable of over season's final stretch |work=Wisconsin State Journal |url=https://madison.com/wsj/sports/college/football/with-ankle-injury-behind-him-badgers-outside-linebacker-andrew-van/article_0f19882b-4944-5ede-8216-d80dc363b85a.html |access-date=April 5, 2020}}</ref> 

==College career==
Van Ginkel began his college career at the [[University of South Dakota]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=February 13, 2014 |title=Van Ginkel Signs With USD Football |work=Yankton Daily Press and Dakotan |url=https://www.yankton.net/sports/article_dddfd04a-9539-11e3-9d63-001a4bcf887a.html |access-date=April 5, 2020}}</ref> where he played [[defensive end]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Feldman |first=Mark |date=November 16, 2018 |title=UW football: Linebacker Van Ginkel ready to end career with a flourish |work=The Journal Times |url=https://journaltimes.com/uw-football-linebacker-van-ginkel-ready-to-end-career-with/article_d5edbc8b-cae7-53d0-b0bf-ea015c66b964.html |access-date=April 5, 2020}}</ref>  He redshirted, then played for one season, earning first-team all [[Missouri Valley Football Conference]] honors as a freshman. Van Ginkel then transferred to [[Iowa Western Community College]] after head coach [[Joe Glenn (American football)|Joe Glenn]] retired.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cowley |first=Jason |date=January 11, 2016 |title=Van Ginkel transferring from USD to Iowa Western |work=Sioux City Journal |url=https://siouxcityjournal.com/sports/football/van-ginkel-transferring-from-usd-to-iowa-western/article_929322c9-a34f-5ee3-ae56-073be59f6421.html |access-date=April 5, 2020}}</ref> At Iowa Western, Van Ginkel continued to play defensive end.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Potrykus |first=Jeff |date=December 23, 2018 |title=UW staff believes T.J. Edwards, Ryan Connelly and Andrew Van Ginkel have NFL potential |work=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/uw/2018/12/23/uw-staff-believes-edwards-connelly-and-van-ginkel-have-nfl-potential/2393585002/ |access-date=April 5, 2020}}</ref> He transferred to the [[University of Wisconsin]] and played [[outside linebacker]] for two seasons.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Temple |first=Jesse |date=February 13, 2017 |title=Andrew Van Ginkel a rare junior college find for Wisconsin |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/ncfnation/post/_/id/136668/andrew-van-ginkel-a-rare-junior-college-find-for-wisconsin |access-date=April 5, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Polzin |first=Jim |date=August 23, 2018 |title=Wisconsin outside linebackers Zack Baun, Andrew Van Ginkel set the bar high |work=Wisconsin State Journal |url=https://madison.com/wsj/sports/college/football/wisconsin-outside-linebackers-zack-baun-andrew-van-ginkel-set-the/article_b04499b2-154c-51d1-904c-1a39d42e8313.html |access-date=April 5, 2020}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
Van Ginkel was drafted by the [[Miami Dolphins]] in the fifth round, 151st overall, of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dolney |first=Kevin |date=April 27, 2019 |title=Miami Dolphins draft results 2019: Andrew Van Ginkel selected in fifth round |url=https://www.thephinsider.com/2019/4/27/18520178/miami-dolphins-draft-results-2019-andrew-van-ginkel-selected-in-fifth-round |access-date=September 4, 2019 |website=[[SB Nation]] |publisher=[[Vox Media]]}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on September 6, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 6, 2019 |title=Dolphins Sign J'Marcus Webb, Place Andrew Van Ginkel On IR |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-sign-j-marcus-webb-place-andrew-van-ginkel-on-ir |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref> He was designated for return from injured reserve on November 13, 2019, and began practicing with the team again.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Poupart |first=Alan |date=November 13, 2019 |title=Andrew Van Ginkel Returns To Practice On Wednesday |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/andrew-van-ginkel-returns-to-practice-on-wednesday |access-date=November 13, 2019 |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref> He was activated on November 20, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 20, 2019 |title=Dolphins Sign Adrian Colbert, Activate Andrew Van Ginkel, Promote Gerald Willis |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-sign-adrian-colbert-activate-andrew-van-ginkel-promote-gerald-willis |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref> On November 1, 2020, against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Van Ginkel recovered a [[fumble]] lost by [[Jared Goff]] and returned it for a 78-yard [[touchdown]] during the 28–17 win. This was the second longest fumble return in Dolphins' team history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Rams at Miami Dolphins – November 1st, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202011010mia.htm |access-date=November 6, 2020 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>
In Week 11 against the [[Denver Broncos]], Van Ginkel forced a fumble on [[running back]] [[Melvin Gordon]] at the goal line which was recovered by the Dolphins during the 20–13 loss.<ref>{{cite web |title=Miami Dolphins at Denver Broncos - November 22nd, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202011220den.htm |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |access-date=28 November 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

On March 23, 2023, Van Ginkel re-signed with the Dolphins on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-re-sign-andrew-van-ginkel|title=Miami Dolphins Re-Sign Andrew Van Ginkel|work=MiamiDolphins.com|date=March 23, 2023|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> On January 9, 2024, the Dolphins placed him on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-make-roster-moves-1-9-24|work=MiamiDolphins.com|title=Miami Dolphins Make Roster Moves|date=January 9, 2024|accessdate=January 10, 2024}}</ref>

Jonathan Greenard, Blake Cashman & Andrew Van Ginkel | website=Vikings.com | date=2024-03-13 | url=https://www.vikings.com/news/greenard-cashman-van-ginkel-agree-to-terms-2024 | access-date=2025-01-18}}</ref> In his first game with the team on September 8 against the [[New York Giants]], he recorded a sack and an interception, joining [[Kevin Williams (defensive tackle)|Kevin Williams]] and [[Harrison Smith]] as the third Vikings player since 2000 to do both in the first game of a season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Craig |date=September 8, 2024 |title=Vikings at Giants Game Observations: Darnold to Jefferson Keys 99-Yard Drive, Defense Dominant |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-giants-justin-jefferson-sam-darnold-defense-dominant '''Andrew Ken Thomas''' (born January 22, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]] for the [[New York Giants]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]] and was selected by the Giants fourth overall in the [[2020 NFL draft]].

== Early life ==
Thomas attended [[Pace Academy]] in [[Atlanta]].<ref name="R&B">{{Cite web |last=Russo |first=Kelsey |date=October 11, 2018 |title=Don't doubt Thomas: Andrew Thomas battles through position change and injury |url=https://www.redandblack.com/sports/football/don-t-doubt-thomas-andrew-thomas-battles-through-position-change/article_a4f0c25c-cce9-11e8-a600-b717b59082e9.html |access-date=May 7, 2019 |website=The Red & Black}}</ref> Following his high school career, Thomas played at the [[All-American Bowl (high school football)|Army All-American Game]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alexander |first=Wilson |date=January 7, 2018 |title=Georgia's Andrew Thomas ready for final test of freshman season in national championship |url=https://www.macon.com/sports/college/university-of-georgia/bulldogs-beat/uga-football/article193427204.html |access-date=May 8, 2019 |website=[[The Telegraph (Macon)|The Telegraph]]}}</ref> He committed to [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia]] on July 10, 2016,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zucker |first=Joseph |date=July 10, 2016 |title=Andrew Thomas to Georgia: Bulldogs Land 4-Star OT Prospect |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2633811-andrew-thomas-to-georgia-bulldogs-land-4-star-ot-prospect |access-date=May 8, 2019 |website=[[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref> choosing the Bulldogs over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]], [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn]], [[Florida Gators football|Florida]] and others.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Thomas, 2017 Offensive Tackle |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2017/andrew-thomas-3106#school-interests |access-date=May 8, 2019 |website=[[Rivals.com]]}}</ref>

== College career ==
Thomas started every game at right tackle his true freshman season, earning him a Freshman [[All-American]] accolade after the conclusion of the season.<ref name="Anchor">{{Cite web |last=Weiszer |first=Mark |date=March 23, 2019 |title=Andrew Thomas: All-American anchor of Georgia offensive line |url=https://www.savannahnow.com/sports/20190323/andrew-thomas-all-american-anchor-of-georgia-offensive-line |access-date=May 7, 2019 |website=Savannah Now}}</ref> Thomas switched to left tackle for his sophomore season. He injured his left ankle playing [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina]], and didn't play the following game against [[Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders football|Middle Tennessee]]. During the next two games, Thomas worked his way back to full participation,<ref name="R&B" /> though he was forced to wear a brace after re-injuring the ankle later in the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Griffith |first=Mike |date=April 6, 2019 |title=All business: Georgia offensive tackle Andrew Thomas leads the way |url=https://www.dawgnation.com/football/georgia-uga-thomas-scrimmage-kirby-smart |access-date=May 8, 2019 |website=DawgNation}}</ref>  After helping to pave the way for 331 rushing yards against [[Kentucky wildcats football|Kentucky]], Thomas was named the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) offensive lineman of the week.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Soderstrom, Alex |date=November 5, 2018 |title=D'Andre Swift and Andrew Thomas awarded SEC player of the week honors |url=https://www.redandblack.com/sports/football/d-andre-swift-and-andrew-thomas-awarded-sec-player-of/article_6d83daf0-e11d-11e8-bd15-db99557099f5.html |access-date=May 4, 2019 |website=The Red & Black}}</ref> He was named a first-team All American and to the first-team All-SEC after the season.<ref name="Anchor" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 27, 2018 |title=2018 All-SEC Football Team announced |url=https://www.saturdaydownsouth.com/sec-football/2018-all-sec-football-team-announced/ |access-date=May 4, 2019 |website=Saturday Down South}}</ref>

Thomas was also invited to the [[NCAA]] Elite Football Synopsium in the winter following his sophomore season; the program helps athletes prepare for the transition from college to the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vitale |first=Joe |date=March 9, 2019 |title=Georgia juniors Jake Fromm and Andrew Thomas get a taste of NFL life |url=https://ugawire.usatoday.com/2019/03/09/uga-football-juniors-jake-fromm-and-andrew-thomas-get-a-taste-of-nfl-combine/ |access-date=May 7, 2019 |website=[[USA Today]]}}</ref> Before his junior season, Thomas projected out as a potential first-round pick in the 2020 [[NFL draft]] if he chose to leave Georgia after his junior year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trapasso |first=Chris |date=May 6, 2019 |title=2020 NFL Mock Draft: Bengals take Justin Herbert, three WRs land in top 10 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/news/2020-nfl-mock-draft-bengals-take-justin-herbert-three-wrs-land-in-top-10/ |access-date=May 8, 2019 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> On December 17, 2019, Thomas announced that he would forgo his senior year and enter the [[2020 NFL draft]], thus also skipping the [[2020 Sugar Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kercheval |first=Ben |date=December 17, 2019 |title=2020 NFL Draft: Georgia OL Andrew Thomas, a potential top-five pick, to forgo senior season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/2020-nfl-draft-georgia-ol-andrew-thomas-a-potential-top-five-pick-to-forgo-senior-season/ |access-date=December 22, 2019 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref>

Thomas was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the first round (4th overall) of the 2020 NFL draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lombardo |first=Matt |date=April 23, 2020 |title=NFL Draft 2020: Giants take Georgia OT Andrew Thomas No. 4 {{!}} Instant analysis as Dave Gettleman bags top lineman |url=https://www.nj.com/giants/2020/04/nfl-draft-2020-giants-take-georgia-ot-andrew-thomas-no-4-instant-analysis-as-dave-gettleman-bags-top-lineman.html |access-date=April 23, 2020 |website=NJ.com}}</ref>

Thomas played left tackle for the first five weeks of his rookie season. Thomas was relieved of duties by [[Matt Peart]] during their Week 6 match against Washington because he arrived late for a team meeting.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maya |first=Adam |date=October 18, 2020 |title=Giants sit first-round OT Andrew Thomas for being late to team meeting |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/giants-sit-first-round-ot-andrew-thomas-for-being-late-to-team-meeting |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He ended up starting the remainder of the season at left tackle.

Thomas entered the 2021 season as the Giants starting left tackle. He suffered an ankle injury in Week 6 and was placed on [[injured reserve]] on October 19, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=October 19, 2021 |title=Andrew Thomas, CJ Board placed on injured reserve |url=https://www.giants.com/news/andrew-thomas-cj-board-injured-reserve-benardrick-mckinney-practice-squad-roster |access-date=May 31, 2023 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> On November 22, Thomas was activated from injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=November 22, 2021 |title=OT Andrew Thomas activated ahead of MNF |url=https://www.giants.com/news/andrew-thomas-trent-harris-pharoh-cooper-roster-tampa-bay-buccaneers |access-date=May 31, 2023 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> The same day, Thomas scored his first career touchdown, a two-yard reception, against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the Giants' Week 11 game. In February 2022, Thomas underwent surgery to repair the same left ankle that he had injured earlier in the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Benton |first=Dan |date=February 17, 2022 |title=Giants' Andrew Thomas underwent surgery to repair left ankle |url=https://giantswire.usatoday.com/2022/02/17/new-york-giants-andrew-thomas-underwent-surgery-repair-left-ankle/ |access-date=May 31, 2023 |website=Giants Wire}}</ref>

On July 26, 2023, Thomas signed a five–year, $117.5 million contract extension with the Giants.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salomone |first=Dan |date=July 26, 2023 |title=Giants sign left tackle Andrew Thomas to extension |url=https://www.giants.com/news/andrew-thomas-contract-extension-left-tackle-georgia-bulldogs-daniel-jones-2023 |access-date=July 26, 2023 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> The deal included $67 million guaranteed at signing and set a new NFL record for an offensive lineman.<ref name="t511">{{cite web | last=Raanan | first=Jordan | title=Giants sign star LT Thomas to record extension | website=ESPN.com | date=2023-07-26 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/38074146/giants-andrew-thomas-signs-record-setting-5-year-extension | access-date=2024-08-13}}</ref>

On October 15, 2024, Thomas underwent successful surgery to repair a [[Lisfranc injury]] in his foot suffered during the Giants' week 6 matchup against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]]. As a result, he missed the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/giants-lt-andrew-thomas-likely-to-miss-rest-of-season-after-lisfranc-surgery |title=Giants LT Andrew Thomas likely to miss rest of season after Lisfranc surgery |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=October 16, 2024 |access-date=October 16, 2024 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Thomas entered the 2025 season as one of New York's starting tackles, recovering one fumble across 13 appearances. On December 27, 2025, Thomas was placed on season-ending injured reserve due to a hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Giants put Andrew Thomas, John Michael Schmitz on IR|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/giants-put-andrew-thomas-john-michael-schmitz-on-ir|access-date=January 20, 2026|website=nbcsports.com|language=en}}</ref>

'''Andrew Wingard''' (born December 5, 1996), nicknamed "'''Dewey'''", is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for the [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  He played [[college football]] for the [[Wyoming Cowboys football|Wyoming Cowboys]]. He was signed as an undrafted free agent by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] after the [[2019 NFL draft]].

== College career ==
Wingard played [[college football]] at [[Wyoming Cowboys football|Wyoming]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Heilman |first=Phillip |date=July 31, 2019 |title=Long-haired adrenaline junkie (and undrafted safety) Andrew Wingard trying to leave mark on Jaguars |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1107561/2019/07/31/long-haired-adrenaline-junkie-and-undrafted-safety-andrew-wingard-trying-to-leave-mark-on-jaguars/ |access-date=September 2, 2019 |website=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref> Between [[2015 Wyoming Cowboys football team|2015]] and [[2018 Wyoming Cowboys football team|2018]], Wingard totaled 454 [[tackle move|tackles]], the second most in program history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Harvey |first=Demetrius |date=August 11, 2019 |title=Jaguars safety Andrew Wingard: "I wouldn't be here if I wasn't determined" |url=https://www.lockedonjaguars.com/jaguars/jaguars-safety-andrew-wingard-determined/ |access-date=September 2, 2019 |website=Locked On Jaguars |language=en-US}}</ref> He finished his college career tied for most tackles all-time in the [[Mountain West Conference]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Potter |first=Davis |date=March 4, 2019 |title=Wyoming draft prospect Andrew Wingard posts solid numbers at NFL combine |url=https://trib.com/sports/college/wyoming/football/wyoming-draft-prospect-andrew-wingard-posts-solid-numbers-at-nfl/article_c98677bf-13bb-50c1-af74-dfaf9af4cc95.html |access-date=September 2, 2019 |website=[[Casper Star-Tribune]] |publisher=[[Lee Enterprises]] |language=en}}</ref>
