===Jacksonville Jaguars===
====2019 season====
Wingard went undrafted in the [[2019 NFL draft]]. On April 29, 2019, the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] signed Wingard to a three-year, $1.76 million contract that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $5,000.<ref>{{Cite web |last=[[RotoWire]] |date=April 29, 2019 |title=Jaguars' Andrew Wingard: Joins Jacksonville |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/jaguars-andrew-wingard-joins-jacksonville/ |access-date=September 2, 2019 |website=[[CBS Sports]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Andrew Wingard contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/jacksonville-jaguars/andrew-wingard-29463/#:~:text=Current%20Contract,dead%20cap%20value%20of%20%241%2C668. |access-date=October 2, 2021 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

On August 31, 2019, Wingard made the Jaguars final 53-man roster.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kurland |first=Jon |date=August 31, 2019 |title=Jaguars make final cuts, trim roster to 53 |url=https://www.bigcatcountry.com/2019/8/31/20842310/jacksonville-jaguars-cut-roster-moves-53-players |access-date=September 2, 2019 |website=[[SB Nation]] |publisher=[[Vox Media]]}}</ref> In week 13 against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], Wingard recorded a strip sack on [[Jameis Winston]] that he recovered in the 28–11 loss. This was Wingard's first career sack in the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 1, 2019 |title=Bucs turn Foles' turnovers into touchdowns, beat Jags 28-11 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128063 |access-date=December 1, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

====2020 season====
Wingard was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the Jaguars on August 2, 2020,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Oehser, John |date=August 2, 2020 |title=Transactions: Minshew, four others added to reserve/COVID-19 list |work=Jaguars.com |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/transactions-minshew-four-others-added-to-reserve-covid-19-list |access-date=August 2, 2020}}</ref> and was activated from the list two days later.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Oehser, John |date=August 4, 2020 |title=Transactions: Minshew, Hayden moved to active roster |work=Jaguars.com |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/transactions-minshew-hayden-moved-to-active-roster |access-date=August 4, 2020}}</ref> In Week 1 of the 2020 season against the [[Indianapolis Colts]], Wingard recorded his first career interception off a pass thrown by [[Philip Rivers]] during the 27–20 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars - September 13th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009130jax.htm |access-date=September 17, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on October 12, 2020, with an abdominal strain.<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 12, 2020 |title=Jaguars' Andrew Wingard: Moves to injured reserve |work=CBSSports.com |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/jaguars-andrew-wingard-moves-to-injured-reserve/ |access-date=October 29, 2020}}</ref> He was activated on November 14, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 14, 2020 |title=Jaguars Make Roster Moves and Announce Updates for Tomorrow's Game |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-make-roster-moves-and-announce-updates-for-tomorrow-s-game |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref>
In Week 17 against the Indianapolis Colts, Wingard recorded his second career interception off a pass thrown by Philip Rivers during the 28–14 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Indianapolis Colts - January 3rd, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101030clt.htm |access-date=January 7, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2021 season====
In the 2021 season, Wingard had one sack, 88 tackles, one interception, and one pass defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Wingard 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WingAn01/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2022 season====
On March 15, 2022, the Jaguars placed a restricted free agent tender on Wingard.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sanchez |first=Carlos |date=March 14, 2022 |title=Jaguars tender Andrew Wingard but should not keep him in starting lineup |url=https://blackandteal.com/2022/03/14/jaguars-tender-andrew-wingard-starter/ |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=Black and Teal |language=en-US}}</ref> He appeared in all 17 games and started three. He recorded 37 total tackles, one interception, one pass defended, and one forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Wingard 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WingAn01/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2023-11-06 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2023 season====
On March 15, 2023, Wingard signed a three-year, $9.6 million contract extension with the Jaguars.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 15, 2023 |title=Official: Wingard agrees to terms |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/official-wingard-agrees-to-terms |access-date=2023-11-06 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> He caught an interception against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in Week 8.<ref name="t374">{{cite web | last=Stites | first=Adam | title=Watch: Jaguars celebrate interception vs Steelers with Terrible Towels | website=Jaguars Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2023-10-29 | url=https://jaguarswire.usatoday.com/2023/10/29/jaguars-andrew-wingard-interception-terrible-towel/ | access-date=2024-10-14}}</ref> In the 2023 season, Wingard had 45 tackles, one interception, two passes defended, and one forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Wingard 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WingAn01/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2024 season====
On August 27, 2024, Wingard was placed on injured reserve to begin the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 27, 2024 |title=Roster Moves: Jacksonville Jaguars Make The Following Roster Moves Hours Before 2024 Roster Deadline |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-jacksonville-jaguars-make-the-following-roster-moves-hours-before-2024-roster-deadline |access-date=2024-10-14 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> He was activated on November 9.<ref name="c123">{{cite web | last=Goodall | first=Zach | title=Jaguars activate S Andrew Wingard from injured reserve | website=Jaguars Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2024-11-09 | url=https://jaguarswire.usatoday.com/2024/11/09/jacksonville-jaguars-activate-andrew-wingard-injured-reserve/ | access-date=2024-12-27}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On March 11, 2026, Wingard signed a one-year, $3 million contract with the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Urban |first1=Darren |title=More Expected Additions In Andrew Wingard, Casey Kreiter |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/more-expected-additions-in-andrew-wingard-casey-kreiter |website=azcardinals.com |access-date=12 March 2026}}</ref>

'''Andrew Stueber''' (born July 1, 1999) is an American professional [[American football]] [[tackle (gridiron football position)|offensive tackle]] for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]], receiving second-team [[All-American]] recognition by the [[American Football Coaches Association|AFCA]] in 2021. Stueber was selected by the [[New England Patriots]] in the seventh round of the [[2022 NFL draft]].

==College career==

===New England Patriots===
Stueber was selected by the [[New England Patriots]] in the seventh round (245th overall) of the [[2022 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cohen |first=Michael |date=April 30, 2022 |title=NFL draft: Michigan football OL Andrew Stueber picked by New England Patriots in Round 7 |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2022/04/30/michigan-football-andrew-steuber-nfl-draft/9545900002/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220430223601/https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2022/04/30/michigan-football-andrew-steuber-nfl-draft/9545900002/ |archive-date=April 30, 2022 |access-date=April 30, 2022 |newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]]}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve/non-football injury list with a torn hamstring on August 23, 2022, and missed the [[2022 NFL season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 23, 2022 |title=Patriots Place LB Ronnie Perkins on Injured Reserve; OL Andrew Stueber Placed on Reserve/NFI |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-place-lb-ronnie-perkins-on-injured-reserve-ol-andrew-stueber-placed-on- |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929044715/https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-place-lb-ronnie-perkins-on-injured-reserve-ol-andrew-stueber-placed-on- |archive-date=September 29, 2022 |access-date=March 10, 2023 |website=Patriots.com}}</ref>

On August 29, 2023, Stueber was waived by the Patriots and re-signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2023 |title=Patriots Make Roster Moves to Reach the 53-Man Roster Limit |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-make-roster-moves-to-reach-the-53-man-roster-limit |website=Patriots.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2023 |title=Patriots sign 15 players to the practice squad |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-15-players-to-the-practice-squad-x7482 |website=Patriots.com}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 8, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 8, 2024 |title=Patriots Sign Seven Players to Future Contracts |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-seven-players-to-future-contracts-x3311 |website=patriots.com}}</ref> On June 3, 2024, he was released by the Patriots.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-rookie-free-agent-wr-david-wallis-release-ol-andrew-stueber |title=Patriots Sign Rookie Free Agent WR David Wallis; Release OL Andrew Stueber |website=patriots.com |date=June 3, 2024 |access-date=June 3, 2024}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons (first stint)===
On June 4, 2024, Stueber was claimed off waivers by the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/falcons/news/falcons-claim-former-michigan-wolverines-new-england-patriots-ol-01hzjf2bn90c |title=Falcons Claim Former Michigan Wolverines, New England Patriots OL Off Waivers|website=SI.com |first=Daniel |last=Flick |date=June 4, 2024 |access-date=June 4, 2024}}</ref> He was waived on August 27, and was re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Waack |first=Terrin |date=August 27, 2024 |title=Falcons announce initial 53-man roster for 2024 |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/initial-53-man-roster-2024-season-announced |access-date=2024-11-03 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Waack |first=Terrin |date=August 28, 2024 |title=Falcons sign 13 to practice squad, plus an international player |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/initial-practice-squad-2024-announced |access-date=2024-11-03 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
On October 7, 2024, Steuber was signed by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] to their active roster off the Falcons' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clark |first=Dave |date=8 October 2024 |title=Guard Andrew Stueber to sign with Bengals off Falcons' practice squad, per report |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/guard-andrew-stueber-sign-bengals-030058740.html |access-date=8 October 2024 |website=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref> He was waived on November 28, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bengals Waive OT/G Andrew Stueber | BENGALS ROSTER UPDATE |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-waive-ot-g-andrew-stueber-bengals-roster-update |website=bengals.com |access-date=29 November 2024}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 4.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2024 |title=Bengals Sign K Cade York to Practice Squad, Place K Evan McPherson on Reserve/Injured List |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/cade-york-practice-squad-place-evan-mcpherson-reserve-injured-list-andrew-stueber-bengals-roster-update |access-date=2025-07-29 |website=Bengals.com}}</ref>

On August 25, 2025, Stueber was waived by the Bengals.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals Make Roster Moves Ahead of 53-Man Deadline|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-roster-update-waive-11-players-taven-bryan-august-25-2025|website=Bengals.com|date=August 25, 2025}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons (second stint)===
On November 4, 2025, Stueber signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]]' active roster.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Waack |first1=Terrin |title=Falcons bring back familiar face on offensive line |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/andrew-stueber-signed-offensive-lineman |website=AtlantaFalcons.com |access-date=5 November 2025}}</ref>  He was waived on November 15 and re-signed to the practice squad three days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons sign defensive lineman off Giants practice squad; elevate CB Cobee Bryant to active roster|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-giants-elijah-garcia-cobee-bryant|author=Elhaney, Tori|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=November 15, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Urben |first1=Matt |title=Falcons make changes to roster, practice squad ahead of Week 12 |url=https://thefalconswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/falcons/2025/11/18/falcons-michael-penix-andrew-stueber/87323675007/ |website=Falcons Wire |access-date=19 November 2025}}</ref> Stueber signed a reserve/future contract with Atlanta on January 5, 2026.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons sign 7 players to reserve/future contracts for 2026|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-sign-7-players-reserve-future-contracts-2026|author=McElhaney, Tori|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=January 5, 2026}}</ref>

'''James Andrew Gibler''' (born April 30, 1961) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] for one season in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Missouri Tigers football|Missouri Tigers]] and went undrafted in {{NFL Year|1983}}.

==Early life and college==
Andy Gibler was born on April 30, 1961, in [[Independence, Missouri]]. He attended Grandview High School in [[Grandview, Missouri]], playing [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] and [[defensive end]].<ref name="auto4">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98656460/the-kansas-city-times/|newspaper=[[The Kansas City Times]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=September 5, 1981|author=Sambol, Rich|page=62|title=Area star finds niche as Mizzou's tight end}} {{Open access}}</ref> Gibler enrolled at the [[University of Missouri]], where he reported to football camp as a [[tight end]], despite having no catches in high school (two catches he made were called back by penalty).<ref name="auto4"/><ref name="auto1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98656087/the-kansas-city-times/|newspaper=[[The Kansas City Times]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=September 13, 1979|page=34|title=Gibler Moves Up In New Position As MU Freshman|author=Shatel, Tom}} {{Open access}}</ref> He competed with Tom Anderson, Tim Hornof, Willie Rogers, Greg Kahl, and James Lockett for tight end, starting the season third on the depth chart behind Anderson and Hornof.<ref name="auto1"/> After Hornof missed several games due to [[Infectious mononucleosis|mononucleosis]], Gibler moved up to number two on the depth chart.<ref name="auto1"/> For the sixth game of the season, against [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado]], he was named the team's starter.<ref name="auto4"/> In the game, Gibler made two catches for 47 yards and scored the game-winning touchdown in a 13–7 win.<ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98656187/the-kansas-city-star/|newspaper=[[The Kansas City Star]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 19, 1980|page=199|title=Colorado a favorite foe for Missouri's Gibler|author=Perine, Drew}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref name="auto4"/> He finished the year with 23 receptions for 316 yards, leading the school.<ref name="auto4"/>

In 1980, Gibler remained the team's starting tight end and posted 80 receiving yards in a win over Colorado.<ref name="auto"/> He made 26 catches for 298 yards on the season, which earned him second-team all-[[Big Eight Conference]] honors.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98656241/the-lincoln-star/|newspaper=[[The Lincoln Star]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=November 20, 1980|page=27|title=Five Nebraskans named to AP all-Big Eight squad|author=Tucker, Doug|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> As a [[Junior (education year)|junior]], he made 27 catches, but "slumped" and made some "crucial drops," having "lost his concentration," according to coach [[Warren Powers]].<ref name="auto2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98656708/the-kansas-city-star/|newspaper=[[The Kansas City Star]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 29, 1982|page=25, [https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98656730/the-kansas-city-star/ 27]|title=For the record, Gibler places team ahead of history book|author=Friend, Tom}} {{Open access}}</ref> As a [[Senior (education)|senior]], Gibler rebounded, and had 17 receptions for 298 yards through the first seven weeks of the season.<ref name="auto2"/> In week six, he broke the all-time Missouri record for career catches, surpassing Joe Stewart.<ref name="auto2"/> At the end of the year, Gibler was named second-team all-conference.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98656639/the-des-moines-register/|newspaper=[[The Des Moines Register]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=November 24, 1982|pages=1, 18|title=Dickey leads second team}} {{Open access}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After going unselected in the [[1983 NFL draft]], Gibler was signed by the [[Cleveland Browns]] as an [[undrafted free agent]]. Gibler was also selected in the 18th round (211th overall) of the [[1983 USFL draft]] by the [[Chicago Blitz]], who traded his rights to the [[Denver Gold]], but opted not to play for them.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerg/gibl00200.html|website=Pro Football Archives|title=Andy Gibler NFL Stats}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98655399/springfield-leader-and-press/|newspaper=[[Springfield Leader and Press]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=November 14, 1983|page=12|title=Also...}} {{Open access}}</ref> He was released by the Browns on August 23.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98655274/st-louis-post-dispatch/|newspaper=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|page=32|date=August 23, 1983|title=Sports Shorts}} {{Open access}}</ref> After being released by the Browns, he was claimed off waivers by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], who later waived him on August 29.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98655338/the-marion-star/|newspaper=[[The Marion Star]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 26, 1983|page=10|title=Gibler to join Bengal squad}} {{Open access}}</ref> He was later re-signed in October, and appeared in two regular season games: a 38–10 win over the [[Houston Oilers]] in week 12, and a 14–38 loss versus the [[Miami Dolphins]] in the following week.<ref name="auto3"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GiblAn20/gamelog/|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|title=Andy Gibler Career Game Log}}</ref> He was released by the Bengals at the final roster cuts in {{NFL Year|1984}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98655457/arizona-daily-star/|newspaper=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|page=12|title=Bengals|date=August 28, 1984}} {{Open access}}</ref>

In {{USFL Year|1985}}, Gibler was signed by the [[Orlando Renegades]] of the [[United States Football League]] (USFL), but did not make the final roster.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98655505/the-orlando-sentinel/|newspaper=[[The Orlando Sentinel]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|page=80|date=February 12, 1985|title=Orlando Renegades}} {{Open access}}</ref>

==Later life==
Gibler later became a manager for the [[National Nuclear Security Administration]] (NNSA).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.energy.gov/nnsa/articles/playing-college-and-professional-football-taught-nnsa-manager-be-leader-diverse-team|website=[[Energy.gov]]|title=Playing college and professional football taught this NNSA manager to be a leader of a diverse team |date=December 12, 2019}}</ref>

'''Andrew Michael Vorhees''' (born January 21, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive guard]] for the [[Baltimore Ravens]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]].

==College career==
After attending [[Kingsburg High School]] in [[Kingsburg, California]], Vorhees committed to play [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]] in 2016. He was named as a first-team selection on the [[2021 All-Pac-12 Conference football team]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Utah's Whittingham unanimous AP Pac-12 Coach of the Year|newspaper=Arizona Daily Star|date=December 11, 2021|page=C5|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/106354672/2021-all-pac-12-conference-football-team/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> A super senior, Vorhees announced that he would return to USC in 2022.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kartje |first=Ryan |date=December 10, 2021 |title=Top-rated USC offensive lineman Andrew Vorhees will return for sixth season |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/usc/story/2021-12-10/usc-offensive-lineman-andrew-vorhees-returning-lincoln-riley |access-date=2024-07-20 |work=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> That season, he was named a first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] and was the recipient of the [[Morris Trophy]], awarded to the conference's best offensive lineman.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 20, 2022 |title=USC's Andrew Vorhees and Tuli Tuipulotu Win Morris Trophy |url=https://usctrojans.com/news/2022/12/20/football-andrew-vorhees-and-tuli-tuipulotu-win-morris-trophy.aspx |access-date=22 January 2023 |website=USCTrojans.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On March 5, 2023, Vorhees participated in the 2023 [[NFL Scouting Combine|NFL Combine]]. During one of the drills he [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|tore]] his [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]]; he was slated to be a late first to early third round pick.{{Citation needed|date=June 2023}}

'''Andrew Rupcich''' (born April 1, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for the [[New England Patriots]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Culver–Stockton Wildcats football|Culver–Stockton Wildcats]] and was signed by the Titans as an [[Free agent#Undrafted free agent|undrafted free agent]] in {{NFL Year|2022}}.

==Early life and education==
Rupcich was born on April 1, 1999, in [[Wonder Lake, Illinois]].<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RupcAn00.htm|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|title=Andrew Rupcich Stats}}</ref> He attended [[McHenry High School]], where he played both basketball and football. On the gridiron he was a two-way [[Lineman (gridiron football)|lineman]], and he was selected all-conference at [[right tackle]] as a [[Senior (education)|senior]].<ref name="auto4">{{Cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231113163528/https://www.tennesseetitans.com/team/players-roster/andrew-rupcich/|archive-date=November 13, 2023|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/team/players-roster/andrew-rupcich/|publisher=[[Tennessee Titans]]|title=Andrew Rupcich}}</ref><ref name="auto5">{{Cite news|url=https://titanswire.usatoday.com/lists/titans-udfa-ol-andrew-rupcich-scouting-reports/|date=May 26, 2022|author=Moraitis, Mike|title=What scouting reports said about Titans UDFA OL Andrew Rupcich|newspaper=[[USA Today]]}}</ref> Qualifying for college late, he signed to play [[college football]] with the [[Culver–Stockton Wildcats football|Culver–Stockton Wildcats]] of the [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics]] (NAIA) rather than try [[junior college]] football or be a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] at a higher level.<ref name="auto5"/>

==College career==
Rupcich gained a starting role at [[left tackle]] as a [[freshman]] in 2017 and went on to play every snap for the rest of his collegiate career.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.whig.com/sports/culver-stockton-standout-chases-nfl-dream/article_3e6f8424-09e8-11ed-9577-e3ed73c84122.html|newspaper=[[Herald-Whig]]|title=Culver-Stockton standout chases NFL dream|date=July 23, 2022|author=Adams, Cam}}</ref> He started all 11 games in 2017 and did the same in 2018 while being named first-team All-[[Heart of America Athletic Conference]] (HAAC) North Division.<ref name="auto4"/><ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://www.whig.com/archive/article/rupcich-leads-brigade-of-wildcats-receiving-all-heart-honors/article_80934806-8f59-5712-b267-63890214d35e.html|newspaper=[[Herald-Whig]]|title=Rupcich leads brigade of Wildcats receiving All-Heart honors|date=November 21, 2019}}</ref> He was named the school's athlete of the year in 2018.<ref name="auto6">{{Cite web|url=https://khmoradio.com/all-america-honors-for-culver-stockton-lineman/|publisher=[[KHMO]]|title=All America Honors for Culver Stockton Lineman|date=December 5, 2019|author=Shuler, Bill}}</ref> He was also chosen a first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] by the [[American Football Coaches Association]] (AFCA), being the fifth All-American in school history and the first award|date=August 14, 2019}}</ref>

Rupcich started all four games at left tackle in the [[COVID-19]]-shortened 2020 season, being first-team AFCA All-American and first-team All-HAAC North Division.<ref name="auto4"/> He became Culver–Stockton's first two-time All-American.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://khqa.com/sports/content/the-rupcich-repeat-c-sc-tackle-becomes-schools-first-two-time-all-american|publisher=[[KHQA-TV]]|title=The Rupcich Repeat: C-SC Tackle becomes program's first Two-Time All-American|date=May 5, 2021|author=Duerr, Christopher}}</ref> After returning for a final year in 2021, he started all 11 games and was first-team All-American from [[Associated Press]], web|url=https://www.wgem.com/2021/12/14/wgem-sports-six-monday-december-13-culver-stocktons-andrew-rupcich-dalton-huffman-are-selected-members-afca-naia-all-american-football-team/|publisher=[[WGEM-TV]]|title=WGEM the NAIA level," and Rupcich was both the only NAIA player to be invited to the [[NFLPA Collegiate Bowl]] and to the [[NFL Scouting Combine]].<ref name="auto5"/><ref name="auto1"/> He graduated in ===Tennessee Titans===
After going unselected in the [[2022 NFL draft]], Rupcich was signed by the [[Tennessee Titans]] as an [[Free agent#Undrafted free agent|undrafted free agent]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/northwest-herald/135126098/|newspaper=[[Northwest Herald]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=May 2, 2022|page=A15|title=McHenry alum Rupcich agrees to deal with Titans|author=Stevenson, Joe}} {{Open access}}</ref> He was released at the final roster cuts, on August 30, and was re-signed to the [[practice squad]] the following day.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/nfl/titans/2022/08/30/tennessee-titans-53-man-roster-cuts-2022/7927620001/|newspaper=[[The Tennessean]]|title=Tennessee Titans set 53-man roster: Here's who did — and didn't — make the cut|date=August 30, 2022|author=Arthur, Ben}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/northwest-herald/135126350/|newspaper=[[Northwest Herald]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=September 2, 2022|page=A18|title=Streveler, Rupcich land on practice squads|author=Stevenson, Joe}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wgem.com/2022/09/06/andrew-rupcich-makes-titans-practice-squad/|publisher=[[WGEM-TV]]|title=Andrew Rupcich Makes Titans Practice Squad|date=September 5, 2022|author=Reidy, Brendan}}</ref> He did not appear in any games in his first season, spending the entire year on the practice squad as the Titans finished with a record of 7–10.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wgem.com/2023/09/01/former-c-sc-tackle-rupcich-joins-titans-practice-squad/|publisher=[[WGEM-TV]]|title=Former C-SC tackle Rupcich joins Titans' practice squad|date=September 1, 2023|author=Potts, John}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wgem.com/2023/01/19/former-c-sc-offensive-lineman-rupcich-discusses-first-year-nfl/|publisher=[[WGEM-TV]]|title=Former C-SC offensive lineman Rupcich discusses first year in NFL|date=January 19, 2023|author=Potts, John}}</ref>

Rupcich signed a reserve/future contract on January 23, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-11-players-to-reserve-futures-contracts-x1007|publisher=[[Tennessee Titans]]|title=Titans Sign 14 Players to Reserve/Futures Contracts |date=January 23, 2023|author=Wyatt, Jim}}</ref> He was released at the final roster cuts on August 29, 2023, and then re-signed to the practice squad the following day.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/titans-keep-11-rookies-on-their-initial-53-man-roster|website=[[ProFootballTalk]]|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|title=Titans keep 11 practice squad announced: Which players were brought back after cut day?|date=August 30, 2023|author=Suss, Nick}}</ref> Rupcich was elevated to the active roster for the team's Week 10 game against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], and made his debut in the 20–6 loss, appearing on 45 offensive snaps and three [[special teams]] snaps after coming in at [[right guard]] for the injured [[Andre Dillard]].<ref name="auto3"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/titans-place-nicholas-petit-frere-on-injured-reserve|website=[[ProFootballTalk]]|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|title=Titans place leaves Tennessee Titans game vs. Buccaneers, being evaluated for concussion|date=November 12, 2023|author=Suss, Nick}}</ref> He became the third Culver–Stockton NFL player in history, following [[Bob Hendren]] (1949–1951) and [[Jason Kaiser]] (1998–1999).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/schools/culverstockton/index.htm|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|title=Culver-Stockton Players/Alumni}}</ref> Rupcich was signed to the 53-man Rupcich appeared in the first seven games of the [[2024 Tennessee Titans season|2024 season]], playing 16 offensive snaps as a rotational right guard and 22 snaps on special teams,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andrew Rupcich 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RupcAn00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=Dec 21, 2024 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> but unfortunately suffered a season-ending [[triceps|tricep]] tear during a Week 8 game against the [[Detroit Lions]]. '''Andrew Raym''' (born May 2, 2001)<ref name=birthday /> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Center (gridiron football)|center]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]] and was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Carolina Panthers]] in [[2024 NFL draft|2024]].

==Early life==
Raym grew up in [[Broken Arrow, Oklahoma]], and attended [[Broken Arrow High School]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1467434/2019/12/17/oklahoma-recruit-andrew-raym-2020-prospect/|website=[[The Athletic]]|title=‘I’ve been wearing the jersey since I was 1’: Lineman Andrew Raym was born to be a Sooner|date=December 17, 2019|author=Kersey, Jason}}</ref> He quickly became a top [[offensive line]] recruit after becoming a full-time starter as a [[freshman]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/tulsa-world/140163511/|newspaper=[[Tulsa World]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=July 13, 2017|page=17, [https://www.newspapers.com/article/tulsa-world/140163587/ 19]|title=Super sophomore|author=Lewis, Barry}} {{Open access}}</ref> By his [[sophomore]] year he had become a first-team all-state selection and [[All-American]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/tulsa-world/140163693/|newspaper=[[Tulsa World]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=July 5, 2018|page=13, (education year)|junior]] and as a [[Senior (education)|senior]] helped them set school rushing records.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.normantranscript.com/oklahoma/ou-football-broken-arrows-andrew-raym-stands-out-even-on-oklahomas-star-studded-ol-class/article_d79c48a0-21fe-11ea-a920-3bf228666108.html|newspaper=[[Norman Armour All-American]], he was ranked the consensus top recruit in the state and the number one [[offensive guard]] nationally.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://tulsaworld.com/sports/photo/the-recruiting-journey-of-broken-arrows-andrew-raym-the-states-no-1-football-recruit-in/collection_b3f934c6-02a9-5ad9-a6b2-14eab4df0172.html|newspaper=[[Tulsa === Carolina Panthers ===
Raym signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]] as an undrafted free agent on May 10, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers make roster moves, including signing 19 undrafted free agents|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-make-roster-moves-including-signing-18-undrafted-free-agents|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=May 10, 2024}}</ref> He was also selected by the [[Memphis Showboats (2022)|Memphis Showboats]] in the sixth round of the [[2024 UFL draft]] on July 17.<ref>{{cite news |title=2024 UFL College Draft: Showboats select Kansas QB Jason Bean with No. 1 pick |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/ufl/2024-ufl-college-draft-tracking-every-selection |website=FoxSports.com |date=July 17, 2024 |access-date=July 19, 2024}}</ref> Raym notably made the Panthers' 53 man roster out of training camp as a UDFA. He was waived on October 19, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers add two to active roster Saturday|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-add-two-to-active-roster-saturday-dane-jackson-tj-smith-troy-hill|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=October 19, 2024}}</ref>

Raym signed a reserve/future contract with Carolina on January 6, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers sign 10 players to reserve/future contracts on Monday|url=https://pantherswire.usatoday.com/2025/01/06/panthers-sign-10-players-reserve-future-contracts/|work=Panthers Wire|publisher=USA Today|date=January 6, 2025}}</ref> On May 8, Raym was waived by the Panthers.<ref>{{cite web |title=Panthers make roster moves, release Jadeveon Clowney |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-make-roster-moves-release-jadeveon-clowney |website=panthers.com |access-date=9 May 2025}}</ref>

'''Andrew Wyatt Wayne Bowers''' (born February 22, 1976) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] for one season with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played  [[college football]] for the [[Utah Utes football|Utah Utes]].

==Early life and college==
Andrew Wyant Wayne Bowers was born on February 22, 1976, in [[Salt Lake City, Utah]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/b/bowe00780.html | title=Andy Bowers | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=6 May 2025}}</ref> He played [[high school football]] at [[Hillcrest High School (Midvale, Utah)|Hillcrest High School]] in [[Midvale, Utah]] as a [[defensive end]], earning first-team All-Region and second-team All-State honors.<ref name="Af">{{cite web | url=https://www.arenafan.com/players/Andy_Bowers-4845/ | title=Andy Bowers | publisher=ArenaFan.com | accessdate=6 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="Pfa"/> He was also a football [[team captain]] and a two-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] in [[basketball]].<ref name="Af"/>

Bowers spent three years on an [[LDS Church]] mission in [[Denmark]] before playing [[college football]] for the [[Utah Utes football|Utah Utes]] of the [[University of Utah]].<ref name="Af"/> He was a four-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]]  for the Utes from 1997 to 2000.<ref name="Pfa"/>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[2001 NFL draft]],  Bowers signed with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] on April 23, 2001.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/b/bowe00780.html | title=Andy Bowers Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=6 May 2025}}</ref> He was released on September 2, signed to the practice squad on September 3, promoted to the active roster on October 25, released again on November 6, signed to the practice squad again on November 7, and promoted to the active roster again on November 30, 2001.<ref name="transactions"/> Overall, he played in, and started, one game for the Cardinals during the 2001 season; the November 4 loss to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BoweAn20/gamelog/2001/ | title=Andy Bowers | publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] | accessdate=6 May 2025}}</ref> Bowers posted one assisted tackle during the game.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BoweAn20/gamelog/2001/ | title=Andy Bowers 2001 Game Logs | publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] | accessdate=6 May 2025}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve the next year on September 5, 2002, and was released on November 12, 2002.<ref name="transactions"/>

Bowers was signed by the [[Buffalo Bills]] on February 4, 2003.<ref name="transactions"/> He was later released on July 14, 2003.<ref name="transactions"/>

Bowers was signed to the practice squad of the [[Arizona Rattlers]] of the [[Arena Football League]] on June 16, 2004.<ref name="Arena">{{cite web | url=https://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=21 | title=Historical Team Transactions | publisher=ArenaFan.com | accessdate=6 May 2025}}</ref> He re-signed with the Rattlers on October 22, 2004, but was later waived on January 21, 2005.<ref name="Arena"/>

'''Andrés "Andy" Borregales''' ({{Respell|BORE|eh|gah|les}};<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-06 |title=Pronunciation Guide – Patriots |url=https://patriots.1rmg.com/pronunciation-guide/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251121204527/https://patriots.1rmg.com/pronunciation-guide/ |archive-date=2025-11-21 |access-date=2026-01-06 |website=patriots.1rmg.com}}</ref> born January 2, 2003) is a Venezuelan professional [[American football]] [[Placekicker|kicker]] for the [[New England Patriots]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]] and was selected by the Patriots in the sixth round of the [[2025 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Borregales was born in [[Caracas]], Venezuela, and immigrated to the United States with his family at the age of one. Borregales attended [[Chaminade–Madonna College Preparatory School]] in [[Hollywood, Florida]]. He went seven for nine on his field goal attempts as a sophomore and finished his high school career with a long of 56 yards.<ref name="commit">{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=David |date=June 7, 2019 |title=Chaminade–Madonna kicker Andres Borregales commits to Miami Hurricanes’ Class of 2021 |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article231280758.html |access-date=January 19, 2025 |website=Miami Herald}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Wilson |first1=David |date=October 29, 2019 |title=A brief conversation with Chaminade K Andres Borregales, UM's unlikely popular recruit |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article236758903.html |access-date=January 19, 2025 |website=Miami Herald}}</ref> He committed to play [[college football]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]].<ref name=commit/>

==College career==
Heading into his freshman season in 2021, Borregales was named the Hurricanes starting kicker and kickoff specialist.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wilson |first1=David |date=September 7, 2022 |title=An underrated special teams weapon and feedback on 'very Miami-ish' new recruiting suite |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article265419991.html |access-date=January 19, 2025 |website=Miami Herald}}</ref> He finished the 2021 season hitting 17 out of his 21 field goals and all 45 of his extra points attempts.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Schifman |first1=Mike |date=June 28, 2022 |title=2022 Miami Hurricanes player preview: Andres Borregales |url=https://www.stateoftheu.com/2022/6/28/23183731/miami-hurricanes-football-2022-season-player-preview-kicker-andres-borregales |access-date=January 19, 2025 |website=State of the U|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> In week 10 of the 2022 season, Borregales hit four field goals in an overtime win over [[2022 Virginia Cavaliers football team|Virginia]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Miller Degnan |first1=Susan |last2=McPherson |first2=Jordan |date=October 29, 2022 |title=Borregales' clutch field goals, injury updates and more from Miami's win over Virginia |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article267874057.html |access-date=January 19, 2025 |website=Miami Herald}}</ref> In 2022, he went 17 for 20 on his field goal attempts and converted on all 35 of his extra points.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andy Borregales 2022 Stats per Game - NCAAF |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/gamelog/_/id/4569923/andy-borregales |access-date=2026-02-13 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> In week 9 of the 2023 season, Borregales hit three 45-plus yard field goals including a game-tying 48-yard field goal to force overtime in a win over [[2023 Virginia Cavaliers football team|Virginia]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wilson |first1=David |date=October 30, 2023 |title='Thank God for Andy Borregales.' Miami kicker makes history with another clutch kick |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article281084203.html |access-date=January 19, 2025 |website=Miami Herald}}</ref> He finished the 2023 season converting on 22 of his 26 field goal attempts and 44 of his 45 extra points.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lichtenstein |first1=Adam |date=August 19, 2024  |title=Hurricanes kicker Andres Borregales named a preseason All-American |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/2024/08/19/hurricanes-kicker-andres-borregales-named-a-preseason-all-american/ |access-date=January 19, 2025 |website=Sun Sentinel}}</ref> In week 5 of the 2024 season, Borregales hit a career-long 56-yard field goal in a win over [[2024 Virginia Tech Hokies football team|Virginia Tech]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=McPherson |first1=Jordan |date=October 1, 2024 |title=Andres Borregales keeps climbing in Hurricanes record book. And Malik Bryant's growth |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article293279644.html |access-date=January 19, 2025 |website=Miami Herald}}</ref> He finished his final collegiate season in 2024, going 18 for 19 on his field goals, while also making all 62 of his extra point attempts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Andres Borregales 2024 Game Logs |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/andres-borregales-1/gamelog/2024/ |website=Sports Reference |access-date=January 19, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Borregales is a [[Christianity|Christian]]. He is married to Stephanie Borregales.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Claybourn |first1=Cole |date=January 29, 2026 |title=Patriots rookie kicker Andy Borregales heads to Super Bowl knowing ‘God put me in this position’ |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/sport/football/2026/01/29/patriots-kicker-andy-borregales-super-bowl-god-position/ |access-date=30 January 2026 |website=Sports Spectrum}}</ref>

Borregales's older brother, [[José Borregales]], also attended Miami and won a [[Lou Groza Award]] after three seasons at [[Florida International University]]. José was briefly on the rosters of the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[Orlando Guardians]], and [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Miller Degnan |first=Susan |date=September 8, 2021 |title=The gang's all crying for Andy Borregales, Miami's baby-faced kicker with a man-sized leg |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article254062358.html |access-date=January 19, 2025 |website=Miami Herald}}</ref>

While growing up, Borregales “looked up to” kicker [[Adam Vinatieri]], who played ten seasons with the Patriots.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Geagan |first=Matt |date=April 26, 2025 |title=New Patriots kicker Andres Borregales idolized Adam Vinatieri growing up |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/andres-borregales-new-england-patriots-nfl-draft-adam-vinatieri/ |access-date=November 6, 2025 |website=CBS News - Boston |language=en-US}}</ref>
